job.title: Senior Systems Engineer
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

NPR is seeking an experienced, technically rigorous Senior IT Systems Engineer to join our IT Systems team. In this role, you will serve as a primary technical lead responsible for the design, deployment, administration, and optimization of NPR’s core virtualized data center infrastructure. The ideal candidate brings deep, hands-on expertise in VMware vSphere, enterprise Storage Area Networks (SAN/NAS), and Cisco Unified Computing System (UCS) environments.

You will play a critical role in ensuring the high availability, scalability, performance, and security of our enterprise systems while partnering across Technology to advance infrastructure modernization and automation initiatives in support of our nationwide public media mission.

Responsibilities

Data Center Architecture & Storage Administration

  1. Architect Virtualized Infrastructure: Design, deploy, and manage core virtualized data center infrastructure, leading enterprise VMware vSphere environments, Cisco UCS compute platforms, and SAN/NAS storage arrays.
  2. Administer Enterprise Compute & Storage: Execute routine server builds, security patch management, virtual machine lifecycle administration, and enterprise storage capacity allocation.
  3. Advance Cloud & Hybrid Integration: Evaluate systems architecture and hybrid-cloud strategy, taking operational ownership of the maintenance and integration of cloud infrastructure (AWS or Azure).

Systems Governance & Disaster Recovery

  1. Govern Disaster Recovery Strategies: Design, maintain, and rigorously test business continuity and disaster recovery strategies, including enterprise backups, data replication, and automated site failovers.
  2. Manage Structured Change Processes: Recommend, test, and implement system enhancements in strict adherence to established organizational change management policies and procedures.
  3. Publish System Documentation & SOPs: Author and maintain comprehensive systems architecture diagrams, standard operating procedures (SOPs), runbooks, and technical documentation for IT colleagues and system stakeholders.

Incident Escalation & Operational Automation

  1. Lead Tier-3 Escalations & Root Cause Analysis: Serve as the senior technical escalation point for enterprise technology teams, isolating root causes and resolving complex production incidents.
  2. Automate Infrastructure Operations: Design and execute automation scripts using modern scripting languages to streamline routine administrative tasks, infrastructure provisioning, and systems health reporting.
  3. Maintain Operational Communications: Provide timely status reporting on system health to engineering leadership, manage incident response on a 24x7 rotation, and articulate outage impact clearly to technical and operational partners.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • 5+ years of dedicated experience as a Systems or Infrastructure Engineer supporting, administering, and troubleshooting systems in an enterprise data center environment.
  • Proven, hands-on experience designing and managing complex VMware vSphere environments (clustering, DRS, HA, vMotion).
  • Extensive experience with Cisco UCS Manager, configuring service profiles, templates, and physical hardware deployment.
  • Strong background in configuring and managing enterprise SAN/NAS storage arrays and storage networking protocols.
  • 2+ years of experience planning, designing, and maintaining cloud infrastructure (AWS or Azure).
  • Strong working knowledge of the Microsoft ecosystem, including Windows Server (2016+), Active Directory, Azure AD, Office 365, IIS, SQL, DFS, DHCP, and DNS.
  • Experience creating detailed systems documentation and flow charts.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to successfully handle multiple projects in a high-pressure, collaborative environment.
  • Ability to participate in an on-call rotation and a 2-week onsite rotation every two months (or as required).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Infrastructure Automation & Scripting: Experience utilizing configuration management tools (Ansible, Puppet) and writing automation scripts (PowerShell, Python, or Bash).
  • Identity, Access & Messaging Services: Practical experience managing enterprise SSO/MFA solutions, Exchange Online/Hybrid environments, or Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI).
  • Industry Certifications: Active professional certifications in VMware (VCP), Cisco (CCNA/CCNP Data Center), Microsoft, or AWS/Azure solutions architecture.

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Expert-level analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to resolve complex hardware, software, and performance issues under pressure.
  • Deep understanding of networking concepts (VLANs, routing, switching, LACP, DNS, DHCP) as they relate to virtualization and server infrastructure.
  • Strong understanding of security best practices for data center infrastructure and virtualization platforms.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of translating technical challenges to cross-functional teams and leadership.
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to lead infrastructure upgrades and migrations independently.
  • Self-motivated team player with a willingness to participate in an on-call rotation and perform after-hours maintenance.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

Work Location & Requirements

  • Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. Some aspects of this role require duties better performed at an NPR facility. The employee will be required to be in the office at the Washington, D.C. location for a two-week block approximately every two months. The employee will also be  expected to be onsite as needed to support onsite projects.

Job Type

  • This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S.-based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $125,000 - $145,000 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees. 

Does this sound like you? If so, we want to hear from you.

job.title: Editorial Data Analyst
job.description:
Join our team at the Guardian and be a part of a diverse and inclusive global organisation that delivers fearless, investigative journalism, and holds power to account. Our team of award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial professionals, and industry-leading digital experts are committed to making a difference and represent a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We offer a challenging and exciting environment for career development, with a focus on training, growth and fostering an inclusive culture.

 

We are now looking for a Data Analyst to join our Editorial Analytics team. You’ll use data to help understand how our journalism reaches and engages readers, and supports decision making across the newsroom and wider business. 

 

About the role

  • Provide insights on reader engagement and content performance to inform newsroom strategy.
  • Develop an understanding of editorial workflows, audience behaviour and business priorities, and apply this context when interpreting data.
  • Communicate findings clearly, tailoring outputs to different audiences and explaining context and limitations.
  • Collaborate with Product, Engineering and other teams to support feature development, experimentation and performance analysis.
  • Work responsibly and ethically with data, following privacy and governance standards.

 

About you

  • Experience working with data using SQL (in a professional or academic setting).
  • Understanding of core analytical concepts (e.g. averages, distributions, basic statistical testing).
  • Familiarity with data visualisation tools (e.g. Tableau, Looker).
  • Ability to think logically about problems and break them down into manageable analyses.
  • Comfortable working with stakeholders and building positive working relationships.

We operate in a hybrid environment working 3 days a week from our offices in Kings Cross and 2 days a week remotely. 

We actively encourage applications from groups traditionally underrepresented in the UK media

 

We value and respect all differences (seen and unseen) in all people. We aspire to have inclusive working experiences and an environment that reflects the audience we serve, where our people have equal access to career development opportunities, their voices are heard and can contribute to our future. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. Many of our staff work flexibly and we will consider all requests for flexible working arrangements.

 

How to apply

To apply, please upload your latest CV. You don't need to provide a cover letter. Instead, we have included a question on the application questionnaire relating to editorial analytics that we would like applicants to complete. This question should take about 5 minutes to answer, so please factor in the extra time when applying.

 

We appreciate the time taken to prepare each application we receive. We do not use AI-assisted technology to review applications; every application is reviewed by a member of our recruitment team. Thank you for bearing with us during the screening process. 

 

The closing date for applications is Wednesday 18th November 2026. 

 

All roles at the Guardian are open for everybody to apply. It is important to us that you feel supported and comfortable throughout your recruitment process, in order to perform your best. Please let us know if there are any changes we could make to help your application, this includes providing documents in accessible formats or personalising the process to better support your needs. Please contact Anna Vipers on anna.vipers@guardian.co.uk to discuss further so we can work with you to support you through your application.

 

Benefits at the Guardian

You'll have 30 days of annual leave per year (plus bank holidays) with the option to purchase an additional 5 days. Our pension scheme is generous; if you contribute 5% then we will contribute 8-12% (depending on your age). We believe in giving back, which is why employees are given 2 volunteering days annually and the option of payroll giving. Season ticket loans are also available.

You are entitled to private healthcare, life cover, income protection, and eye tests. You can also opt in to dental insurance.

We have enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave policies in place. We also support our employees by offering an IVF, menopause, baby loss, and trans equality policy.

 

Culture and wellbeing

We want everyone to feel like they belong at the Guardian and we champion diversity of thought. Our various employee forums provide a platform to use their voice to foster an inclusive workplace. We became the first major media organisation to achieve B Corp status.

We offer tools to help you prioritise your wellbeing including access to our employee benefits platform which provides tailored support for health and wellbeing. In addition, we also offer free yoga and pilates classes. These run alongside our corporate gym membership and cycle to work scheme.

Our canteen has views overlooking the Regents Canal and caters for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

 

Learning and development

We encourage personal and professional growth. Employees have access to a broad range of tools and solutions, and we are happy to support the pursuit of professional qualifications through vocational courses and apprenticeships.

 

Guardian News and Media is proud to be a London Living wage employer. The minimum salary for any full-time role within the organisation is £30,000 per annum. Salary ranges are dependent on skills and experience.

Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry is looking for a Art Supervisor to join our growing team!  

21GRAMS, part of Real Chemistry, is a full-service healthcare advertising agency built on the belief that healthcare should feel more human. We combine bold creativity, strategic rigor, and deep scientific understanding to create work that changes behavior, improves outcomes, and makes a meaningful impact on people's lives. This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Carmel, Lambertville, or San Francisco—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs.

What you'll do:

  • Responsible for art direction and design across a variety of digital tactics, including websites, interactive visual aids, videos, banners, landing pages, and emails, for branded and unbranded HCP clients
  • Convey scientific information into compelling and memorable messages for HCP campaigns
  • Champion creative thinking for campaigns and initiatives that advance creative strategy and brand personality

  • You are adaptable, resilient, and comfortable adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment. As our business grows and changes, so do we.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful, with strong prioritization skills, intellectual curiosity, and a desire to leverage data to inform decisions and drive outcomes.
  • You are energized by innovation and the transformative potential of AI, actively exploring new technologies, identifying opportunities to work smarter, and championing practical, responsible AI adoption that drives meaningful business impact.

What you should have:

  • 5+ years healthcare/pharmaceutical art direction and design
  • College degree in a related field preferred
  • Experience in the healthcare/pharmaceutical industry in an agency setting required
  • Proficiency in Adobe CS required, other relevant design software programs a plus
  • Portfolio or PDF of relevant work samples required
  • A comprehensive creative portfolio, demonstrating strong conceptual capabilities and ability to produce work in high-science pharma categories

 

Pay Range: $110,000-$130,000
The anticipated salary range for this position is listed above. Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, and internal parity.

We believe we can do our best when feeling our best, which is why we’ve put together a benefits program designed to give you the support you and your family need at every stage of life. job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:
Opportunity  

Our Brunswick Arts team, known as B’Arts, is an international communications consultancy specialising in championing and protecting the reputations and interests of leading arts, cultural and charitable organisations worldwide. With teams in London, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, New York and Hong Kong, we work alongside some of the most prestigious institutions and exciting initiatives across the global cultural landscape.

We are looking for a highly organised, proactive and adaptable Executive Assistant to join our London team on a 12-month fixed-term contract. This is a pivotal role providing high-level support to two Partners, ensuring the smooth running of their day-to-day activities and anticipating their needs in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

The role is based in our London office Monday to Thursday, with the flexibility to work remotely on Fridays. The ideal candidate will be a confident self-starter who thrives in a creative and collaborative environment, bringing exceptional organisational skills, sound judgement, discretion and a genuine interest in the arts and cultural sector.

About the Role

As an Executive Assistant at Brunswick Arts, you will:

  • Provide comprehensive diary, inbox, and communications management for two Partners.
  • Organise and maintain Partner inboxes and diaries with a clear, structured system, using colour coordination and folders to ensure efficiency and visibility.
  • Prepare daily briefs and materials, ensuring leaders are fully equipped and informed for client meetings, events, and travel.
  • Draft, prioritise, and triage communications on behalf of senior leaders — from client correspondence to internal notes.
  • Manage complex international travel arrangements, including visas, itineraries, and on-the-ground logistics.
  • Coordinate high-profile client dinners, cultural events, and hospitality with creativity and attention to detail.
  • Oversee financial administration including expenses, billing, and budget tracking.
  • Submit and manage timesheets on behalf of the Partners, ensuring timely and accurate completion each week.
  • Serve as a trusted point of contact for clients and their offices, building relationships with professionalism, warmth, and discretion.
  • Ensure the quality and presentation of client-facing deliverables, from proposals to event materials.
  • Conduct research and compile insights to support client engagements and leadership decision-making.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of systems and workflows across the team.

What We're Looking For

We’re seeking someone who brings:

  • A genuine interest in the arts, culture and charitable sectors, with an enthusiasm for the work of Brunswick Arts (B’Arts) and the organisations and institutions we support across the global cultural landscape.
  • At least 4 years’ experience supporting senior leaders at Partner, Director or C-suite level, ideally within professional services, consultancy or the creative industries.
  • Exceptional organisational skills and sound judgement, with the ability to manage competing priorities, adapt to changing demands and maintain a high level of accuracy and discretion.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a polished, professional and adaptable communication style.
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office, alongside the confidence and willingness to embrace new digital tools and systems.
  • Strong financial administration skills and meticulous attention to detail, with experience managing expenses, invoicing, timesheets and budget tracking.
  • Proven relationship-building skills, with the confidence to engage effectively and establish trust with senior stakeholders, colleagues and clients.
  • A proactive, solutions-focused approach, with the ability to anticipate challenges, exercise initiative and navigate demanding situations with professionalism and diplomacy.
  • A calm composed and adaptable manner, with the ability to anticipate needs, remain one step ahead and deliver consistently under pressure.
  • A collaborative and team-oriented mindset, with a genuine commitment to contributing to a supportive, inclusive and high-performing assistant team.

Why Join Us

Whether you are joining a client-facing team, a core services team, or starting out on your professional career journey, joining Brunswick unlocks a range of exceptional employee benefits to support your financial future, health and wellness, family and community and continuous professional development

About Brunswick

Brunswick is a global advisory firm. We help companies tackle high-stakes issues, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, and deliver high-impact outcomes. 

Our clients value our ability to anticipate, shape, and respond to the key players and forces in the financial and investment arena, regulatory and geopolitical universe, NGO community, workforce and beyond. They rely on us for deep experience, fresh perspectives and original thinking. So, in Brunswick you will find an exceptional range of experience and talent with a rich mix of backgrounds. From the beginning, we have prioritized attracting, developing, and retaining the best professionals in the industry, united by a culture of inclusivity, excellence, and intellectual curiosity.

Founded in 1987 in London, the firm has organically grown to 27 offices in 18 countries across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia and Australia. We operate as a “one-firm firm” with no individual profit centers. This allows us to assemble fully integrated, bespoke teams for each client, able to draw on the full resources of Brunswick anywhere in the world. 

 

Brunswick is an equal opportunity employer.  All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law. Please read our Global Privacy Notice to understand how your data is managed.

job.title: GRAY MEDIA TRAINING PROGRAM SPRING '27 - KWCH
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first and/or second-highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 of such markets that were measured by Nielsen in 2025. We also own the largest Telemundo Affiliate group with 46 markets and Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies with the most advanced digital products and services. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KWCH:

KWCH-TV (12 News) is a CBS television affiliate operated by Gray Television with one of the best corporate and local cultures in the country. Our top-rated station is located in the beautiful south-central region of Kansas. KWCH-TV is the market leader, with viewers relying on news and weather coverage. Along with strong programming ratings, the #1 website, CBS Sports, and CBS Primetime, we deliver results for our advertisers.

The Training Program:

Are you tired of just watching from the sidelines? Ready to stop "shadowing" and start actually doing the work that reaches thousands of people every single day? We’re looking for the next generation of media powerhouses, producers, reporters, weather experts, and sales executives who are hungry to dive head-first into the fast-paced world of local media. This isn't your typical "get the coffee" internship. The Gray Media Training Program is a high-octane, 10-week immersive experience where you don’t just learn the job; you own it. Whether you’re crafting the lead story for the evening news, tracking a cold front on our weather tech, or closing a digital ad deal, you’ll be a vital part of our award -winning team from day one. The intern rate of pay can range from the minimum wage in your state to $15 an hour.

General Requirements: 

What You’ll Do:

  • Own the role: Step into the shoes of a producer, MMJ, meteorologist, or media sales executive and handle real-world assignments (yes, the kind that may go on air and online). 
  • Drive digital engagement: Create content that lives beyond the TV screen; think social media, streaming apps, and web stories—because we’re digital-first, always.
  • Collaborate with pros: Work side-by-side with seasoned veterans who are the best in the business, gaining insights you won’t find in any textbook. 
  • Commit to the craft: Dedicate 25 hours per week for 10 weeks to mastering your specialty and building a professional-grade portfolio.
  • Make an impact: Tell stories that matter to the community or help local businesses grow through innovative media strategies.
  • Build your future: Position yourself at the front of the line for full-time career opportunities within Gray Media’s network of 113 stations.

What You Bring:

  • Current enrollment: You’re a college student (Junior or Senior status preferred) chasing a degree in Journalism, Communications, Sales, Marketing, or a related field.
  • A "doer" mindset: You aren't afraid to get your hands dirty and take initiative; you’re here to work, not just watch.
  • Digital savvy: You understand that media happens everywhere, from the big screen to the palm of someone’s hand. 
  • Strong work ethic: You bring urgency, organization, and a "can-do" attitude to every shift. 
  • Communication skills: You can tell a story, pitch an idea, or explain a forecast with clarity and confidence. 
  • Reliability: You’re ready to commit to the full 10-week program and the 25-hour weekly schedule. 
  • Passion for local: You care about the community and want to see how local media makes a real difference.

Why You’ll Love It Here:

  • Real-world experience: You’ll graduate with more than just a line on your resume; you’ll have the experience of having done the job.
  • Unprecedented access: With 113 stations across the U.S., you’re part of a massive, innovative network that’s leading the future of media.
  • Career fast-track: We love hiring our own. This program is designed to be the ultimate audition for your first full-time role with Gray.
  • Paid training: Earn while you learn—this is a paid internship.
  • A culture of innovation: We’re evolving on purpose, and you’ll be right there on the front lines of that evolution.

Qualifications/Requirements: 

▪️ Be currently enrolled in a college/university (preferred: Junior/Senior)
▪️ Strong work ethic and organizational skills
▪️ Earning a degree in Journalism/Communications, News, or related fields, with a desire to get hands-on experience in the local media industry

If you are interested in interning in these areas, the station may have openings in these departments for you:

- Sports
- Weather
- News MMJ

Ready to stop practicing and start performing? Let’s build the future of media together

The intern rate of pay can range from the minimum wage in your state to $15 an hour.

▪️ Interested in the program?  Go to https://gray.tv/careers#currentopenings, type "KWCH" (in the search bar)

job.title: Manager, Production Finance
job.description:
Tennis Channel’s Production Finance Manager manages day-to-day production accounting and financial analysis for domestic and international production activities. Reporting to the Director of Production Finance, the role supports live events, studio productions, original content, and digital initiatives through accurate close, event cost reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and financial controls. The manager works closely with Production, FP&A, and Accounting, coordinating broader accounting requirements with the Director of Accounting. This role is onsite and located in Santa Monica, CA.

In this role, you will do the following:

  • Manage the production-related monthly close in accordance with corporate deadlines, including production and program costs by line of business, prepaid assets, accrued liabilities, amortization entries, and account reconciliations. Maintain job-cost schedules and supporting calculations; reconcile production records to the general ledger and investigate discrepancies.
  • Support the Director of Production Finance in preparing annual budgets, quarterly forecasts, long-range planning schedules, variance analyses, and monthly reporting packages for Finance and Production leadership.
  • Maintain event-level estimates of total expected costs, incorporating actual spending, outstanding commitments, and remaining costs. Review assumptions with Production, explain cost drivers, and escalate potential overruns, forecast changes, and financial risks promptly.
  • Track production costs, vendor obligations, talent commitments, and open purchase orders. Prepare recurring event cost reports and post-event analyses, including budget-to-actual comparisons and recommendations for future planning.
  • Review crew payroll, timecards, overtime, labor coding, and related production labor costs for accuracy, budget impact, supporting documentation, and required approvals. Coordinate exceptions with Production, HR, and payroll providers in accordance with established responsibilities and approval authority.
  • Review production payables, purchasing card activity, employee expense reimbursements, and per diem payments for appropriate coding, documentation, approvals, and compliance with policy. Approve transactions within delegated authority and coordinate with Corporate AP and expense systems, including Concur.
  • Support financial review of production agreements and vendor commitments for cost tracking, accounting treatment, payment timing, and budget impact. Escalate exceptions to the Director of Production Finance and coordinate technical accounting questions with the Director of Accounting.
  • Serve as a day-to-day finance contact for Production on project setup, chart of accounts, transactional workflows, policies, and procedures. Coordinate with Production on financial requirements while Production retains responsibility for talent, hotel, and crew booking and operational logistics.
  • Prepare production-related audit schedules and supporting documentation, coordinating submissions and requests through the Director of Accounting. Support Corporate tax requests related to production, including international costs and tax/VAT documentation, as directed by Accounting and Corporate Tax.
  • Coordinate production accounting priorities, close deadlines, and supporting work with Finance and Accounting team members. Maintain clear process documentation, reporting calendars, and follow-up on unresolved items.
  • Improve production accounting, forecasting, and reporting processes through standardized templates, reconciliations, and approved automation and AI-enabled tools. Maintain cost benchmarks, savings trackers, and operational metrics across vendors, staffing, travel, and other production spending.
  • Support production-related corporate initiatives, parent-company integration, and system upgrades under the Director of Production Finance, coordinating with the Director of Accounting and VP Finance/Controller as appropriate.

 

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA or a relevant master’s degree preferred.
  • Five to seven years of progressive accounting or finance experience, including hands-on budgeting, forecasting, production or project job costing, monthly close, and reconciliations.
  • Experience in live sports, production finance, entertainment, or media preferred; familiarity with domestic and international production costs is valuable.
  • Ability to build and maintain event cost forecasts, analyze actuals and commitments, and translate financial results into clear explanations for production managers and Finance leadership.
  • Strong understanding of accrual accounting, financial controls, production labor and vendor cost review.
  • Advanced Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookup functions, and financial modeling; experience with Oracle or a comparable ERP/project accounting system preferred.
  • Strong communication, organization, and judgment; ability to manage competing deadlines, work independently, collaborate across teams, and deliver accurate work with appropriate review.
  • Experience documenting processes and improving reporting workflows; familiarity with BI tools and approved automation is a plus.

job.description:
Integrated Media Specialist (Account Executive– Outside Sales)

Territory-Based | Hybrid | Client-Facing Market Role

Company: LocaliQ, powered by the USA TODAY Network Location: Outside Sales, territory-based role in Nashville, TN | Hybrid (Remote + In-territory + 1 day in-office)

About LocaliQ

At LocaliQ, part of USA TODAY Co., we help businesses grow by bringing together advanced marketing technology, trusted audience reach, and the expertise to turn it into results. In this role, you’ll work at the intersection of digital marketing and one of the most trusted media networks in the country—helping businesses connect with customers across the full marketing funnel.

You’ll partner with clients to understand their goals, build strategies that combine performance-driven digital solutions with the reach of the USA TODAY Network, and deliver measurable outcomes. This is an opportunity to be part of a team that doesn’t just sell products. We bring together the right mix of solutions to drive real business growth.

About the Role

Our Integrated Media Specialist role is a consultative, relationship-driven sales position for someone who loves owning the full sales cycle—from net-new prospecting through long-term account growth—and who thrives in both hunting and managing client relationships.

In this role, you will actively hunt for net-new business, while also managing, growing, and expanding an ongoing book of clients. You’ll create tailored marketing strategies, guide businesses from first conversation through ongoing performance discussions, and continually identify opportunities to deepen partnerships over time. You’ll act as a trusted marketing partner—not a transactional seller—balancing new business development with retention, upsell, and account expansion to drive long-term client value.

Our Integrated Media Specialist role is partnered with a post-sales team that manages campaign performance, optimizes results, and prepares reporting. Additional support resources are available, including the Data and Insights team, Client Strategists, and other product-specific resources.

In your first 90 days, you’ll gain confidence in LocaliQ’s solutions, tools, and sales approach while building meaningful prospecting and discovery habits. By the end of this period, you’ll be owning your territory and sales cycle end-to-end, with the support and coaching needed to set you up for long-term success.

Why This Role Stands Out:

Competitive base salary with uncapped commission and strong earning potential

Contests, and recognition programs for top performers

Consultative, full-cycle sales role with ownership from first conversation through long-term account growth

Hybrid flexibility with autonomy to manage your schedule and territory

Strong onboarding, coaching, and sales enablement to support a successful ramp

Access to an extensive mix of digital and traditional marketing solutions, enabling consultative, end-to-end strategies tailored to each client’s growth objectives

Career progression into senior sales and leadership roles

Backed by marketing expertise, post-sale specialists, and industry-leading tools

What You Will Do

Build a consistent prospecting cadence using cold calls, email, social outreach, networking, and in-person or virtual meetings to develop a strong pipeline.

Manage and grow a territory by balancing new business development, client retention, and account expansion.

Lead thoughtful discovery conversations to understand business goals, marketing challenges, and growth opportunities.

Build and present data-informed digital and traditional marketing proposals that connect strategy, tactics, and budget to client goals.

Own the full sales cycle—from initial outreach through close—while maintaining accurate CRM activity, pipeline management, and forecasting.

Partner with internal account management, creative, and strategy teams to support strong client outcomes.

Stay engaged post-sale through reporting, optimization, and performance conversations that support renewals and continued growth.

Qualifications

3+ years of B2B sales experience with success in new business development, account growth, or business development roles (experience level may vary by market and role level; Recruiter to update).

Ability to run a full-cycle, consultative sales process—from discovery through proposal, negotiation, and close.

Strong prospecting skills across phone, email, social, networking, and relationship-based outreach.

Experience using CRM and sales tools with disciplined pipeline management and follow-up.

Comfort learning and discussing digital marketing solutions such as search, social, display, and video (direct experience is a plus, not required).

Excellent communication skills, business curiosity, and the ability to build credibility with diverse clients and stakeholders, influencing decisions through clear data-driven recommendations.

Proficiency with CRM, Microsoft Office Suite, and AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot and Perplexity.

Valid driver’s license and vehicle insurance

Who Thrives Here

High performers in this role are resilient, self-motivated, strategic and creative minded and competitive, with a strong drive to outperform and continuously take on greater impact. They are coachable and highly self-directed, comfortable initiating outreach, staying organized, asking thoughtful questions, and using data and tools to work efficiently. Energized by real-time results, they handle rejection well and maintain full ownership of their performance and trajectory.

Benefits

We believe high performance should be recognized and supported through compensation, development, and real opportunity to grow your skills.

Competitive base salary + Uncapped commission opportunity

401(k) with company match

Career progression opportunities

Flexibility and autonomy in a hybrid/remote work environment

High-performance culture with recognition, incentives

Comprehensive health, dental & vision coverage options and more

Unlimited MTO time off, including paid holidays

Structured onboarding to get you ramped fast

Ongoing coaching from experienced leaders

Access to industry-leading tools, resources, and marketing expertise

Step into a territory where you can own the full sales cycle, bring smart marketing solutions to the table, and be recognized for the results you deliver. If you’re ready to grow your career and be part of a high-performing team, we encourage you to apply.

job.title: Manager, AI Engineering and Vendor Operations
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

NPR's AI Labs team is looking for a Manager of AI Engineering and Vendor Operations. This person will serve on the AI Labs leadership team and help inform NPR's AI technical strategy. We are seeking a player-coach style who understands the complexities of building adaptive and conscientious AI coding teams, and can help us apply rigor and standards to our infrastructure decisions and rollouts. In this role, you will supervise the mid-level engineering staff, provide mentorship and support to NPR's larger engineering teams and own the evaluation and deployment of the team's AI tools and vendors. This role suits someone who can weigh build-versus-buy decisions honestly, explain technical trade-offs to non-technical colleagues, and hold both vendors and our own work to NPR's standards for privacy, security, and accuracy. This is a chance to shape a new team and have a tangible effect on how NPR uses AI responsibly in service of its mission, on a team built on respect, trust, and work-life balance.

Responsibilities

  • People Leadership: Manage and mentor a team of entry and mid-level AI engineers, including hiring, onboarding, and supporting each person's professional growth.
  • Delivery: Lead technical planning, scoping, and sprint execution for AI Labs engineering work, such as NPR's AI-powered metadata service, in partnership with AI Labs leadership and editorial and business stakeholders.
  • Engineering Standards: Work with AI Labs leadership to develop AI coding frameworks, practices, and expectations for the team.
  • Code Quality and Architecture: Review designs and code, and contribute hands-on where it helps the team, keeping systems maintainable, secure, and consistent with NPR's technical standards.
  • Testing and Evaluation: Build and maintain automated testing and model evaluation practices, including regression tests and evaluation checks before release, aligned with quality bars set by the product team.
  • Production Support: Coordinate the team's response to production bugs and infrastructure incidents, and lead follow-up reviews to prevent repeat problems.
  • Vendor Evaluation: Lead technical evaluations of AI vendors, models, and tools, covering architecture, data handling, security, and cost, and recommend whether NPR should build, buy, or partner.
  • NPR-wide AI Tool Review: Participate in AI Labs' review of AI tools requested by teams across NPR, working with IT Security through the vendor risk and security intake processes. AI Labs assesses, and IT and the Office of General Counsel approve.

job.title: Data Architect I
job.description:
Want to lead the technical design behind modernizing AccuWeather For Business — the platform that delivers AccuWeather’s data and services to more than half of the Fortune 500? We are looking for a Data Architect I who combines strong platform design expertise with the judgment to assess legacy infrastructure and design an implementable, cloud-native architecture; someone who wants to own the technical direction of a critical modernization initiative without compromising the reliability enterprise clients depend on. Reporting directly to the Data Architect II overseeing AccuWeather’s data architecture function, this position will assess the legacy, on-premises infrastructure behind AccuWeather For Business and design the cloud-native architecture that will support its future. You will produce architecture and modernization design documents — including current-state assessments, target-state designs, transition and sequencing plans, and technical specifications — and work alongside engineering teams to implement key components of the architecture, while maintaining the reliability of the backend data systems that support critical data delivery services.

You will demonstrate high-level knowledge across cloud platforms and legacy enterprise systems, independently resolve complex architecture and modernization challenges, and collaborate closely with the Data Architect II and engineering teams. Your work will help modernize the technology foundation behind AccuWeather For Business, creating a more scalable, resilient, and cloud-native platform while maintaining the reliability expected by the Fortune 500 companies that depend on it.

We are open to hiring candidates to work from our global headquarters in State College, PA, USA, or remotely.

 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

· Assess the legacy, on-premises infrastructure behind AccuWeather For Business, documenting current-state architecture, system dependencies, data flows, and technical debt to inform modernization priorities.

· Design the cloud-native architecture, producing architecture designs, technical specifications, and other documentation needed to guide implementation.

· Own the architectural direction for the modernization effort, ensuring a cohesive approach across the platform rather than individual services or components.

· Develop a roadmap and sequencing plan that provides a practical path from the current environment to the cloud-native architecture while minimizing disruption to enterprise clients.

· Design backend data systems to maintain continuity of critical data delivery services throughout the transition.

· Partner with engineering and data teams to validate and implement architecture designs, ensuring solutions are secure, scalable, performant, and maintainable.

· Contribute hands-on to the implementation of architecture designs, including developing and modifying code, data models, schemas, and supporting data platform components.

· Estimate data consumption, capacity, and infrastructure requirements, incorporating cloud infrastructure costs into architecture decisions and trade-offs.

· Identify and document architectural and operational risks associated with modernizing a customer-facing production platform, and design appropriate mitigation strategies.

· Ensure the cloud-native architecture addresses performance, security, scalability, resiliency, recoverability, compliance, and data residency requirements.

· Understand system scheduling, integrations, and dependencies across the platform and incorporate them into planning and sequencing.

· Serve as a technical point of contact for questions and decisions related to the modernization effort’s architectural direction.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

· Required Qualifications:

o BA/BS in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, with 5+ years of experience in data or enterprise architecture, or MS with 3+ years of experience.

o High-level knowledge of cloud platforms (e.g., Microsoft Azure) and cloud-native architecture.

o Demonstrated experience assessing legacy, on-premises systems and designing modern, cloud-native architectures.

o Demonstrated experience planning or supporting large-scale modernization initiatives for production, customer-facing platforms.

o Experience designing production data platforms for performance, scalability, resiliency, and recoverability.

o Experience analyzing complex system dependencies, integrations, data flows, and scheduling requirements to inform architecture and modernization decisions.

o Demonstrated experience working with PostgreSQL, including relational data modeling, schema design, and query development.

o Advanced proficiency in Python or Go, with experience developing production-quality code for data platforms or backend systems.

· Preferred Qualifications:

o Experience designing backend data platforms that support data delivery to external or enterprise clients.

o Experience evaluating technology and architecture options, including build-versus-buy decisions and alternative modernization approaches.

o Experience evaluating infrastructure requirements and costs to inform cloud architecture decisions and design trade-offs.

o Familiarity with enterprise security, compliance, and data governance requirements, including SOC 2 and data residency considerations.

· Skills & Competencies:

o Strong systems thinking, with the ability to design architectures that engineering teams can implement and maintain effectively.

o Excellent written communication, with the ability to produce clear, actionable architecture and technical design documentation.

o Sound technical judgment, with the ability to translate business and platform requirements into pragmatic architecture without overengineering or underspecifying solutions.

o Ability to move effectively between architecture and hands-on implementation, translating designs into working solutions in collaboration with engineering teams.

o Ability to mentor team members and help develop the architectural judgment of less experienced engineers.

o Ability to independently lead complex, large-scale architecture initiatives and drive technical decisions through ambiguity.

 

About AccuWeather and Dr. Joel N. Myers

job.title: Database Administrator III
job.description:
Want to be part of a team that keeps AccuWeather's critical database environments reliable, secure, performant, and available around the clock for a global audience? We are looking for an experienced Database Administrator with deep hands-on expertise in SQL Server and PostgreSQL who can take ownership of the health and reliability of our production database systems while helping modernize our database infrastructure for the future. Reporting directly to the Data Architect II overseeing AccuWeather’s data architecture function, this role will serve as a hands-on database administration expert responsible for the day-to-day operational health and long-term reliability of AccuWeather's database environments. Key responsibilities include performance tuning and optimization, backup and recovery, high availability, security and access management, capacity planning, monitoring and maintenance, and incident and root-cause analysis. The DBA will work closely with the Data Architect and engineering teams to establish strong database standards, improve operational practices, and proactively address reliability and performance concerns. This role will also play an important part in the migration of select backend databases to cloud-based environments, helping assess existing workloads, plan and execute migrations, optimize databases for their target environments, and ensure appropriate performance, security, resiliency, and recoverability throughout the transition. It is an opportunity to combine deep database administration expertise with meaningful involvement in the continued modernization of AccuWeather's data infrastructure.

 

We are open to hiring candidates to work from our global headquarters in State College, PA, USA, or remotely.

 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

· Administer SQL Server and PostgreSQL databases end to end — performance tuning, query optimization, indexing strategy, and execution plan analysis.

· Design, implement, and regularly test backup, replication, and disaster recovery procedures for databases, ensuring high availability across production environments.

· Manage database security — roles, permissions, access control, and auditing.

· Monitor and plan for database capacity — storage growth, connection pooling, and resource allocation.

· Manage database version upgrades, patching cycles, and configuration tuning.

· Perform routine database maintenance — index/statistics upkeep, vacuuming, storage optimization, and space reclamation — to sustain performance over time.

· Proactively monitor database health and performance, identifying and resolving issues before they affect production.

· Manage cloud cost optimization and capacity planning, including license reporting and true-ups, resource forecasting, and optimization of Azure compute spend through Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, and related strategies.

· Partner with the Data Architect and engineering teams to establish database standards, improve operational practices, and proactively address reliability and performance concerns.

· Plan and execute database migrations to the cloud, optimizing configurations for target environments, and ensuring performance, security, resiliency, and recoverability throughout the transition.

· Build strong working relationships with engineering teams, communicating database constraints and recommendations in terms they can act on.

· Share database expertise and best practices with less experienced administrators and engineering team members.

· Performs other duties as assigned.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

· Required Qualifications:

o BA/BS in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, with 5+ years of experience in data operations or database administration, or MS with 3+ years of experience.

o Demonstrated experience as a database administrator with SQL Server and/or PostgreSQL, including performance tuning, backup and recovery, high availability, security and access management, and capacity planning.

o Advanced SQL/T-SQL proficiency, with working knowledge of at least one scripting language (Python or PowerShell) for database automation.

o Ability to design and implement monitoring solutions for database health, performance, and capacity.

o Experience with, or strong working knowledge of, migrating databases to cloud-based environments (e.g., Microsoft Azure).

o Awareness of the monetary costs associated with operational work.

o Demonstrated experience mentoring or coaching less experienced engineers.

· Preferred Qualifications:

o Experience with advanced replication topologies (e.g., multi-region, active-active) for SQL Server and/or PostgreSQL.

o Experience administrating, performance monitoring, troubleshooting, and performing backup/recovery of database systems (e.g. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Azure SQL or similar systems).

o Familiarity with, or willingness to grow into, modern cloud data platforms, including Databricks and Snowflake. Experience with CI/CD automation.

o Experience with Azure Data Factory (ADF) for building, orchestrating, and maintaining reliable data ingestion and loading pipelines.

o Experience participating in structured post-mortems and root cause analysis for significant incidents.

o Familiarity with data governance practices (quality checks, lineage documentation, access control).

· Skills & Competencies:

o Strong systems thinking; understands how failure in one system cascades to others across a portfolio.

o Sound judgment balancing database performance, availability, security, and cost trade-offs.

o Excellent written communication; operational health reports are usable by data consumers and leadership without interpretation.

o Sound judgment distinguishing proximate causes from systemic causes when writing postmortems.

o Mentoring and coaching skills; able to develop the operational judgment of less experienced engineers.

job.title: Senior Lightning Scientist
job.description:
The Senior Lightning Scientist is a subject-matter expert responsible for advancing AccuWeather’s lightning detection, analysis, and interpretation capabilities. This role combines deep scientific understanding of lightning physics with practical expertise in RF systems, sensor networks, and algorithm development. The Senior Lightning Scientist plays a critical role in improving lightning detection accuracy, developing new methodologies, guiding technical strategy, and collaborating across science, engineering, and product teams to deliver industry-leading lightning intelligence products.

Working closely with data science, hardware, and software engineering teams, this role drives innovation in lightning detection technologies, signal processing, and real-time analysis systems that support AccuWeather’s operational, commercial, and public safety offerings.

 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Serve as a technical and scientific authority on lightning physics, detection methodologies, and operational interpretation.
  • Lead the development, evaluation, and improvement of lightning detection algorithms using techniques such as TOA, TDOA, interferometry, and hybrid approaches.
  • Analyze RF signals across relevant frequency bands used in lightning detection, including waveform characterization, noise mitigation, and signal classification.
  • Collaborate with hardware and electrical engineering teams on sensor design, RF front-end considerations, antenna design, placement, and calibration strategies.
  • Develop and refine signal processing pipelines for real-time and post-processed lightning data.
  • Design, test, and validate algorithms for lightning geolocation, flash clustering, classification (e.g., CG vs IC), and quality control.
  • Evaluate network performance, detection efficiency, location accuracy, and timing precision using ground truth and statistical methods.
  • Contribute to the integration of lightning data into forecasting, nowcasting, severe weather detection, and machine learning systems.
  • Provide technical leadership, mentorship, and guidance to scientists and engineers working on lightning-related systems.
  • Document methodologies, assumptions, system limitations, and scientific findings for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with product, operations, and research teams to translate scientific advances into scalable, customer-facing solutions.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Advanced degree (PhD or MS with significant experience) in Atmospheric Science, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Geophysics, or a related field.
  • Deep understanding of lightning physics, electromagnetic emissions from lightning, and storm electrification processes.
  • Strong background in RF systems, signal processing, and spectral analysis.
  • Demonstrated experience with lightning detection techniques such as TOA, TDOA, interferometry, or related geolocation methods.
  • Proficiency in algorithm development and data analysis using Python, C++, or similar scientific computing environments.
  • Experience working with large-scale, real-time observational data systems.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.
  • Ability to communicate complex scientific and technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences

 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience designing or working directly with lightning detection hardware, sensors, or ground-based networks.
  • Background in antenna theory, antenna design, and RF propagation effects.
  • Familiarity with FPGA, SDR, or embedded systems used in RF signal acquisition.
  • Experience with cloud-based data platforms and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
  • Published research or patents related to lightning detection, RF sensing, or atmospheric electricity.
  • Experience collaborating with operational forecasting or severe weather teams.
  • Familiarity with machine learning applications applied to lightning or RF signal classification.

job.title: Alert Team Lead I
job.description:
Who We Are:

SiriusXM and its brands (Pandora, SiriusXM Media, AdsWizz, Simplecast, and SiriusXM Connect) are leading a new era of audio entertainment and services by delivering the most compelling subscription and ad-supported audio entertainment experience for listeners -- in the car, at home, and anywhere on the go with connected devices. Our vision is to shape the future of audio, where everyone can be effortlessly connected to the voices, stories and music they love wherever they are.

 

This is the place where a diverse group of emerging talent and legends alike come to share authentic and purposeful songs, stories, sounds and insights through some of the best programming and technology in the world. Our critically-acclaimed, industry-leading audio entertainment encompasses music, sports, comedy, news, talk, live events, and podcasting. No matter their individual role, each of our employees plays a vital part in bringing SiriusXM’s vision to life every day.

 

SiriusXM Connect (SiriusXM CV) is a leading provider of connected services to vehicle manufacturers, delivering one of the most broadly adopted connected vehicle platforms in North America for the last 25 years. Named the 2020 Company of the Year in the Telematics Industry by Frost & Sullivan, we provide safety, security and convenience services to millions of vehicle owners across major automotive brands. Our teams are continuously working to develop leading-edge technology that can not only add convenience to the daily lives of so many drivers across the country but our advancements in safety and security could also help save their lives.


How you’ll make an impact:
As an Alert Team Lead I, you will play a critical role in supporting the daily operations of the SiriusXM Connect Help Desk and Response Center. This position serves as a second-level support resource for contact center agents, internal business partners, and external customers. The Alert Team Lead I is responsible for resolving complex customer escalations, troubleshooting technical and service-related issues, coordinating with internal support teams, and assisting with time-sensitive safety and security requests.

You will also provide guidance to frontline agents, support operational processes, and help ensure customer concerns are handled accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with established procedures. Success in this role requires strong problem-solving skills, sound judgment, attention to detail,
and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

What You'll Do:

Operational Support & Escalation Management
• Serve as a second-level support resource for contact center agents, internal departments and external customers.
• Research, troubleshoot, and resolve complex customer concerns involving connected vehicle services, account management, billing, enrollment, and service delivery.
• Handle escalated customer interactions professionally, demonstrating empathy, accountability, and effective de-escalation techniques.
• Provide real-time guidance to frontline agents to support accurate issue resolution and minimize unnecessary escalations.

• Assist with complex service requests, including account adjustments, refund research, subscription issues, and other operational activities.
• Manage multiple priorities while maintaining service quality, accuracy, and responsiveness.

Technical Troubleshooting & Incident Management
• Investigate technical issues involving connected vehicle functionality, remote services, provisioning, enrollment, and system-related errors.
• Research account information, service history, system activity, and technical errors to identify potential causes and appropriate next steps.
• Create, document, monitor, and escalate technical support tickets through established incident management processes.
• Collaborate with internal technical teams to investigate system defects, service interruptions, and recurring technical issues.
• Communicate known system issues, approved workarounds, and troubleshooting procedures to frontline agents and operational teams.
• Follow up on unresolved technical issues and provide timely updates to appropriate stakeholders.

Safety, Security & Stolen Vehicle Support
• Support Stolen Vehicle Location (SVL) requests in accordance with established company procedures and security requirements.
• Coordinate with law enforcement agencies, Public Safety Answering Points (PSAPs), and authorized third parties when handling specialized or time-sensitive requests.
• Assist with exigent requests, missing/endangered person cases, and other safety-related escalations as authorized by company policy.
• Verify required information and documentation while maintaining customer privacy and compliance with established procedures.
• Coordinate with internal departments and external partners to support timely and accurate handling of safety and security requests.
• Maintain accurate case documentation and follow established escalation and
communication protocols.

Agent Support, Quality & Development
• Provide guidance and support to contact center agents regarding complex procedures, troubleshooting, and customer escalations.
• Reinforce established processes, service standards, and customer experience
expectations.
• Identify recurring agent knowledge gaps and communicate coaching or training opportunities to leadership.
• Assist with quality monitoring, interaction reviews, and performance feedback as assigned.
• Support new and existing agents by sharing knowledge, clarifying procedures, and promoting consistent service delivery.

• Contribute to achieving operational performance, service quality, and customer satisfaction objectives.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Client Support
• Partner with Account Managers and internal business teams to research customer concerns and support client relationships.
• Provide accurate updates regarding escalated issues, service tickets, and operational concerns.
• Collaborate with technical support teams, operations, and other departments to resolve issues affecting customers or service delivery.
• Communicate process changes, system updates, and operational guidance to
appropriate teams.
• Identify opportunities to improve workflows, reduce repeat contacts, and enhance operational efficiency.

Documentation, Reporting & Continuous Improvement
• Maintain accurate and complete documentation of customer interactions, escalations, service tickets, and operational activities.
• Assist with operational reporting, quality reviews, audits, and special projects as assigned.
• Monitor recurring issues and identify trends that may require additional investigation or process improvements.
• Support compliance with established policies, procedures, privacy requirements, and quality standards.
• Perform administrative duties and other responsibilities as assigned by leadership.

What You'll Need:

Required Qualifications
• High school diploma or equivalent.
• Minimum of one year of experience in a fast-paced customer service or contact center environment.
• Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex information clearly and professionally.
• Demonstrated customer service skills, including empathy, active listening, conflict resolution, and de-escalation.
• Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
• Ability to research complex issues, exercise sound judgment, and determine appropriate resolution or escalation paths.
• Ability to multitask and manage competing priorities while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.
• Willingness to learn new technologies, systems, and operational procedures.

• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with team members and cross-functional partners.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook and other standard business applications.
• Must have legal authorization to work in the United States.

Preferred Qualifications
• One to two years of operations, customer service leadership, or contact center support experience.
• Experience providing agent guidance, coaching, training, or second-level operational support.
• Familiarity with contact center performance metrics, quality standards, and escalation procedures.
• Experience with customer relationship management (CRM), ticketing, or incident management systems.
• Familiarity with Salesforce, ServiceNow, Genesys, or similar applications.
• Technical troubleshooting experience involving connected services, mobile applications, account provisioning, or system-related issues.
• Knowledge of automotive connected vehicle services, safety and security operations, or telematics.
• Experience working with internal technical teams, external business partners, or law enforcement agencies.

Key Competencies
• Customer Focus & Accountability.
• Technical Troubleshooting & Critical Thinking.
• Communication & De-escalation.
• Operational Excellence & Attention to Detail.
• Leadership & Team Collaboration.
• Adaptability & Continuous Improvement.
• Sound Judgment & Confidentiality.

Research & Development at The New York Times explores how emerging technologies can be applied in service of journalism. We collaborate with designers, developers, reporters, photographers and editors to bring new forms of storytelling to life, from prototyping to publishing.

At The Times, technology permeates every aspect of our business, from our thought-provoking coverage of technological trends to the digital-first transformation of our own business to the changing world of our readers. The Research & Development team explores the new opportunities that emerging technologies may provide the New York Times and our commercial and strategic goals.

You will report to the Executive Director of R&D.

Responsibilities:

  • Design and implement LLM-backed APIs – driving improvements to reach target outcomes through evaluation, grounding and fine-tuning best practices.
  • Deploy reliable services within cloud environments (such as GCP or AWS) to support high-traffic LLM applications.

  • Maintain comprehensive documentation to facilitate feature handoff and future maintenance.

Through industry expertise, account intelligence, and close collaboration with Client Partners, BDAs translate market opportunities into focused prospecting strategies and meaningful conversations with prospective advertisers. Their work strengthens pipeline quality, expands our reach into priority markets, and increases the team’s capacity to develop and grow advertising partnerships.

Go deeper: As a BDA, you will develop and execute business-development initiatives across assigned industries, markets, or products. You will work alongside Client Partners to evaluate opportunities, prioritize accounts, understand prospective advertisers’ business needs, and determine effective approaches to engagement.

  • The role combines research and analysis with direct prospect engagement, performance evaluation, and continuous improvement. 
  • You will exercise judgment in selecting accounts and stakeholders, developing messaging, evaluating advertiser fit, and recommending next steps.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Shape prospecting priorities: Analyze industry trends, buying signals, account potential, and alignment with Axios audiences and products to develop prioritized account recommendations. Explain the rationale, potential value, and trade-offs behind proposed priorities, and reassess them as market conditions and prospect needs change.
  • Partner on account strategy: Develop account briefs that synthesize prospective advertisers’ business priorities, relevant stakeholders, potential needs, and engagement opportunities. Recommend messaging and engagement approaches, and partner with Client Partners to evaluate alternatives and determine next steps aligned with advertiser needs and revenue goals.
  • Develop prospective relationships: Create targeted outreach connecting prospect objectives with Axios audiences, products, and proof points. Adapt engagement based on responses and results.
  • Evaluate early opportunities: Assess advertiser fit, needs, timing, and potential; nurture interest and equip Client Partners with context and recommended next steps.
  • Improve performance: Analyze outreach effectiveness, prospect feedback, and pipeline progression to identify barriers and evaluate alternative approaches. Recommend and implement approved improvements to targeting, messaging, follow-up, and handoffs, and assess whether those changes improve results.
  • Refine tools and workflows: Test AI and automation with leadership, Revenue Operations, and Enablement to improve effectiveness, validate quality, and create capacity.
  • Build shared expertise: Translate successful campaigns, industry insights, and workflow improvements into practical playbooks and resources for the broader team.

Worthy of your time: Ideal candidates will embody an entrepreneurial spirit, a passion for Axios’ mission, and the following skills:

  • Experience in business development, advertising, sales, marketing, or a related client-facing role; at least one year preferred.
  • Strong research and analytical skills, including the ability to translate market information and performance data into actionable recommendations.
  • Sound commercial judgment and the ability to evaluate opportunities, weigh alternatives, and explain priorities.
  • Experience developing targeted outreach and managing early-stage sales opportunities.
  • Ability to build productive partnerships and contribute ideas to shared account and business-development strategies.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to connect advertiser needs with a relevant value proposition.
  • Strong project management skills and the ability to manage competing priorities with initiative and accountability.
  • Proficiency with CRM and sales-engagement tools, and curiosity about using AI and automation to improve results. 
  • A willingness to test approaches, learn from feedback, and share successful practices with others.

Starting salary for this role is in the range of $65,000 - $75,000 annually and is dependent on numerous factors, including but not limited to location, work experience, and skills. This range does not include other compensation and benefits.

Axios is committed to embracing artificial intelligence as a core part of how we work. All team members are expected to actively develop AI literacy and use AI tools to enhance their productivity, creativity, and efficiency. We invest in ongoing learning to ensure every employee is equipped to responsibly and effectively integrate AI into their daily workflows.

  • Robust PPO and High Deductible health insurance options on the Blue Cross Blue Shield network
  • Employer Health Savings Account (HSA) contribution for the high-deductible health plan option

  • Inclusive fertility, hormonal health, and family-forming benefits through Carrot Fertility
  • Access to the Axios “Family Fund”, which was created to allow employees to request financial support when facing financial hardship or emergencies
  • Increased work flexibility for parents and caretakers
  • Virtual company-sponsored social events
