LEAD SOFTWARE ENGINEER — ROKU

 

Location: On-Site - New York / Los Angeles / San Francisco / Ft. Lauderdale


ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll own the technical direction of the Paramount+ Roku application — the platform, the patterns, the architecture. This is a hands-on leadership role where you write and review code and set the standard for a team of engineers shipping features to millions of viewers.

Roku's constraints — tight memory budgets, a single-threaded render loop, hardware spanning five years of device generations — are the environment you thrive in, not just tolerate. You know these constraints well enough to teach them, and you'll lead a team through them.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Set technical direction for the Paramount+ Roku application — choose the patterns, own the architecture, defend the decisions
• Build and maintain core framework components and features — this is a hands-on role where you ship code
• Lead a team of Roku engineers through code reviews, pair programming, and feedback that helps people grow• Architect around Roku's constraints: memory limits, render-thread/task-thread boundaries, device performance tiers, and certification requirements• Ship real-time personalization features — personalized recommendations, dynamic artwork, and ad engagement experiences — within Roku's memory and threading constraints
• Drive adoption of RSG 1.3 data transfer APIs, BrightScript Memory Monitor, and Perfetto tracing across the team
• Scope projects, identify risks before they become blockers, and keep the team shipping
• Coordinate with Product, Design, Backend Engineering, and DevOps/SRE to translate requirements into plans your team can execute
• Write architecture docs, RFCs, and component guides so decisions are visible and durable
• Maintain and improve CI/CD pipelines, testing infrastructure, and build tooling
• Design and run A/B tests, then act on the results
• Use AI development tools to move faster, and help the team adopt them


WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE

• Your team ships on time because you scoped the work correctly — not because anyone worked weekends
• Engineers on your team grow quarter over quarter. They take on harder problems this quarter than last. You can name what changed
• You open a 200-file BrightScript repo you've never seen and start making changes the same day — and you've given your team the docs and context to do the same• You notice a memory spike on a Roku Express before QA files a ticket. You fix it, write up what happened, and turn it into a pattern the team follows• You write architecture decisions down. Six months later, a new engineer reads one and understands why you chose what you chose
• You push back when a plan has gaps and suggest a better one — without making people feel small
• You treat the build pipeline, test coverage, and error monitoring like product features
• You make the people around you better at their jobs. They'd say so if asked


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 8+ years writing software
• 4+ years building Roku applications
• 2+ years leading a team or serving as a technical lead• BS in Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent work experience• Strong foundation in OOP, data structures, and algorithms — able to design systems and evaluate others' designs
• BrightScript and SceneGraph SDK, including RSG 1.3 — you can explain the tradeoffs between MoveIntoField, PostMessage, and CopyMessage without looking them up
• Deep command of the Roku threading model and where performance falls apart on low-end devices
• Roku frameworks and services: RAF, RMF, RokuPay
• Unit and integration testing on Roku — you've built test infrastructure, not just written tests
• RESTful API design, HTTP caching behavior, and CDN interaction
• Git and GitHub
• Strong technical writing — architecture docs and plans that people actually read and act on
• Active use of AI development tools (Copilot, Claude, Cursor, or similar) with concrete examples of how they've changed how you work


DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• BrighterScript and Roku community tooling (ropm, bslint, roku-debug)
• Other OTT platforms: Fire TV, Android TV, Apple TV, Samsung TV, LG webOS
• Observability tools: Conviva, New Relic, Datadog, Sentry• Microservices and backend-for-frontend patterns• Experience integrating personalization or recommendation systems into connected-device applications
• Experience with real-time or event-driven architectures on client platforms
• E2E testing for connected-device applications
• Docker and CI/CD tooling (Jenkins or similar)
• GraphQL
• Track record of introducing AI tools to a team — actual adoption, not just a demo
• You care about UX enough to push back on Product and Design when something isn't right

job.description:
Storytelling is, and will always be, the heart of what we do at Skydance.
Our vision is to build a thriving entertainment ecosystem where stories and worlds are imagined, brought to life and experienced. If you’re energized by the opportunity to help build the next-generation global media and entertainment company powered by creativity and technology, we’d be thrilled to welcome you aboard. LET’S GO!

 

Overview
As Principal Product Manager, Ads Monetization, you’ll use machine learning and AI to help Paramount+ and Pluto TV earn more from advertising while keeping the viewing experience great. Sitting within our Consumer AI group, you’ll do two things: lead the product direction for ML-driven improvements to our ad systems, and act as the Ads team’s go-to product partner for AI/ML needs. You’ll work as a senior individual contributor under limited supervision, setting your own priorities and making most product calls individually, with executive team guidance on overall strategy. This is a [hybrid] role.

 

Primary Responsibilities

  • Own the vision, strategy and roadmap for AI/ML-driven ads monetization across Paramount+ and Pluto TV, spanning areas such as ad decisioning, result optimization, pacing, forecasting and personalization. Make self-directed decisions on prioritization, trade-offs and sequencing, and align the roadmap with Consumer AI and Ads executive team.
  • Drive ML-powered optimization of ad systems by partnering with data scientists and ML engineers to define model objectives, constraints and success metrics. Balance revenue, viewer experience and advertiser outcomes, and decide independently which model and product bets to pursue.
  • Serve as the AI/ML product partner to the Ads team. Gather needs from Ad Sales, Ad Operations, Planning and Finance, and shape them into AI/ML solutions (including generative AI workflows). Prioritize requests independently, and align on cross-team commitments with Ads product leadership.
  • Define requirements and evaluation frameworks for ML-based products, including data needs, experiment design, A/B testing and ongoing model performance monitoring. Use results to quantify revenue impact and decide whether to scale, iterate or stop initiatives.
  • Influence stakeholders at all levels, including Engineering, Data Science, Ad Sales, Ad Operations, Finance, Legal and Privacy. Present strategy, results and trade-offs to senior executives. Decisions with significant budget, privacy or advertiser-contract implications are made jointly with the hiring manager or relevant committees.
  • Raise the bar for product practice by mentoring other product managers, setting standards for how ML products are scoped and measured, and sharing learnings across Consumer AI. Provide indirect executive team through influence, with no formal direct reports at this time.

Basic Qualifications  

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Business or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10+ years of product management experience, including 5+ years managing advertising, ad tech or monetization products.
  • Extensive knowledge of how ML is applied to advertising problems such as ranking, prediction, forecasting and optimization, with 3+ years shipping ML-driven products in partnership with data scientists and ML engineers.
  • Working knowledge of the ad serving and decisioning stack, including auctions, pacing, outcome management, and supply- and demand-side technologies.
  • Expertise in experimentation and measurement, including defining success metrics, A/B testing and interpreting results to drive decisions.
  • Knowledge with generative AI and LLM product concepts, including evaluation and iteration.
  • Proven ability to lead cross-functionally without direct authority and to communicate clearly with senior executives.

 

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with linked TV (CTV), video or live sports advertising.
  • Advanced degree or hands-on technical skills (e.g., SQL, Python) for working directly with data.
  • Experience with identity, audience signals, clean rooms or privacy-compliant data use in advertising.
  • Experience with generative AI applied to ad creative or ad operations workflows.
  • Experience mentoring or managing product managers.

job.title: Breaking News Reporter
job.description:
The Cincinnati Enquirer/cincinnati.com part of the USA TODAY NETWORK, is seeking a digital-first reporter to be part of the Breaking News team.

Job Details:

This reporter will be at the center of the region's biggest stories, from breaking crime and public safety news to severe weather. The reporter understands that breaking news is often the front door to deeper accountability and enterprise reporting.  A great breaking news reporter cuts through official-speak and lets the community know what’s happening clearly and concisely. We’re looking for a reporter who goes beyond standard press releases, digging into how and why things happen. Reporters on this team also pursue explainers, features and other enterprise stories that reflect life in Greater Cincinnati.  The position requires urgency, curiosity, accuracy and a willingness to chase news wherever it leads. It also demands strong news judgment and the ability to find and identify stories with impact and reflect the community through the inclusion of a variety of voices.

About The Enquirer:

The Enquirer, founded in 1851, serves communities in southwest Ohio and Northern Kentucky. With major league sports (go Bengals!), a blossoming food and craft beer scene, hundreds of parks, world-class performing arts and eight Fortune 500 companies, Cincinnati offers the amenities of a big city with the comfort and charm of a small town.

Responsibilities:

Monitor real-time news and sniff out stories that are important to our audiences.

Report quickly, clearly and accurately and deliver news via stories, video, newsletters, Facebook, X, Instagram, TikTok or any other methods available to reach our audience and develop new audiences.

Use metrics to inform story choices and shape beat strategies.

Work a schedule that may include nights, weekends and whenever news demands.

Work with editors to experiment with new ways of informing and engaging audiences on social platforms and through alternate story forms. This includes long-tail (evergreen) content.

Requirements:

Bachelor's or master’s in communications, journalism or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

2 + years of reporting experience, applicants with less experience and strong clips may be considered.

Proven ability to write on deadline.

Exceptional core journalism skills (reporter, producing, editing). Strong command of AP grammar and style.

Familiarity with public records and their use in reporting.

Self-motivation and self-direction.

Photo and video skills.

Effective communicator; able to get along with diverse personalities.

Knows how to use time effectively in a 24-hour news environment.

Works collaboratively within a cross-functional environment.

Must embrace peer-to-peer feedback and training.

Applies innovative, creative thinking to support the company's goals.

Industry knowledge.

Organizational skills.

Command of media law and Principles of Ethical Conduct.

This position sometimes requires employees to work extended hours, evening, weekends and holidays, sometimes unexpectedly.

This role requires a valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, and the minimum liability insurance required by state law.

Employment is contingent on passing a post-offer pre-employment background check, motor vehicle record check.

Application Instructions:  We are eager to learn more about you and how you fit this role. When you apply, don’t limit your upload to a resume; show us what you’ve done. To do so, put together a single document file that includes the following, in this order:

Your resume – one to two pages.

A cover letter that outlines how you would approach the job.

Links to 3-6 online samples of your work. Show us what you’ve produced or had a hand in that best reflects what you can do in your desired role.

It is important that these items be assembled into a single document and uploaded in PDF format. Completing these steps will ensure that your application receives the highest consideration.

job.title: Video Producer
job.description:
USA TODAY Co. is seeking a detail-oriented, platform-native video producer to expand video support for local USA TODAY Network newsrooms. This full-time role will use strong editorial judgment and AI-assisted production workflows to turn local reporting, photos, data and graphics into timely, accurate and engaging short-form video.

The producer will work directly with local reporters, editors and newsroom leaders to identify stories that can reach broader audiences through video. Coverage will span the range of local journalism, including breaking news, public safety, weather, government, education, business, consumer issues, community stories, major local events and other topics important to individual markets. This is a hands-on production and service role focused on helping local newsrooms publish more video efficiently across owned and social platforms.

What you’ll do:

Serve as a dedicated video production resource for local USA TODAY Network newsrooms, supporting market needs and network-wide local coverage priorities.

Use AI-assisted platforms, including Stringr, along with templates, automation and editing tools to produce a high volume of accurate, on-brand video from local reporting, photos, data, graphics, user-generated content and newsroom briefs.

Use Stringr AI UGC production capabilities to help local newsrooms identify and develop relevant user-generated content into publishable video while following verification, sourcing, rights and editorial standards.

Use Stringr Clip Gen to create timely clips and short-form video from press conferences, public meetings, interviews, podcasts and other longer recordings.

Use Stringr Show Stacker and other AI-assisted long-form production tools to assemble structured video from local programs, interviews, recurring shows and extended newsroom content.

Partner with local reporters, editors and newsroom leaders to identify stories with strong visual, audience and distribution potential.

Respond quickly to local breaking news and major developing stories while also supporting planned enterprise, service and community coverage.

Create useful explainers that make complex local topics clear, accessible and relevant to the communities our newsrooms serve.

Turn newsroom briefs and published stories into clear video treatments, selecting effective visuals, scripts, on-screen text, audio, pacing and formats.

Adapt local journalism into platform-native vertical video for TikTok, Instagram Reels, Facebook, YouTube Shorts and other platforms.

Repurpose AI-assisted and automated content for owned-and-operated and social platforms, tailoring each version to the audience, market and platform.

Optimize video length, aspect ratio, captions, headlines, thumbnails, metadata and calls to action using platform best practices and performance insights.

Program videos on corresponding local articles and support distribution workflows that increase the reach and value of local journalism.

Manage and prioritize requests from multiple newsrooms, communicate progress and blockers, and balance planned work with urgent coverage needs.

Maintain editorial, legal, brand and visual standards, including accuracy, sourcing, attribution, captions, fonts, colors and overall presentation.

Track core performance metrics, identify successful local formats and topics, and share repeatable lessons with newsroom and video partners.

job.title: Account Manager, Strategic Partnerships
job.description:
AccuWeather’s mission is to save lives, protect property, and help people and companies make the best weather-impacted decisions. We are seeking an enthusiastic, curious, and growth-oriented Account Manager to advance that mission through our technology and media partnerships.

You will manage a portfolio of technology and media partners and work with some of the world’s leading companies. Your work will help partners strengthen their products, serve their audiences, and achieve their business goals—bringing trusted weather intelligence to the platforms people use every day.

As part of the Strategic Account Management team, you will gain exposure to AccuWeather’s top strategic accounts and complex commercial deals, learning how major partnerships are developed, negotiated, and expanded. You will build skills in commercial judgment, data analysis, storytelling, negotiation, and strategic relationship management.

You will understand your partners’ businesses, dig into performance data, and identify how AccuWeather’s Proven Superior Accuracy™, proprietary products, and ongoing innovation can help them achieve more.

Success requires a commitment to partner service and a drive to grow revenue. Business development will focus on expanding existing relationships across technology and media, primarily in the business-to-business-to-consumer (B2B2C) space. External prospecting is outside this role’s scope.

You will be part of a collaborative team, sharing insights, contributing ideas, and working toward shared goals. You will receive direct training, coaching, and mentorship while taking increasing ownership of your accounts. We are looking for someone who takes initiative, follows through independently, welcomes feedback, and helps improve both our partnerships and how we work together.

What you will do

  • Own partner relationships. Manage a portfolio of technology and media accounts, developing a strong understanding of each partner’s goals, products, audiences, and priorities. Build trust through thoughtful engagement, responsive service, and reliable follow-through.
  • Know the data. Analyze revenue, API usage, audience engagement, referral traffic, and other relevant metrics. Investigate changes, recognize opportunities, and turn findings into recommendations that improve performance and support partner goals.
  • Lead business reviews. Prepare and conduct regular partner meetings and quarterly business reviews that demonstrate value, assess performance, and look ahead. Work with partners to identify priorities, explore opportunities, and agree on actions and next steps.
  • Tell the AccuWeather story. Learn how AccuWeather’s forecast accuracy, scientific expertise, and proprietary offerings—including AccuWeather MinuteCast® and RealFeel®—help partners deliver differentiated experiences and enable users to make more confident decisions.
  • Bring fresh opportunities to partners. Gather relevant product updates, innovations, success stories, awards, and achievements from across AccuWeather. Connect them to each partner’s needs to strengthen their offerings and expand the value of the relationship.
  • Grow existing accounts. Identify where additional AccuWeather capabilities can advance partner goals through expanded usage, new products, new applications, and broader partnerships. Develop account plans, advance commercial opportunities, and achieve revenue growth targets.
  • Collaborate and advocate for partners. Bring partner needs, feedback, and ideas into AccuWeather. Work with product, technical account management, forecasting, marketing, finance, legal, and other teams to resolve issues, develop solutions, and advance shared opportunities.
  • Present with clarity and impact. Develop and deliver presentations for partners and internal audiences. Use compelling narratives, clear visuals, and well-presented data to communicate results, explain opportunities, and support decisions.
  • Use AI to increase effectiveness. Apply AI tools to research, analysis, presentation development, and routine workflows to improve efficiency and the quality of your work. Explore emerging capabilities and use judgment to verify outputs and protect confidential information.
  • Maintain account discipline. Keep account plans, CRM records, revenue forecasts, commitments, and follow-up actions accurate and current. Track contractual obligations, renewals, and emerging risks.

What you bring

  • Energy and enthusiasm: You take an active interest in your work, engage thoughtfully with people, and bring momentum to opportunities and challenges.
  • Curiosity and a learning mindset: You ask good questions, seek context, and enjoy building expertise in unfamiliar subjects.
  • Coachability: You listen to feedback, put it into practice, and take responsibility for improving your work.
  • A commitment to partner service: You listen carefully, seek to understand what success means for your partners, and care about helping them achieve it.
  • Commercial motivation: You want to achieve measurable revenue growth by connecting partner needs with valuable business opportunities.
  • An interest in data: You like working with numbers, investigating what drives performance, and explaining what the findings mean.
  • Communication and visual storytelling: You enjoy—or are motivated to develop your ability in—presenting to others and translating complex information into clear conversations, written updates, and visually effective presentations.
  • Self-awareness and ownership: You understand that your actions, communication, and follow-through affect partners and teammates. You take responsibility for your work, acknowledge mistakes, seek help when needed, and act on what you learn.
  • Initiative and independent judgment: You organize your work, solve problems, and move priorities forward while recognizing when to seek guidance.
  • Teamwork and collaboration: You enjoy working within a team, share knowledge and ideas, and support your colleagues. You contribute to shared goals and look for ways to improve how the team works together.
  • AI curiosity and adaptability: You follow emerging AI tools and trends and actively look for ways to use them to improve productivity, strengthen your work, and increase your impact.

Relevant experience and skills

  • Experience in account management, customer success, partnerships, business development, or a related client-facing setting. Relevant experience may come from employment, internships, or substantial academic, volunteer, or leadership responsibilities.
  • Strong organization and the ability to manage multiple relationships, priorities, and commitments.
  • Comfort using spreadsheets to analyze data and presentation tools to communicate findings.
  • Practical familiarity with generative AI tools and a willingness to build proficiency in applying them to business tasks.
  • Experience with technology, digital media, APIs, data licensing, or B2B2C partnerships is helpful.
  • An interest in weather and its impact on people and businesses, along with a desire to learn and communicate AccuWeather’s brand and story.

We welcome early-career candidates and those with transferable experience who can demonstrate the curiosity, analytical ability, initiative, and sense of responsibility this role requires.

What success looks like

Your partners view you as a trusted, proactive resource who understands their business and helps them achieve meaningful results. You have a strong command of account performance, deliver engaging and useful business reviews, and turn insights into action. You achieve revenue growth goals by expanding the value partners receive from AccuWeather.

As you build your expertise, you demonstrate increasing independence, sound judgment, and confidence. You apply feedback, contribute to your teammates’ success, and grow into a capable commercial professional who makes a measurable impact.

 

About AccuWeather and Dr. Joel N. Myers

AccuWeather, recognized and documented as the most accurate and most used source of weather forecasts and warnings in the world, has saved over 12,000 lives, prevented injury to over 100,000 people, and saved companies tens of billions of dollars through better planning and decision-making. Over one billion people around the world rely on AccuWeather’s proven Superior Accuracy™. AccuWeather.com is the #1 weather destination globally and one of the top 100 most-visited websites in the world, and our award-winning AccuWeather app delivers detailed real-time forecasts to tens of millions of smartphones.

AccuWeather forecasts also appear on digital signage, in 700 newspapers, are heard on over 400 radio stations, and viewed on 100 television stations. The AccuWeather Network and AccuWeather NOW® reach an audience of over 250 million on cable and streaming platforms including DirecTV, Charter Communications - Spectrum, Verizon, Philo, Frndly TV, Comcast’s Xfinity X1 and Xfinity Stream, Roku, Xumo, Rockbot, Samsung, LG, and Amazon Freevee.

AccuWeather For Business serves more than half of the Fortune 500 companies and thousands of other businesses and government agencies globally.

Dr. Joel Myers, Founder and Executive Chair, established AccuWeather in 1962 and is considered the “father of modern commercial meteorology.” Myers, a leading creative thinker and visionary, has been called “the most accurate man in weather” by The New York Times and has been recognized as one of the top entrepreneurs in American history by Entrepreneur’s Encyclopedia of Entrepreneurs. Dr. Myers was inducted into the Broadcasting+Cable Hall of Fame, Class of 2026, in recognition of his role in revolutionizing weather forecasting through teaching, research, and building AccuWeather into one of the world’s major sources of weather data, forecasts, and warnings.

  • Ability to present complex thinking in a clear, linear and succinct manner
  • Incorporate the passion, excitement and experience of one’s MINOR in relevant ways that inform and validate the company’s output

Role Overview We are looking for a Research Scientist, AI Music to advance the state of the art in AI-powered music creation, transformation, and interaction. In this role, you will research, develop, and evaluate machine learning models that enable new ways for people to play with music, while translating cutting-edge research into intuitive, high-quality product experiences. You’ll work at the intersection of music, machine learning, and creative technology, collaborating closely with our music technology team, producers, and product and engineering partners to turn creative ideas into powerful AI tools. From exploring generative audio models and music understanding to developing novel ways to remix, transform, and interact with music, you’ll help define how AI can make musical expression more accessible. At Hook, we believe the future of AI music should be built responsibly. We are committed to developing tools that respect artists, their creative work, and the rights of music creators and rightsholders. You’ll help shape this approach by building AI systems that enable creative expression while prioritizing ethical data practices, transparency, and responsible use of music. Responsibilities Research and develop AI music models: Design and develop machine learning models for music generation, transformation, remixing, and creative interaction. Explore emerging technologies: Investigate advances in generative audio, music understanding, audio representation learning, and related areas of machine learning. Translate research into products: Turn research ideas and prototypes into practical, high-quality AI capabilities, working closely with engineering and music technology teams. Experiment and evaluate: Design experiments and evaluation frameworks to assess audio quality, musicality, controllability, performance, and creative usefulness. Collaborate with creative teams: Work closely with producers, musicians, and cross-functional teams to understand creative workflows and develop intuitive, musically meaningful tools. Champion responsible AI development: Consider music rights, training data provenance, artist consent, and attribution throughout model development. Qualifications Advanced degree (PhD or MS) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Audio Signal Processing, Music Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Strong foundation in machine learning, deep learning, and statistical methods, with experience developing and evaluating ML models. Experience with audio or music-related machine learning, such as generative audio, music understanding, audio representation learning, source separation, or signal processing. Proficiency in Python and modern ML frameworks, such as PyTorch. Familiarity with audio processing libraries, datasets, and evaluation techniques. Ability to conduct independent applied research and translate research insights into working prototypes and real-world applications. Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical and creative disciplines. Genuine interest in music, creative tools, and the ways technology can expand musical expression. Bonus Qualifications Experience training, fine-tuning, or deploying generative audio or music models, including diffusion-based, autoregressive, or other neural audio architectures. Experience with audio codecs, neural vocoders, audio tokenization, text-audio models, or multimodal learning. Familiarity with agent frameworks and workflow orchestration tools for building multi-step AI applications. Familiarity with music production workflows, DAWs, audio plugins, or creative software. Experience collaborating directly with producers, musicians, or other creative professionals to develop or evaluate AI-powered tools. Experience building low-latency, interactive audio systems or deploying ML models in production environments. Experience designing evaluation methods for subjective qualities such as musicality, expressiveness, controllability, and creative utility. Knowledge of responsible AI practices for music, including rights-aware dataset development, artist consent, data provenance, and attribution. Research publications or contributions in machine learning, audio processing, generative AI, or music information retrieval. Our Approach to Responsible AI Music At Hook, we believe AI should expand what people can do with music while respecting the people who create it. We build with artists and rightsholders in mind, and we aim to develop AI tools that support creative expression rather than undermine the value of human creativity. This means taking a thoughtful approach to the music and data used in model development, respecting rights and permissions, and considering how our technology affects artists, producers, and the broader music ecosystem. We value researchers who bring both technical ambition and a strong sense of responsibility to their work, and who see ethical considerations as an integral part of building great products. What We Offer The opportunity to shape the future of AI-powered music creation and expression. Freedom to explore ambitious research ideas and influence technical and product direction. Close collaboration with a multidisciplinary team of researchers, engineers, music technologists, and producers. The opportunity to see your research become real tools used in creative workflows. A mission-driven environment focused on making music more interactive, accessible, and expressive while respecting the people behind it. Support for continued learning, research, and professional growth. Competitive compensation and benefits.

What We Offer Hands-on experience researching and building AI-powered music tools. The opportunity to work on real-world challenges in generative AI, audio modeling, and music technology. job.title: Lead Software Engineer (Portals)
job.description:
About SoundExchange

SoundExchange is the largest global neighboring rights organization in the world, redefining how creators in the music industry get paid. By turning data into fast, accurate revenue for artists and rights owners, we have collected and distributed more than $13 billion in digital performance royalties to date on behalf of more than 800,000 music creators. As the sole organization designated by the U.S. government to administer the Section 114 sound recording license, SoundExchange seamlessly collects and distributes digital performance royalties from platforms like Pandora, SiriusXM, iHeartRadio, and thousands more, as well as all available international performance royalties through a strong global partnership network. 

 

Title: Lead Software Engineer/Engineering Manager (Portals Team)
Department: Technology
Job Location: Washington, DC or anywhere (Continental US) (If local, on-site Tuesdays and Wednesdays)
Reports To: Director, Engineering
Supervisory Role: No
FLSA Status: Exempt

Position Summary:

The Lead Software Engineer for our Portals team will be a key contributor to full lifecycle software development while coaching, leading, and mentoring their small technical team. This role oversees the technical details and day-to-day execution of all new features and operational activities within the development team in collaboration with the technical product owner. The Lead Engineer is a critical element in our agile delivery process for new features and capabilities to support our growing music royalty processing platform.

Essential Functions:

• Provide hands-on technical leadership to a small team of software engineers
• Collaborate across teams to estimate, design, develop, support, test, and deliver data driven solutions
• Facilitate architecture discussions and decision-making both within and across teams
• Interface with key project stakeholders, mentor team members, and promote and improve software engineering practices
• Demonstrate responsibility, accountability, and dedication to engineering team and company success
• Establish and promote use of technologies and processes that lower risk and increase efficiency
• Support and improve software development standards and best practices, including generative coding, peer reviews, and source control
• Support and improve existing software applications and design, or collaborate on designing, new software applications or features
• Take responsibility for full Agile SDLC, especially from refinement to release
• Lead, coach, and develop team members by setting clear expectations, providing timely feedback, supporting growth, and fostering a collaborative and accountable work environment

Required Knowledge, Skills, Abilities (KSAs):

• Proficiency at designing and developing software using many of the following: Python, Django, SQL (Postgres), AWS (S3, ECS, OpenSearch, RDS, Cloudfront, etc.), JavaScript, Typescript, JPax, Git, Kiro
• Experience with Terraform or other infrastructure as code technologies
• Experience with Vue3 or other UI frameworks
• Experience with migrating legacy application to modern technologies
• Experience building enterprise software with complex business rules and data models
• Experience designing and developing microservices or other distributed systems
• Experience with scaling to work with large data sets
• Ability to influence and communicate effectively with team members, peers, and business partners
• Proficiency in Agile software development methodology, processes, and practices

Required Education, Certifications/ Licenses, Related Experience:

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent experience
• 7 or more years of experience in software engineering
• At least 2 years of experience leading a software engineering team

ADA Specifications:

• This position requires the ability to remain in a stationary position (standing and/or seated) all of the time
• This position requires the ability to spend all of the time viewing computer monitors

Travel Requirements:

• If hired remote, this person is expected to travel to the Washington DC corporate office as needed (3-4 times per year).

 

PAY RANGE: $171,000.00 - $209,000.00 

Note:

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by the individual(s) assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required. Management reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary.

Taking Care Of The Band:

At SoundExchange we empower creators and help shape the future of music. One way we do this is by respecting different voices, varied perspectives, and distinct backgrounds of all our team members. We are intentional in creating a culture where we recognize that all employees have the opportunities and support needed to thrive. We strive to create teams that reflect the music community we serve – every individual’s unique attributes and abilities are valued, and are part of how we innovate, create, and deliver experiences to the creators we champion.

SoundExchange has an employee-led committee that focuses on amplifying different voices and backgrounds and undertakes activities to promote inclusion and access. It helps to cultivate SoundExchange culture and policies, advocates for equality within the music industry, and participates in community building activities in the Washington, DC area where SoundExchange is located.

All with the goal of promoting more belonging and access in the workplace, music industry, and local community.

We will make a determination on your request for reasonable accommodation on a case-by-case basis.  If you need an accommodation, please email jobs@soundexchange.com.

job.title: Promoter's Assistant, Outdoor Shows
job.description:
Job Summary:

Company: Cuffe & Taylor

Department: Outdoor Promoters

Location: Preston, Lancashire or Farringdon, London

Reports to: Executive Assistant to the Outdoor Promoters

Working Hours: Full time, 40 hours per week with extra weekend working throughout festival season onsite. Some travel required.

Job Type: Permanent

 

Role Description

 

Cuffe & Taylor is one of the UK’s leading live music, theatre and entertainment promoters, delivering major concerts, festivals and tours across the UK and internationally.

 

The company has worked with some of the world’s biggest artists, including Diana Ross, Lionel Richie, Britney Spears, Kylie, Lewis Capaldi, Sam Fender, Stevie Wonder, Justin Timberlake, Noah Kahan, Alanis Morissette, Robbie Williams, Richard Ashcroft, Becky Hill, Biffy Clyro and Fatboy Slim.

 

Its extensive outdoor portfolio includes Lytham Festival, Blackweir, Live at Powderham, Scarborough Open Air Theatre, Live at The Piece Hall, Blenheim Palace Festival, Bedford Summer Sessions, Depot Live at Cardiff Castle, Forest Live and Live at Lincoln Castle.

 

Cuffe & Taylor also operates a successful UK and international theatre touring division, programming thousands of performances across live entertainment, podcasts, screen-to-stage adaptations and musical theatre. In 2023, its original production Hey Duggee – The Live Theatre Show won the Olivier Award for Best Family Show.

 

The Promoter Assistant will be a key member of the Outdoor Promoter team, providing support in the programming and delivery of festivals, concerts and tours. The role covers the administrative side of events, from the offer letter stage right through to settlement, which involves working closely with the Operations, Finance, Ticketing, Marketing and Production and Artist Liaison teams.

 

The role will also involve diary management, scheduling and preparation for meetings, travel logistics for the Promoter team and general administration, including filing and coding of expenses.

 

We are looking for someone with excellent organisational, administrative and communication skills and a keen eye for detail, who can manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced live events environment. Experience in artist management, agency and/or promoter administration would be advantageous, particularly within live music and touring. Flexibility and a willingness to travel and work on site during the summer months, including evenings and weekends, will be required

 

What it’s like to work in the Team

 

Cuffe & Taylor is made up of a diverse group of individuals, but we all share the same passion for putting our employees first. We have a fun atmosphere within the team, which helps us maintain an open, approachable department, and build genuinely authentic and valuable relationships with our employees. We are committed to working as a team and so support each other to achieve wins.

 

Who you are

 

Competencies / Skills / Knowledge / Experience

 

Essential

  • Demonstrable experience of live music or events administration
  • Ability to work efficiently under pressure and tight deadlines
  • A self-starter with excellent organisational and administrative skills
  • Excellent IT skills including Microsoft Office and Adobe
  • Excellent formatting skills
  • Exemplary attention to detail
  • Excellent communication skills

 

Desirable

  • Experience with Monday.com, Jotform, Claude

 

Behaviours

 

The following attributes determine how the role will be carried out and are required to be a success


  • Extremely well organised and self-motivated
  • High level of integrity and discretion
  • Flexibility – ability to respond to constantly shifting priorities
  • Sound judgement and level-headedness
  • Proactive approach to problem solving
  • Effective communicator with the ability to interact with staff across all levels of the organisation

What the role includes


  • Work closely with the Executive Assistant to the Outdoor Promoters and the wider Promoter team to deliver events and festivals in collaboration with the Operations, Ticketing, Marketing, Finance and Customer Service teams
  • Diary management for the Promoter team
  • Keep accurate financial records for all confirmed shows
  • Mark up all agency confirmations and contracts in line with Live Nation guidelines
  • Schedule show announcements and coordinate relevant teams to ensure the best on-sale experience for all involved
  • Work on site at events and festivals, including evenings and weekends, when required
  • Liaise with heads of department across Cuffe & Taylor, the wider Live Nation group and high-profile external stakeholders
  • Manage Promoter guest ticketing and accreditation requests
  • Book travel and hotels throughout the year, as required
  • Handle all requirements for VIP guests of the company across outdoor shows during the summer season
  • Keep all documentation organised and filed correctly
  • Relay invoices to the finance team for payment
  • Book and manage promoter reps and freelancers across festivals and theatre tours.
  • Undertake ad hoc tasks as required

 

Equal Opportunities

 

We are passionate and committed to our people and go beyond the rhetoric of diversity and inclusion. You will be working in an inclusive environment and be encouraged to bring your whole self to work. We will do all that we can to help you successfully balance your work and homelife. As a growing business we will encourage you to develop your professional and personal aspirations, enjoy new experiences, and learn from the talented people you will be working with. It’s talent that matters to us and we encourage applications from people irrespective of their gender identity, race, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability status or caring responsibilities.

 

The Company

 

Cuffe & Taylor is part of Live Nation Entertainment which is the world’s leading live entertainment company comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, LN Media and Artist Nation Management.

job.title: Senior Product Designer, Editorial Technology
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times ranks among the world’s foremost news organisations. It is known globally for its authority, integrity, and accuracy. Its mission is to provide quality information and services across the globe.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, build work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and encourage you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Develop a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our dedication to inclusion and fairness

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our dedication is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are evaluated by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

The role

We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to join our Editorial Technology team, helping build the tools journalists and editors use to compose, manage, and publish world-class journalism.

You’ll build experiences across Spark, our newsroom content management system (CMS), and related editorial tools supporting written stories, video and audio.

This role involves working on intricate products that directly aid journalism production at the FT. Work often starts without a clear brief or defined project. You will need to be comfortable investigating problems, grasping detailed workflows, and helping decide the appropriate course.

Collaborating with product managers, engineers, and newsroom colleagues, you'll merge user research, systems thinking, and strong design skills to develop intuitive, accessible tools for expert users.

You'll also consider how editorial tools interact with the reader experiences they facilitate across our website and apps, partnering with our Customer Products teams as needed.

AI is increasingly crafting editorial workflows, and you'll have chances to explore how new technologies can assist journalists and editors. These include tools that improve editorial quality and accuracy.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead the end-to-end build process, from early problem framing and discovery through information architecture, exploration, prototyping, testing and delivery.
  • Develop a deep understanding of how journalists and editors work, using research, workflow mapping and direct engagement to find opportunities for improvement.
  • Partner with product managers and engineers to build product direction, define problems and establish clear priorities, particularly where requirements are ambiguous.
  • Build intuitive, accessible experiences for complex editorial workflows, including the creation and management of written and multimedia content.
  • Work closely with engineering teams to understand technical architecture, data, systems and constraints, ensuring built solutions are practical and achievable.
  • Build positive relationships with newsroom collaborators, bringing their expertise into the development process while applying sound design judgement.
  • Consider how editorial tools connect with customer-facing experiences, collaborating with Customer Products teams to support consistency and shared development patterns.
  • Communicate build decisions, recommendations and trade-offs clearly, helping teams navigate complexity and make informed decisions.
  • Investigate ways AI can assist editorial workflows, such as quality and accuracy checks, while collaborating closely with editorial, product, and engineering colleagues.
  • Use AI-enabled tools such as Codex or Figma Make, where appropriate, to prototype, test ideas and communicate technical assumptions.
  • Stay informed about developments in AI-assisted build and prototyping, bringing relevant approaches and ideas into the team.

Required skills and experience

  • Strong product development experience across user research, UX, visual design, information architecture and prototyping.
  • A portfolio demonstrating high-quality product development work, your individual contribution and measurable impact.
  • Experience crafting and delivering complex digital products, including internal tools and workflows for expert users.
  • Demonstrated capability to carry projects from initial problem identification through research, prototyping, validation, and final delivery.
  • Strong product and systems thinking, with an ability to understand how interconnected tools, workflows and technologies work together.
  • A thoughtful and analytical approach to problem-solving, with the confidence to challenge assumptions and explore alternative solutions.
  • Experience planning and conducting proportionate user research, combining qualitative and quantitative insights to inform development decisions.
  • Sufficient technical understanding to collaborate effectively with engineers and navigate complex systems, data and technical constraints.
  • Strong Figma and prototyping skills, with practical experience applying accessibility principles.
  • Experience using AI-assisted prototyping or development tools, with the judgement to assess their opportunities and limitations.
  • Excellent communication and collaborator management skills, with the ability to build positive relationships across multidisciplinary teams.
  • Confidence working through ambiguity, crafting requirements and helping teams move towards clear, considered solutions.

Desirable

  • Experience crafting content management systems, editorial platforms or newsroom tools.
  • A grasp of digital publishing workflows, including the creation and management of multimedia content.
  • Experience working on products that connect complex internal systems with customer-facing digital experiences.

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing outstanding perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

We currently operate a hybrid model which requires staff to work onsite 50% of the time, subject to role requirements & regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for all roles. We believe this balanced approach supports flexibility and protects our culture, making collaboration and communication easier, encouraging positive relationships and team cohesion, and supporting peer learning. We reserve discretion on reasonable notice to change this approach either generally or for specific individuals or teams.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please inform us if you need any reasonable adjustments or accommodations during the application process or to assist you in attending an interview. If you wish to talk about your needs or have any queries, email talent@ft.com and someone from our team will gladly assist you.

Further information

At the FT, we value innovation and the adoption of technology and accept that applicants may bring AI tools to bear in their application process. Feel free to use AI to aid your application, but all information you provide must be honest and accurately display your skills, experience, and qualifications.

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI during the application process might be observed to guarantee a fair and transparent hiring experience for everyone.

Please be cautious of fake job postings and offers pretending to come from the Financial Times. All genuine roles require applications through the official Financial Times careers website. The FT will never request financial details, payments, or third-party referrals during recruitment. If you doubt a job's authenticity or suspect a scam, contact talent@ft.com.

Interested in the FT but haven’t found the right position yet? Join our Talent Community to get exclusive updates, highlighted jobs, and insights into working at the FT.

job.title: Data Engineer, Communications Intelligence & Insights
job.description:
Who we are:

Burson, part of WPP, is the global communications leader built to create value for clients through reputation. With highly specialized teams, industry-leading technologies and breakthrough creative, we help brands and businesses redefine reputation as a competitive advantage so they can lead today and into the future. When you work at Burson, you are part of a global community of lifelong learners who thrive at the edge of innovation.

WPP (LSE/NYSE: WPP) is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com 

For more information visit bursonglobal.com and follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

More About the Role

 

Are you interested in building the systems that underpin how modern communications intelligence is measured, analysed and scaled?

Burson’s EMEA Intelligence & Insights Hub is a centralised production and engineering capability responsible for developing the data infrastructure, pipelines and workflows that power monitoring, measurement and reporting across the region. Bringing together engineers and analysts, the Hub builds scalable platforms, integrates multiple external data sources and develops AI-enabled workflows that enhance both the efficiency and quality of intelligence delivery.

As a Data Engineer, you will play a key role in developing, maintaining and optimising the engineering systems that sit at the heart of the Hub’s delivery model. You will work across core platform engineering, client-specific solutions and AI workflow development, helping to evolve The Fount and Burson’s wider Data & Intelligence technology stack.

Our technology ecosystem is built on a modern, highly integrated cloud and relational database architecture. Core data-processing pipelines are developed using object-oriented Python and run through scalable cloud-compute orchestration and enterprise ETL tools. Managed SQL environments provide our relational system of record, while raw and semi-structured assets are maintained within secure cloud object storage.

Advanced language models are integrated directly into our processing pipelines to automate enrichment at scale, with the wider ecosystem managed through GitHub, Azure DevOps and Infrastructure-as-Code.

This is an opportunity for an engineer who enjoys solving complex data challenges while building reliable, scalable and reusable systems that support analysts, client teams and global stakeholders.

 

What you'll do:

 

  • Build, develop and maintain Burson’s core data platform and pipelines, supporting scalable ingestion, transformation, storage and delivery of intelligence data across the EMEA Hub.
  • Design and manage robust ingestion pipelines for media monitoring, social listening, APIs, internal datasets and third-party research and analytics sources.
  • Develop transformation and data-modelling layers using SQL and Python, creating both standardised central data models and bespoke client datasets that support downstream reporting, including Power BI.
  • Design and deliver client-specific data engineering solutions, developing custom pipelines, integrations and datasets where off-the-shelf technology does not meet complex or specialist requirements.
  • Optimise the performance, scalability and reliability of data systems, identifying bottlenecks, resolving data-quality issues and continuously improving pipeline efficiency.
  • Develop reusable engineering frameworks, templates and components that enable the Hub to scale solutions consistently across clients, markets and use cases.
  • Contribute to AI-enabled workflows, embedding language models into data pipelines to automate content analysis, classification, tagging, summarisation, relevance, sentiment and other enrichment processes.
  • Develop and refine prompting frameworks and AI-processing workflows, including monitoring and optimising token usage to ensure effective, efficient and commercially sustainable AI enrichment at scale.
  • Partner with analysts, product teams and communications specialists to translate approved business and reporting requirements into clearly defined technical solutions and identify appropriate opportunities for AI and automation.
  • Work within a structured Agile and ticket-driven engineering environment, contributing to sprint planning, daily stand-ups and technical design discussions while delivering against agreed functional specifications and architectural standards.
  • Maintain strong engineering governance and security standards, including consistent code practices, Git workflows, secure credential management, database security and adherence to agreed directory and repository structures.
  • Own high-quality technical documentation, maintaining clear technical guides, markdown documentation, database schemas and system records while contributing to planned refactoring and technical-debt reduction without disrupting production services.

 

 

Experience that contributes to success:

 

  • Strong experience in data engineering, with a track record of designing, building and maintaining reliable production-grade data pipelines and platforms.
  • Advanced SQL skills and strong experience in relational database environments, including data transformation, modelling, optimisation and the creation of data structures for downstream analytics and reporting.
  • Strong Python development capability, including writing clean, readable and object-oriented code, working with pandas and developing concurrent or scalable data-processing workflows.
  • Hands-on experience with APIs, data integrations and ETL/ELT architectures, with the ability to bring together structured and semi-structured data from multiple sources.
  • Experience working within cloud-based data environments, ideally Microsoft Azure, including cloud compute, managed databases, object storage and enterprise data-processing services.
  • Strong software-engineering discipline, including experience designing and writing automated unit, integration and regression tests in Python, ideally using pytest.
  • A strong understanding of secure engineering practices, including database security, firewalls and secure secrets and credential management using tools such as Azure Key Vault.
  • Experience with Git-based engineering workflows and CI/CD environments, ideally including GitHub and Azure DevOps, with an appreciation for structured branching, code governance and multi-developer environments.
  • Familiarity with Infrastructure-as-Code, ideally Terraform or Terragrunt, and the ability to safely manage or update environment variables, configuration and access controls within established infrastructure frameworks.
  • Experience or strong interest in AI-enabled data engineering, including exposure to large language models, prompt-based workflows, automated enrichment or the integration of AI services into production data pipelines.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting and technical-planning skills, with the ability to diagnose complex data and performance issues, scope engineering work effectively and build scalable solutions rather than short-term fixes.
  • A collaborative and disciplined approach to engineering, comfortable working across multiple projects with analysts, engineers, product teams and business stakeholders while maintaining strong documentation, continuous improvement and adherence to agreed technical standards.

job.title: Associate Account Director (Promotional Medical Education)
job.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. job.title: Company Secretary
job.description:
Opportunity

We are looking for an experienced, fully qualified Company Secretary to join our Finance and Tax team and support Brunswick’s international operations.

This is a senior role at the heart of Brunswick’s governance framework, providing trusted advice to the Board of Directors and senior leadership. The Company Secretary will lead our corporate governance and regulatory compliance activities, ensuring Brunswick maintains high standards of governance and meets its obligations under the UK Corporate Governance Code and Companies Act 2006.

Reporting to the Group Head of Tax and Partnership Affairs, the role will work closely with the Group Financial Controller and other senior colleagues across the firm, providing thoughtful, pragmatic guidance on governance and corporate matters.

We are open to considering part-time or flexible working arrangements for the right candidate.

About the Role

Your key responsibilities will include:

Board and governance

  • Support the effective operation of the Board, including preparing agendas and papers, drafting minutes, tracking actions and ensuring appropriate follow-up.
  • Act as a key point of contact for executive and non-executive directors on governance matters.
  • Manage the forward calendar and terms of reference for the Board and its committees.
  • Ensure the Board operates in accordance with the Articles of Association, shareholder arrangements, the Companies Act 2006 and other relevant governance and regulatory requirements.
  • Keep the Board and senior colleagues informed of relevant developments in corporate governance and regulation.

Committee support

  • Provide company secretarial support to the Audit & Risk Committee.
  • Attend committee meetings and prepare accurate and timely minutes.
  • Track actions and support appropriate follow-up.

Shareholder matters

  • Maintain the shareholder register and oversee quarterly updates presented to the Board.
  • Prepare and coordinate communications and documentation for shareholders.
  • Work with the Head of International Tax to support partners on shareholder and share-related matters.

Annual General Meeting

  • Manage the end-to-end delivery of the Annual General Meeting.
  • Prepare notices and supporting documentation.
  • Coordinate communications with shareholders.
  • Manage meeting arrangements and prepare minutes.

Share buy-backs

  • Coordinate the documentation and approvals associated with share buy-backs.
  • Manage relevant filing and record-keeping requirements.

Corporate documentation and records

  • Draft resolutions, letters and other corporate documentation for entities and transactions across the Group.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date statutory books and corporate records for the Group’s subsidiaries using Diligent.
  • Maintain authorised signatory records.
  • Own and maintain the Group structure chart.

Statutory filings and compliance

  • Manage the Group’s Companies House filings, including confirmation statements and other statutory returns.
  • Ensure filings are completed accurately and on time.
  • Maintain oversight of filing deadlines and other company secretarial obligations across the Group.

Corporate transactions

  • Lead the company secretarial and governance aspects of corporate and commercial transactions.
  • Support matters including entity closures, share conversions and Group restructurings.
  • Work closely with Legal, Finance, Tax and other colleagues to ensure transactions are appropriately documented and implemented.

Advice and stakeholder support

  • Provide thoughtful and pragmatic corporate governance advice to directors, Finance, Legal and other senior stakeholders across the firm.
  • Support in-house Legal colleagues on company secretarial and governance matters.
  • Work with and provide guidance to Executive Assistants on Board governance and administration.

KYC

  • Coordinate KYC requests relating to directors and senior management.
  • Ensure relevant information is accurate, current and provided efficiently.

What We’re Looking For

We are looking for someone who brings:

  • Significant corporate secretarial experience, typically gained over 6–8 years, with experience working in a UK-listed, highly regulated or complex international environment.
  • Strong knowledge of the UK Corporate Governance Code, Listing Rules and Companies Act 2006, combined with the judgement to apply this expertise thoughtfully and pragmatically.
  • Excellent written and analytical skills, with the ability to listen carefully, identify what matters and capture complex Board and executive discussions in clear, accurate and considered minutes.
  • High emotional intelligence and strong interpersonal skills, with the confidence and judgement to build trusted relationships across executive and non-executive leadership while maintaining discretion and impartiality.
  • Fellowship or Associate status with the Chartered Governance Institute (CGI, formerly ICSA) is required.
  • A legal degree or professional qualification as a solicitor would be an advantage.

Why Join Us

Whether you are joining a client facing team, a core services team, or starting out on your professional career journey, joining Brunswick unlocks a range of employee benefits to support your financial future, health and wellness, family and community and continuous professional development.

 

About Brunswick

Brunswick is a global advisory firm. We help companies tackle high-stakes issues, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, and deliver high-impact outcomes. 

Our clients value our ability to anticipate, shape, and respond to the key players and forces in the financial and investment arena, regulatory and geopolitical universe, NGO community, workforce and beyond. They rely on us for deep experience, fresh perspectives and original thinking. So, in Brunswick you will find an exceptional range of experience and talent with a rich mix of backgrounds. From the beginning, we have prioritized attracting, developing, and retaining the best professionals in the industry, united by a culture of inclusivity, excellence, and intellectual curiosity.

Founded in 1987 in London, the firm has organically grown to 27 offices in 18 countries across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia and Australia. We operate as a “one-firm firm” with no individual profit centers. This allows us to assemble fully integrated, bespoke teams for each client, able to draw on the full resources of Brunswick anywhere in the world. 

 

Brunswick is an equal opportunity employer.  All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law. Please read our Global Privacy Notice to understand how your data is managed.

job.title: Global PMO Lead - People Technology 12M FTC
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Why we're hiring:

WPP is delivering a significant People Technology transformation, modernising the platforms, processes and data that underpin how we manage and support our people globally.

We’re looking for an experienced PMO Lead to sit at the centre of this transformation, bringing the structure, discipline and visibility needed to successfully deliver a complex, global programme. This is more than a reporting PMO role. You’ll create the governance, integrated planning and delivery controls that enable leaders to make informed decisions and teams to deliver effectively. You’ll connect multiple workstreams, make risks and dependencies visible, ensure actions translate into delivery, and provide a clear view of whether the programme is achieving its objectives and intended benefits.

Working across the intersection of People, Technology, HR processes, data and organisational change, you’ll partner closely with programme leadership, Workstream Leads and cross-functional teams to turn strategy into an executable plan and create the rhythm and discipline needed to deliver transformation at scale.

What you'll be doing:

  • Own and maintain the integrated programme plan, ensuring milestones, dependencies, deliverables and critical paths are clearly understood and actively managed.
  • Establish and maintain effective programme governance, providing appropriate control over scope, cost, timelines, risks and delivery.
  • Lead programme reporting, providing clear and insightful updates on progress, risks, issues, dependencies, decisions and areas requiring intervention.
  • Own the programme RAID process, proactively identifying risks and issues and ensuring clear mitigation, escalation and resolution plans are in place.
  • Coordinate dependencies across workstreams, ensuring actions have clear owners, deadlines and accountability through to closure.
  • Support and facilitate programme governance forums, ensuring decisions are captured and translated into clear actions and outcomes.
  • Establish and maintain the frameworks, processes, templates and programme documentation required to drive consistency and effective ways of working.
  • Ensure programme benefits are clearly defined, baselined and tracked, with appropriate business ownership and measurable outcomes.
  • Develop meaningful metrics and reporting to monitor programme performance and benefits realisation.
  • Partner with Workstream Leads and delivery teams to identify roadblocks, resolve delivery challenges and maintain momentum.
  • Provide leadership and guidance to project and workstream teams, championing strong programme management disciplines and collaborative ways of working.
  • Work across the wider organisation to identify interdependencies with other transformation initiatives and ensure these are reflected in programme planning.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify processes, improve operational effectiveness and strengthen programme delivery.
  • Champion effective ways of working across globally dispersed and cross-functional teams.
  • Act as Project Manager for selected strategic initiatives or workstreams where additional delivery leadership is required

What you'll need:

  • Significant experience working as a PMO Lead, Senior PMO, Programme Manager or in a similar role within a large-scale transformation environment.
  • Strong programme management capability, with hands-on experience of integrated planning, governance, RAID management, dependency management and executive-level reporting.
  • Experience supporting complex programmes involving multiple workstreams, geographies and cross-functional teams.
  • Experience delivering People Technology, HR transformation or enterprise technology programmes would be highly valuable.
  • Experience working with HRIS/HCM platforms, with an understanding of the processes, data, integrations and business change surrounding enterprise HR technology, is strongly preferred.
  • Workday experience would be advantageous but is not essential. We’re equally interested in candidates with experience of other major enterprise HRIS/HCM platforms who can demonstrate strong technology-enabled transformation experience.
  • Strong understanding of Agile and traditional programme delivery approaches, with the ability to apply an appropriate level of governance depending on the programme environment.
  • Experience developing programme governance, reporting frameworks, delivery standards and ways of working.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to turn complex programme information into clear insights and recommendations for senior stakeholders.
  • Experience establishing and tracking programme benefits, KPIs and delivery metrics.
  • Strong facilitation and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to bring diverse teams together around shared priorities.
  • A practical, action-oriented approach, with strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain control across multiple moving parts.
  • Confidence operating in ambiguity, quickly identifying problems and creating the structure needed to move towards resolution.
  • Experience working with globally dispersed teams through significant organisational or technology transformation.
  • Experience of process improvement approaches such as Lean, Six Sigma or Design Thinking would be advantageous.

Who you are:

You're open: We are inclusive and collaborative; we encourage the free exchange of ideas; we respect and celebrate diverse views. We are open-minded: to new ideas, new partnerships, new ways of working.

You're optimistic: We believe in the power of creativity, technology and talent to create brighter futures or our people, our clients and our communities. We approach all that we do with conviction: to try the new and to seek the unexpected.

You're extraordinary: we are stronger together: through collaboration we achieve the amazing. We are creative leaders and pioneers of our industry; we provide extraordinary every day.

What we'll give you:

Passionate, inspired people – We aim to create a culture in which people can do extraordinary work.

Scale and opportunity – We offer the opportunity to create, influence and complete projects at a scale that is unparalleled in the industry.

Challenging and stimulating work – Unique work and the opportunity to join a group of creative problem solvers. Are you up for the challenge?

#LI-Hybrid #LI-DNP

 

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process.

WPP is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to particular characteristics. We are committed to fostering a culture of respect in which everyone feels they belong and has the same opportunities to progress in their careers.

Please read our Privacy Notice (https://www.wpp.com/en/careers/wpp-privacy-policy-for-recruitment) for more information on how we process the information you provide.
