Our vision is to build a thriving entertainment ecosystem where stories and worlds are imagined, brought to life and experienced. We create for every age and audience, anchored by the strength of our content and experiences and the depth of our connection with fans. We are creator-first, audience-focused, tech-forward, globally scaled.

 

Here, you’ll work with talented teams that move fast, think boldly and collaborate with purpose to deliver results. We aim high, champion the best ideas and win together, earning the trust of our employees, creators, partners and audiences every day.

 

If you’re energized by the opportunity to help build the next-generation global media and entertainment company powered by creativity and technology, we’d be thrilled to welcome you aboard. LET’S GO!

 

Overview:

CBS News 24/7, the network’s flagship national streaming news service, is looking for a seasoned Producer to help shape the editorial vision of our live national newscast. This role is central to upholding our 24/7 commitment — delivering urgent breaking news, high impact storytelling, on the ground reporting, and a transparent look at how the news comes together. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-moving environment and embraces innovative tools that deepen context, clarity, and accuracy for our audience. This position will be covered under the WGAE streaming agreement and is based at the CBS Broadcast Center in New York.  

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Develop, research, write, produce, and edit compelling news segments for a national audience.
  • Collaborate with national assignment editors, reporters, writers, and executive producers while making editorial and content decisions in accordance with CBS guidelines and standards.
  • Lead in the control room with calm, confidence, and adaptability, especially during breaking news and high-pressure moments.
  • Oversee editing, script writing and creation of news graphics.
  • Time programs and segments with a good sense of pacing, power and urgency.
  • Uphold impeccable grammar, spelling, and attention to detail in all content produced while ensuring active, conversational style writing.
  • Exhibit well-developed editorial judgment, effective communication, and critical thinking skills.
 

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of broadcast or cable news experience.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
  • Strong journalism foundation and proven television production background, including news judgment, rundown management, and concise broadcast writing.
  • Prior live control room experience, including serving as a Line Producer.

 

Additional Qualifications:

  • Command of AP style and broadcast writing
  • Familiarity with ENPS
  • Basic video editing skills
  • Sophisticated knowledge of current events, geopolitics and pop culture
  • Ability to multi-task and manage multiple assignments for regular programming as well as rolling breaking news coverage
  • Deep understanding of news standards, rights and clearances and fact-checking practices
  • Ability to work early mornings, nights, weekends and holidays, sometimes on short notice
  • Must pass comprehensive writing test


CBS News and Stations, brings together the power of CBS News, 28 owned television stations in 17 major U.S. markets, the CBS News Streaming Network, CBS News Streaming local platforms, local websites and cbsnews.com, under one umbrella. CBS News and Stations is home to the nation’s #1 news program 60 MINUTES, the CBS News Streaming Network, the first 24/7 digital streaming news network, the award-winning broadcasts CBS MORNINGS, CBS SATURDAY MORNING, the CBS EVENING NEWS, CBS SUNDAY MORNING, CBS WEEKEND EVENING NEWS, 48 HOURS and FACE THE NATION WITH MARGARET BRENNAN. CBS News and Stations provides news and information for the CBS Television Network,  CBSNews.com, CBS News Radio and podcasts, Paramount +, all digital platforms, and the CBS News Streaming Network, the premier 24/7 anchored streaming news service that is available free to everyone with access to the internet. The CBS News Streaming Network is the destination for breaking news, live events, original reporting and storytelling, and programs from CBS News and Stations’ top anchors and correspondents working locally, nationally and around the globe. CBS News’ streaming services, across national and local, amassed more than 1.01 billion streams in 2021. Launched in November 2014 as CBSN, the CBS News Streaming Network is available on 30 digital platforms and apps, as well as CBSNews.com and Paramount+. The service is available live in 91 countries. CBS News and Stations is dedicated to providing the highest quality journalism under standards it pioneered and continues to set in today’s digital age. CBS News earns more prestigious journalism awards than any other broadcast news division.  

 

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

 

Hiring Salary Range: $102,035.00 - 102,035.00. 

 

The hiring salary range for this position applies to New York, California, Colorado, Washington state, and most other geographies. Starting pay for the successful applicant depends on a variety of job-related factors, including but not limited to geographic location, market demands, experience, training, and education.  The benefits available for this position include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) plan, life insurance coverage, disability benefits, tuition assistance program and PTO or, if applicable,  as otherwise dictated by the appropriate Collective Bargaining Agreement.

  • Attractive compensation and comprehensive benefits packages. Check out our full list of benefits here.

  • Robust employee engagement opportunities, including access to exclusive screenings and events, speaker series, volunteer activities and more.

job.description:
About TEGNA

TEGNA Inc. helps people thrive in their local communities by providing the trusted local news and services that matter most. With 64 television stations in 51 U.S. markets, TEGNA reaches more than 100 million people monthly across the web, mobile apps, streaming, and linear television. Together, we are building a sustainable future for local news.

 

KARE 11 is a news leader looking for an experienced, engaging and enterprising journalist to join our team. We’re looking for a passionate storyteller and team player that understands reporting isn’t just covering news conferences and what’s written in the paper. We’re looking for a content leader, strong enterpriser and good newsroom citizen that understands how to connect on all platforms as a Multi-skilled Journalist.
We want someone deeply committed to local news who regularly breaks stories in their market and gets noticed. In addition, they must be an efficient writer and developer of sources and strong story pitches.

Responsibilities:
•    Generate unique, compelling and innovative story/show ideas and content.
•    Develop story ideas, cultivate sources, write, shoot and edit stories for on-air
•    Report live from the field.
•    To be a strong communicator with the ability to react quickly to breaking news in a changing environment.

job.title: Chief Business Editor
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application deadline and instructions :

  • Please complete and submit your application by 11:59 pm EST on Monday, December 7th, 2026
  • Please submit your resume and cover letter. In your cover letter please share your philosophy for leading a Business desk and what you envision the top focus areas should be for the desk in 2027.

Intro to Position

NPR’s Chief Business Editor has overall operational and editorial responsibility for business and economics coverage on all platforms. This editor supervises assignments and provides editorial guidance to a team of business reporters, correspondents and editors across the country. The position also advises NPR shows, including Morning Edition and All Things Considered, and coordinates editorial content closely with the Planet Money podcast team. This includes preparation of material on all platforms, overseeing the editorial integrity and quality of content, monitoring and evaluating staff performance, recommending new hires and providing editorial support to the Executive Editor.  This position will be responsible for a team and report to the Executive Editor.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff is defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.    

Responsibilities

  • Leads NPR’s business coverage through a combination of distinctive stories, daily news, enterprise and scoops
  • Identifies and sharpen areas of coverage across broadcast and digital platforms
  • Supervises assignments and provide editorial guidance to staff, station and freelance reporters, and production staff
  • Works across the newsroom to determine the best approaches to stories, subjects to be discussed and treated, and individuals to be interviewed 
  • Tracks station, freelance and staff submissions and assignments. 
  • Ensures that speculative submissions from stations and freelancers are auditioned to determine suitability for airing. 
  • Regularly has critical discussions about pieces with reporters and editors, and with the Executive Editor, as appropriate.   
  • Makes hiring and salary recommendations for staff members under his or her supervision, in consultation with the Executive Editor. 
  • Responsible for preparing performance reviews for assigned staff members. 
  • Assists in planning and monitoring the business unit’s annual budgets and in monitoring current spending. 
  • Coordinates business unit staff schedules, submits and approves time sheets and maintains other personnel records as needed. 
  • Responsible for tracking overtime and travel expenditures.
  • Ensures that all material aired and published meets the highest journalistic standards and practices, including standards of accuracy, fairness and probity. 

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • A minimum of 15 years’ experience as a news reporter or editor, including demonstrated experience covering business and economics
  • Demonstrated experience overseeing editorial output for social media and digital platforms
  • Demonstrated collaborative approach to newsgathering and story presentation across platforms
  • Considerable skill in both news and feature editing

Preferred Qualifications

  • Broadcast and specifically radio news experience
  • Familiarity with the NPR member station network

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Previous managerial experience

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and work experience 

Work Location & Requirements

  • Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. Some aspects of this role require duties better performed at an NPR facility. The employee will be required to be in the office at the Washington, D.C., New York City, or Culver City location at least 3 days a week.

Job Type

  • This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S.-based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $190,000-215,000 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees. 

Does this sound like you? If so, we want to hear from you.

job.title: Director, Podcast Partnerships
job.description:
Who We Are

The Vox Media Podcast Network is one of the largest U.S. podcast publishers, home to some of the most popular and influential shows. Reaching a monthly audience of tens of millions across audio, video, and social platforms, our podcasts spark conversations and shape culture, covering everything from politics, technology, and business to food, lifestyle, sports, entertainment, and more. The Vox Media Podcast Network is powered by thought leaders in modern media, and home to a prestigious portfolio of voices from New York Magazine, Vox.com, and The Bulwark. Learn more at podcasts.voxmedia.com.

 

As a Director of Podcast Partnerships, you will be an important revenue contributor responsible for expanding high-value agency and client direct relationships and driving new business growth across the Vox Media Podcast Network. You will serve as a trusted strategic partner to brand and growth marketers and agencies, delivering innovative podcast and talent solutions that connect brands with highly engaged, intellectually curious communities at scale.

Leveraging Vox Media's premium podcast network — including leading shows and high profile talent across technology, business, sports, science, and culture — high-value audiences, and unique scale, you will build partnerships that drive measurable business outcomes. This role demands a consultative mindset, strong relationship-building skills, the ability to influence across all levels of marketing organizations, a passion for podcasts and talent, and a relentless drive to grow revenue in a fast-paced, ambitious environment.

What You'll Do

Lead Strategic Growth: Develop and execute a long-term revenue strategy to expand business with existing and new direct-response clients across the Vox Media Podcast Network.  This role will focus on both upfront deal expansion and 360 campaign partnerships, integrating performance and growth marketers across audio, video and social platforms.

Cultivate Executive-Level Relationships: Build and deepen relationships with key decision-makers at agencies and pertinent client side partners - VPs of Marketing, Heads of Brand & Growth Marketing - positioning Vox Media as a go-to strategic partner for podcast and talent investment.

Proactive Market Engagement: Identify industry trends, evolving buyer behaviors, and client challenges within the performance marketing sector, proactively delivering cross-platform podcast and talent solutions before RFPs are issued.

Consultative Sales Leadership: Translate client objectives into high-impact campaigns using Vox Media podcasts, host talent, video, social and live event capabilities.

Build & Develop Key Relationships:  Bring a deep understanding of the structure, hierarchy, and strategy of the major performance agencies in order to unlock increased investment, new strategic partners, and a diversified buying approach.

Revenue Accountability: Own forecasting, pipeline development, and quarterly and annual sales targets, with full accountability for results and strategic account planning.

Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate closely with editorial, marketing, creative, production and operations teams to deliver custom, culturally resonant proposals that reflect how performance brands communicate with their audiences.

Brand Advocacy: Represent the Vox Media Podcast Network at key industry events and client forums to expand our presence and thought leadership within the performance marketing  ecosystem.

Who You Are

Proven Media Seller: 7+ years of digital media and/or podcast & talent sales experience with a demonstrated track record of success in direct-response and growth marketing space. This is a NYC based role with potential for additional national travel responsibilities.

Strategic Dealmaker: Skilled in complex, consultative sales to marketing executives and agency leadership, with experience securing large-scale, integrated partnerships.

Podcast & Talent Native: Deep familiarity with the podcast and talent advertising landscape — editorial and talent integrations, multi-platform partnerships, scaled podcast buys — and a genuine passion for the medium.

Visionary & Entrepreneurial: A self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth environment, with the ability to anticipate market shifts and client needs before they surface.

Influential Communicator: Exceptional presentation, negotiation, and storytelling skills, with the ability to inspire and persuade at the highest levels of a client organization. Ability to think critically, connect advertiser needs to the right show and talent and communicate the value proposition with clarity and confidence.

Data-Informed Strategist: Comfortable leveraging performance data, audience insights, and category trends to craft compelling, measurable solutions that justify and grow podcast and talent investment.

In this role, you are not just selling media — you are shaping how performance brands connect with audiences through premium audio and video content, trusted voices, and unique scale. As a Director of Podcast Partnerships, your ability to see around corners, anticipate client needs, and deliver category-defining ideas will directly influence Vox Media's position as a leading force in the podcast and talent space!

Where You’ll Work

This job is located in New York City and requires in-office presence Tuesday through Thursday, with additional in-person expectations for client and agency meetings in and outside of NYC.

 

Compensation

This role is compensated on both a base and bonus structure. The compensation listed below reflects only the base salary. 

 

PAY TRANSPARENCY

The salary range listed below represents the minimum and maximum base pay for this position at the time of this posting. Final salary offered to the candidate selected for the position will be based on factors including but not limited to the candidate's skills and experience.

Pay Range$120,000—$125,000 USD

Vox Media is committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can show up as their authentic selves and create their best work. We recognize that great stories, platforms, products and services come from people with all manner of backgrounds and experiences. We recognize that our commitments require ongoing work and sustained attention, as well as adaptation to new insights and best practices.

We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations as part of the application process to candidates with disabilities. If you require a reasonable accommodation as part of the application process, please contact our recruiting team (recruitment@voxmedia.com).

WHAT COMES NEXT

job.title: Associate Director, Creative Membership
job.description:
About ASCAP

The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers (ASCAP) is a membership association of more than one million songwriters, composers and music publishers, and represents some of the world’s most talented music creators. Founded and governed by songwriters, composers and publishers, it is the only performing rights organization in the U.S. that operates on a not-for-profit basis. ASCAP licenses a repertory of over 20 million musical works to hundreds of thousands of businesses that use music, including streaming services, cable television, radio and satellite radio and brick and mortar businesses such as retail stores, hotels, clubs, restaurants and bars. ASCAP collects the licensing fees; identifies, matches and processes trillions of performances every year; and returns nearly 90 cents of every dollar back to its members as royalties. The ASCAP blanket license offers an efficient solution for businesses to legally perform ASCAP music while respecting the right of songwriters and composers to be paid fairly. ASCAP puts music creators first, advocating for their rights and the value of music on Capitol Hill, driving innovation that moves the industry forward, building community and providing the resources and support that creators need to succeed in their careers. Learn more and stay in touch at www.ascap.com, on X and Instagram @ASCAP and on Facebook.

# # #

Job overview:

The Associate Director, Creative Membership leverages deep music industry knowledge to cultivate and maintain strong relationships within the London and European creative community and its surrounding areas. In this role, you will serve as a vital bridge to songwriters, publishers, major record labels, entertainment lawyers, managers, and talent agents. A primary emphasis is placed on enhancing ASCAP's local presence through active on-the-ground engagement, which includes attending live shows, hosting industry mixers, and conducting in-person meetings with ASCAP members and local executives.

This position is based in our London office and will report to the VP, Creative Membership located in London. This position currently is subject to ASCAP’s in office policy.

Areas of Responsibility & Accountability:

  • Discovery and development of talent, including songwriters, composers and producers, in the London, European, and surrounding area
  • Perform market research and partner closely with the London Creative Team to identify, attract, recruit and successfully transition local up-and-coming creators to ASCAP, in order to grow the value of the ASCAP repertory.
  • Support and maintain relationships within the London, Europe, and surrounding creative community, including songwriters, composers, publishers, major record labels, entertainment lawyers, managers, and agents.
  • Develop an understanding of ASCAP’s Survey and Distribution System and ASCAP membership policies and procedures, to confidently guide members through membership and distribution related inquiries.
  • Stay informed of, escalating and making viable recommendations to the relevant internal subject matter experts on effectively addressing member needs.
  • Partner with and support the London Creative Membership Team, as well as the Marketing & Communications team, to plan, curate, and host high-impact member events and recognition initiatives.
  • Act as a brand ambassador of ASCAP by attending industry panels, conferences and events.
  • Collaborate seamlessly across the ASCAP Creative Membership team to share best practices, align regional goals, and unify strategies.
  • Other duties and special projects as assigned

Qualifications & Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree required in Music Business, Business Administration, Communications, Marketing, or a related field required.
  • 5+ years of experience in the Music Industry.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently, navigate ambiguous environments, and communicate with ASCAP leadership.
  • Excellent interpersonal and relationship building skills with the ability to represent ASCAP with poise and professionalism across diverse creator and executive groups.
  • Exceptional judgment.
  • Knowledge of and enthusiasm for the London and European music industry.
  • Ability to juggle priorities and be a team player.
  • Market research skills.
  • Will be required to travel and attend events, including ASCAP’s membership events, outside of office hours and/or overnight.
  • This position requires the incumbent to be in the office 3 days per week.

Occasional travel for in-person meetings may be required.

Please be aware that ASCAP is not a nut-free or other allergen-free workplace.

ASCAP is an equal opportunity employer. All ASCAP employment decisions are made on the basis of individual qualifications and performance and not on the basis of race, national origin, ethnicity, sex, age, marital status, sexual orientation or preference, gender identity, genetic information, disability, handicap, color, creed, religion, veteran status, or any characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

job.title: Spring Intern, Programming Operations - Part Time
job.description:
Who We Are:
SiriusXM and its brands (Pandora,SiriusXM Media, AdsWizz, Simplecast, and SiriusXM Connect) are leading a new era of audio entertainment and services by delivering the most compelling subscription and ad-supported audio entertainment experience for listeners -- in the car, at home, and anywhere on the go with connected devices. Our vision is to shape the future of audio, where everyone can be effortlessly connected to the voices, stories and music they love wherever they are.
This is the place where a diverse group of emerging talent and legends alike come to share authentic and purposeful songs, stories, sounds and insights through some of the best programming and technology in the world. Our critically-acclaimed, industry-leading audio entertainment encompasses music, sports, comedy, news, talk, live events, and podcasting. No matter their individual role, each of our employees plays a vital part in bringing SiriusXM’s vision to life every day.
SiriusXM:
SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, and the premier programmer and platform for subscription and digital advertising-supported audio products. SiriusXM’s platforms collectively reach approximately 150 million listeners, the largest digital audio audience across paid and free tiers in North America, and deliver music, sports, talk, news, comedy, entertainment, and podcasts. Pandora, a subsidiary of SiriusXM, is the largest ad-supported audio entertainment streaming service in the U.S. SiriusXM's subsidiaries Stitcher, Simplecast and AdsWizz make it a leader in podcast hosting, production, distribution, analytics, and monetization. The Company’s advertising sales organization, which operates as SXM Media, leverages its scale, cross-platform sales organization, and ad tech capabilities to deliver results for audio creators and advertisers. SiriusXM, through Sirius XM Canada Holdings, Inc., also offers satellite radio and audio entertainment in Canada. In addition to its audio entertainment businesses, SiriusXM offers connected vehicle services to automakers.
How you’ll make an impact:
As a Programming Operations Intern, you’ll gain hands-on experience supporting SiriusXM’s talk programming channels while working at the intersection of programming, production, and operations. You’ll collaborate with cross-functional teams, build technical and operational skills, and gain exposure to the people and processes that power SiriusXM’s industry-leading content.
What you’ll do:
-Learn and assist with daily operations for a live radio show.
-Participate in on-air content.
-Run sound board for live show or pre-taped interviews.
-Create content including promos and audiograms for Facebook, Instagram and X.
-Record and edit audio in pre- and post-production for on-air use or to be used on social media.
-Prepare for shows with in-depth research in current events, news and politics by participating in talent and production meetings.
-Assist in tracking and monitoring upcoming broadcast events across the business, including high-profile content
-Support cross-checking of Programming and Broadcast grids to ensure fulfillment, OnDemand setup, and metadata accuracy
-Work in a fast-paced, live environment with active deadlines.
-Interact with listeners through social media, email and on-air phone call screening.
-Conduct outreach to industry professionals, public relations and expert guests.
-Keep detailed logs of shows for producer’s records.
-Perform other duties as required.
What you’ll need:
-Internships are open to current students enrolled at a university (those graduating by January 2028 are preferred) and recent graduates who graduated within the 12-month period prior to the start of the internship as well as broadcasting schools with one-year programs that provide certificates of completion.
-Current or previous enrollment in communications classes preferred.
-Broadcast communications and related majors preferred.
-Experience in radio/TV a plus.
-Experience with digital media systems (Photoshop, Adobe, video editing) a plus.
-Knowledge of Broadcast Automation/On-Air software, a plus.
-Experience with digital editing software (Pro Tools, Adobe Audition), preferred.
-Thorough knowledge of MS-Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access).
-Good project management and planning skills.
-Good personnel management skills.
-Interpersonal skills and ability to interact and work with staff at all levels.

job.title: Sales Director, Luxury
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Job Description

The New York Times' Advertising team is looking for a Sales Director to join our Luxury Sales Team. Sales Directors use existing relationships and establish new ones across agency and client groups to secure advertising investment and ensure success of campaigns. You will tailor and pivot the NYT pitch and solution based on advertisers' needs and goals. Through a consultative approach, you will pitch to clients our full New York Times portfolio, which includes The Athletic, NYT Cooking, Wirecutter, NYT News, Games, Audio, and more.

About the Role

Your primary goal is to grow and diversify the advertising revenue from a slate of enterprise accounts. You are a team player and contribute to the goals and success of The NYT's Advertising Department, and our mission. You will be external-facing, meeting with clients in person frequently, and travel for client meetings will be necessary. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Head of Category. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Oversee and grow a portfolio of luxury clients and agency relationships, building influence with senior decision-makers and expanding partnership depth over time.
  • Lead account strategy and execution, with full accountability for revenue delivery against annual goals.
  • Identify, and close complex advertising opportunities, independently leading deal strategy while engaging internal partners.
  • Be the primary client-facing leader on assigned accounts, delivering presentations and advancing ideas that inspire both client value and revenue growth.
  • Partner across internal teams to develop high-quality proposals, bring new concepts to market, and ensure client outcomes.
  • Manage a disciplined pipeline and accurate forecasting through Salesforce; communicate performance and insights to leadership.
  • Represent The New York Times externally as a trusted partner and category expert; travel as needs require.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

job.title: Senior Producer, Shows
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is developing a video show that aims to transform the journalism our newsroom does every day for a new audience. We are seeking an experienced producer to lead the day-to-day editorial and production work of the show, while helping the team develop and refine formats that serve our journalism and audiences.

You will work closely with reporters, editors, hosts and production colleagues to shape stories from idea through publication. You will set a high bar for accuracy, storytelling and craft; help the team experiment with new approaches to video; and ensure the show’s formats can evolve as we learn what resonates. This is a hands-on role for someone who combines strong news judgment and production instincts with the ability to guide a team and bring ambitious ideas to life.

This is an in-office position based in New York City, with regular attendance four days a week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the editorial and production process for a video show, from story selection and development through filming, editing and publication.
  • Work with Shows leadership, reporters and editors to shape coverage, identify strong stories and translate newsroom journalism into compelling video.
  • Help develop, test and refine formats and visual approaches, balancing creative experimentation with consistent execution.
  • Manage a team of producers 
  • Guide producers, editors, hosts and other collaborators on story structure, scripts, visuals and overall episode craft.
  • Manage production schedules and an editorial calendar, balancing breaking news and immediate priorities with planned stories and longer-term development.
  • Review work for accuracy, clarity and quality; give timely editorial feedback and coach team members in their development.
  • Coordinate with audience, programming and social teams to support distribution and reach audiences across platforms.
  • Contribute to staffing and freelance needs as the show’s production evolves.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Director of Development

  • 10+ years of experience producing or editing journalism for video, audio or digital platforms.
  • 3+ years of experience managing or leading a production team.
  • Strong news judgment and a track record of shaping accurate, engaging journalism for digital audiences.
  • Extensive experience with daily news. Live production a plus. 
  • Experience taking stories from idea through production and publication, with the ability to guide both editorial and craft decisions.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast-paced newsroom.
  • Strong collaboration, communication and feedback skills, and a commitment to fostering an inclusive and supportive team environment.
  • Understanding of social platforms and how audiences discover and engage with video journalism.

Preferred Experience:

  • Experience developing or evolving a video series, show format or recurring editorial product.
  • Experience producing breaking news, features and enterprise journalism for video.

  • Experience working with hosts, reporters, editors and production teams to shape stories for video.

job.description:

Why it matters: Reporting to our News Editor, the news writer-editor will play a critical role as part of the 24/7 nerve center for the newsroom.

  • We are after people with a “see it, write it” mentality who have a personal passion for news and a fast-twitch set of journalistic reflexes.
  • This is a job for the news junkies who “monitor the situation” for fun and want to do it for a living. 
  • We operate at one cadence - do it right now - and are after people who marry a love of news with the thrill of being busy.  
  • This is the ultimate “safe pair of hands” job — someone we can trust to both edit the work of others and write their own, too. 

Go deeper: The role comes with a range of responsibilities, including:

  • Real-time news surveillance
  • Quick-turn writing of spot news stories
  • Editing a wide variety of national news, from breaking stories across the national file to the occasional enterprise.
  • Monitoring developments on key stories and flagging them to experts

Worthy of your time: Ideal candidates will have a get-stuff-done attitude, a strong sense of personal responsibility and urgency, and a passion for being on top of the news at all times. Some of the skills include:

  • Strong interpersonal skills to collaborate with a team of journalists.
  • Writing and editing experience in a fast-paced news environment.
  • Demonstrated experience monitoring and activating on news.

job.title: Business Director
job.description:
Who We Are

We are an award-winning independent creative solutions company that aspires to be the most culturally-influential company in the world. We help ambitious brands harness the power of culture to solve their biggest challenges. As a unique mix of experts in culture, technology, and storytelling, we are united by a passion to grow brands in ways that advertising alone can never do.

We are an entrepreneurial business, not a traditional “ad agency.” That means we value resourcefulness and tenacity just as much as we value creativity and intelligence. We’re unapologetically ambitious!

We are looking for a Business Director to join Translation and help lead our growing Eli Lilly partnership, bringing culturally relevant creative work to life for brands that impact people’s health.

This role is based in Brooklyn, NY, with four days in office and one remote.

Position Summary

As a Business Director, you will serve as a strategic leader and trusted client partner across assigned Eli Lilly brands and workstreams. You will build a deep understanding of the client’s business, patient audiences, and category, translating those insights into clear direction and creative opportunities that connect brands with people in meaningful ways.

Working with the account’s Executive Director, you will lead client relationships, guide cross-functional teams, develop Business Leadership talent, and identify opportunities for growth. You will partner closely with Program Management on delivery and account financial health, balancing creative ambition with the rigor of a regulated category and the needs of a fast-growing business.

What You Will Do

Drive Business and Strategic Leadership

  • Act as the day-to-day senior business lead across assigned Lilly brands and workstreams, building trusted relationships with mid-to-senior client stakeholders and proactively shaping the business agenda.
  • Develop a strong understanding of brand priorities, patient experiences, barriers to engagement, and competitive dynamics to inform strategic counsel and creative development.
  • Translate complex client needs and feedback into clear priorities and actionable direction, constructively challenging clients when needed to strengthen the work.
  • Monitor relationship health and business performance, anticipating risks and partnering with the Executive Director to address issues before they affect the partnership.

Lead Creative Solutions with Business Impact

  • Partner with Strategy, Context, Creative, and Analytics to develop culturally relevant work grounded in business objectives, audience insights, and clear measures of success.
  • Champion communication that reflects real patient experiences and makes complex health topics understandable, empathetic, and relevant to everyday life.
  • Ensure work is strategically sound and client-ready, with compelling rationale and alignment to client-provided medical, legal, and regulatory guidance.
  • Work with Lilly’s brand teams, internal creative team, and agency partners to clarify roles, align recommendations, and maintain continuity across the work.
  • Partner with Production and Program Management to bring approved concepts to life within agreed scope, timing, and budget, advocating for additional investment when warranted.

Lead Teams and Strengthen Partnerships

  • Guide cross-functional teams with clear priorities, expectations, and decisions, creating a collaborative environment with shared accountability for the work.
  • Lead, coach, and develop Business Supervisors and other assigned Business Leadership team members through regular feedback and meaningful development opportunities.
  • Partner with Program Management, which leads operational planning and delivery, to align client expectations with scopes, schedules, staffing, and review requirements.
  • Work with client stakeholders and Program Management to anticipate approval needs, consolidate feedback, and help teams understand review decisions and their implications.
  • Navigate competing stakeholder needs and resolve day-to-day challenges independently, escalating significant relationship, commercial, or delivery risks appropriately.

Champion Growth and Financial Health

  • Develop and action growth plans for assigned brands and workstreams, connecting unmet client needs with Translation’s capabilities.
  • Co-own account financial health with Program Management, contributing to scope development, staffing recommendations, forecasting, and profitability management.
  • Identify scope changes and investment needs early, leading clear client conversations about the associated fees, priorities, and trade-offs.
  • Contribute to new business, recruiting, and departmental improvements that strengthen the agency and develop future Business Leadership talent.

Knowledge Skills and Abilities

  • Strong business judgment and strategic fluency, with the ability to learn complex categories and turn ambiguity into clear direction.
  • Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, including the confidence to advise clients, explain creative rationale, and navigate sensitive conversations.
  • Ability to balance creative ambition with accuracy and client review requirements, partnering effectively with medical, legal, and regulatory stakeholders.
  • Experience leading integrated campaigns across channels, with a strong understanding of creative development and production.
  • Commercial acumen across scopes, staffing, budgets, and account performance, paired with a collaborative approach to Program Management.
  • A proactive, hands-on leadership style, with sound prioritization, attention to detail, and the ability to develop others in a fast-moving environment.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 7-10 years of experience in an agency or communications-related industry, with a well-rounded understanding of advertising, marketing, media, creative, production, and agency finance.
  • Proven success managing integrated campaigns, partnering with mid-to-senior-level clients, and leading cross-functional teams.
  • Hands-on production experience with large-scale, multi-channel initiatives.
  • Experience coaching junior account team members and contributing to scope development, account financial management, and organic growth.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting pharmaceutical, healthcare, or other regulated brands, including familiarity with medical, legal, and regulatory review processes. Direct pharma experience is a plus, not a requirement; curiosity about the category and an eagerness to learn are valued.
  • Experience with consumer-facing health communications, patient storytelling, or brand launches.
  • Experience partnering with in-house creative teams and working within a multi-agency environment.
  • Experience developing culturally relevant campaigns, including talent partnerships, social content, or experiential work.
  • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, or a related field.

AXS connects fans with the artists and teams they love. Each year we sell millions of tickets to thousands of incredible events – from concerts and festivals to sports and theater – at some of the most iconic venues in the world. Since our founding in 2011, we’ve consistently pushed the industry forward and improved experiences for fans, making it easier than ever to discover events, find the perfect seats, and enjoy unforgettable live entertainment, and we continue to lead the evolution of our industry today.

We’re passionate about improving the fan experience and providing game-changing solutions for our clients, and we’re always looking for smart, motivated people to help make it happen. Bring your enthusiasm, your big ideas, and your desire to team up with some of the best and brightest in technology and entertainment.  

The Role

You will lead full-stack work across user interfaces, back-end services, APIs, and integrations. The role combines hands-on development with technical leadership, architecture, and team guidance in a complex enterprise environment. You’ll own initiatives end-to-end on front-end and back-end, drive technical direction, and partner with Product, Design, and engineering to ship secure, scalable software for high-demand, global use cases.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Design, build, and maintain front-end and back-end features for web applications.
  • Lead full-stack architecture and design reviews; author or review technical design as needed.

  • Support agile delivery: planning, estimation, backlog breakdown, risk and blocker management.
  • Champion testing, CI/CD, observability, and operational practices for apps and services.

  • 7+ years of professional software development experience, including technical leadership.
  • Strong front-end experience: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript; frameworks such as React or Next.js; modern UI architecture, accessibility, and responsive design.
  • Strong back-end experience: Java or C# and .NET Core; building APIs, services, and business logic that power web applications.

  • Experience optimizing UI performance and service performance/reliability.

Job Summary

The Privacy Analyst supports AEG’s privacy program by analyzing business activities, systems, products, and proposed uses or disclosures of personal information under applicable privacy laws and regulations. The role gathers and evaluates relevant facts, identifies privacy requirements and risks, and translates that analysis into clear, practical actions for business stakeholders. Responsibilities include conducting privacy impact assessments, supporting data mapping and records of processing, preparing data-sharing arrangements, drafting guidelines and recommendations, supporting consumer-rights compliance, and maintaining accurate privacy-program documentation. The Privacy Analyst partners with Legal, Information Security, Marketing, Global Partnerships, Human Resources, IT, and other business teams and escalates novel or material legal questions as appropriate.

Essential Functions

  • Analyze proposed and existing business activities involving personal information, including products, services, marketing initiatives, employee processes, technologies, vendors, and data-sharing arrangements. Gather relevant facts, identify applicable privacy requirements, assess risks and gaps, document conclusions, and recommend practical actions or escalation.
  • Conduct and document privacy impact, risk, AI and other required assessments under applicable laws. Evaluate issues such as notice, purpose limitation, data minimization, retention, sensitive personal information, consumer rights, targeted advertising, sale or sharing, automated decision-making, AI-enabled processing, profiling, algorithmic decision-making, and contractual requirements.
  • Develop and maintain accurate data maps and inventories by documenting categories of personal information, data subjects, collection sources, business purposes, systems, recipients, disclosures, retention periods, and relevant data flows. Analyze gaps and inconsistencies and work with stakeholders to determine practical solutions.
  • Assess proposed disclosures and transfers of personal information to affiliates, service providers, contractors, and other third parties. Determine whether a data processing, data sharing, confidentiality, or other agreement is required; identify necessary privacy terms and restrictions; document recommendations; and coordinate review or escalation with Legal.
  • Draft and maintain privacy guidelines, assessment templates, standard operating procedures, and playbooks that convert legal and policy requirements into repeatable business practices.
  • Analyze and support data subject requests involving access, deletion, correction, opt-out, limitation, and appeal rights under applicable laws; identify relevant systems and data owners; document exceptions and response decisions.
  • Monitor developments in privacy laws, regulations, enforcement actions, and regulatory guidance; assess their effect on existing business practices, and propose updates to policies, processes, notices, agreements, and training materials.

 

Required Qualifications

  • 2-4 years’ experience in information technology or data privacy and AI governance management, including supporting e-commerce or CRM-focused initiatives.
  • Experience with SaaS privacy platforms such as OneTrust, Ketch, Osano, TrustArc etc.
  • Experience supporting compliance initiatives under North America, APAC, Europe, and LatAm privacy laws.
  • Demonstrated understanding of current data protection and privacy legislation in the United States (must), APAC, Europe, and LatAm (plus).
  • Understanding the role privacy has in supporting business enablement and employee privacy in a global enterprise.  
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong troubleshooting and analytics skills.
  • Detail-oriented and highly motivated.
  • Ability to identify and solve problems quickly.
  • Ability to nurture relationships across large and complex organizations.
  • Comfortable working both independently and in a team setting, in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience in the use of Generative AI tools such as Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, etc.
  • Proficiency in the Microsoft Office 365 suite (Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, etc.)

Job Summary:

JOB DESCRIPTION – DEPOT ENGINEER

Division: Ticketmaster US

Line Manager: VP of Operational Services

Contract Terms: Full Time - ON SITE


THE TEAM

The Enterprise Support Technology Services team is part of the Global Support & Operations organization and is responsible for the deployment, management, and support of hardware and software used across client venues and live events. This includes asset lifecycle management, configuration, and logistics to ensure systems operate reliably in both event and day-to-day environments.

The team partners closely with Technology, Event Operations, and Account teams to support client needs and deliver consistent, high-quality execution. As part of a rapidly evolving live entertainment landscape, the team continuously improves processes, adapts to new technologies, and scales operations to meet growing demand.

THE JOB

The Depot Engineer is responsible for executing day-to-day depot operations, including hardware configuration, logistics, repair, and asset management. This role ensures that all equipment is properly prepared, tracked, and deployed to support live events and client operations.

You will operate as a key contributor within the depot, owning critical workflows across the hardware lifecycle—from receiving and configuration to deployment and return. This role requires strong technical aptitude, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced, agile, event-driven environment.

The Depot Engineer partners closely with internal teams across Technology, Event Operations, and Account Management to ensure hardware is delivered accurately and on time. You will also play an active role in identifying inefficiencies and improving processes to increase reliability, scalability, and operational efficiency.

In addition to execution, you are expected to anticipate operational needs—proactively identifying risks, planning for upcoming demand, and ensuring the depot is prepared to support future events and deployments.

Success in this role means consistently delivering high-quality execution, resolving technical issues effectively, and contributing to the continuous improvement of depot operations.


WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING

  • Configure, stage, test, and deploy hardware for both permanent and temporary installations
  • Manage day-to-day shipping and receiving operations, including tracking and coordinating equipment movement
  • Maintain accurate inventory and asset tracking across systems, ensuring data integrity and visibility
  • Troubleshoot and repair hardware issues across supported devices (POS, networking equipment, peripherals, mobile devices, printers)
  • Execute hardware replacement and refurbishment workflows to maintain deployment readiness
  • Ensure all equipment meets quality standards and is fully prepared prior to deployment
  • Monitor inventory levels and proactively flag risks related to shortages, delays, or upcoming demand
  • Partner with internal teams to support event timelines, client needs, and deployment schedules
  • Communicate status, issues, and risks clearly to stakeholders
  • Follow established operational processes while proactively identifying opportunities for improvement
  • Contribute to the development and refinement of workflows related to configuration, logistics, and asset management
  • Support vendor interactions related to shipping, repairs, and equipment handling as needed
  • Maintain working knowledge of Ticketmaster and company-supported hardware, systems, cyber security requirements and technologies, including emerging platforms and operational tooling across depot and fulfillment workflow.

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW (TECHNICAL SKILLS)

  • 3–6 years of experience in IT support, technical operations, hardware deployment, or logistics environments
  • Hands-on experience configuring, troubleshooting, and supporting hardware (POS systems, peripherals, mobile devices, or similar)
  • Working knowledge of Windows, macOS, and mobile operating systems
  • Basic understanding of networking concepts (wired and wireless, routers, switches, connectivity troubleshooting)
  • Experience with inventory, asset management, or ticketing systems
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize effectively, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to diagnose issues and drive resolution independently
  • Clear communication skills, with the ability to work across technical and non-technical teams
  • Comfortable working in a hands-on environment that includes both technical tasks and physical operations (equipment handling, shipping/receiving)
  • Ability to anticipate needs, plan ahead, and adapt to changing priorities in an event-driven environment
  • Flexibility to support nights, weekends, or holidays based on event schedules
  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in warehouse or depot environments
  • Forklift certification or experience operating material handling equipment
  • Experience supporting live events or field deployments

YOU (BEHAVIOURAL SKILLS)

  • Strong sense of ownership and accountability—follows through on tasks and sees issues through to resolution
  • Detail-oriented and highly organized, with the ability to maintain accuracy in fast-paced operational workflows
  • Effective communicator who can clearly share status, issues, and risks with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Collaborative team player, able to work across functions and support shared goals
  • Proactive mindset with the ability to identify problems early and take action
  • Adaptable and comfortable working in a dynamic, event-driven environment with shifting priorities
  • Ability to take direction, prioritize accordingly, and adjust quickly as operational needs evolve
  • Reliable and consistent, especially during high-pressure or time-sensitive situations
  • Positive, solutions-oriented approach to challenges

BENEFITS & PERKS

Through our ‘Taking Care of Our Own’ program, we provide benefits across six key pillars:


  • HEALTH: Medical, vision, dental and mental health benefits for you and your family, with access to a health care concierge, and Flexible or Health Savings Accounts (FSA or HSA)
  • YOURSELF: Free concert tickets, generous paid time off including paid holidays, sick time, and personal days
  • WEALTH: 401(k) program with company match, stock reimbursement program
  • FAMILY: New parent programs including caregiver leave, plus fertility, adoption, foster, or surrogacy support
  • CAREER: Career and skill development programs with School of Live, tuition reimbursement, and student loan repayment
  • OTHERS: Volunteer time off, crowdfunding match

 

LIFE AT TICKETMASTER

We are proud to be a part of Live Nation Entertainment, the world’s largest live entertainment company.

Our mission at Ticketmaster is to connect people around the world to the live events they love. Ticketmaster is the world’s largest ticket marketplace and the global market leader in live event ticketing products and services. Through official partnerships with thousands of venues, artists, sports teams, festivals, performing arts centers and theaters, Ticketmaster processes 550 million tickets per year across 35+ different countries.

We do it all with an intense passion for Live and an inspiring and diverse culture driven by accessible leaders, attentive managers, and enthusiastic teams. If you’re passionate about live entertainment like we are, and you want to work at a company dedicated to helping millions of fans experience it, we want to hear from you.

 

Our work is guided by our values:

 

Reliability - Fans and clients count on us to power their live event experiences and we rely on each other to make it happen.

Teamwork – While we celebrate individual achievements, we know have more success as a team.

Integrity - We are committed to the highest moral and ethical standards on behalf of the countless partners and stakeholders we represent.

Belonging - We are committed to building a culture in which all people can be their authentic selves, have an equal voice and opportunities to thrive.

Title: Deputy Managing Editor

Schedule Format - Location:Hybrid - San Francisco

Pay Information: $129,776 - $162,220 Annually



A Deputy Managing Editor at KQED’s primary responsibility is to direct strategy and management of senior editors and reporters on beats across the newsroom, as well as to generate story ideas and execute edits with members of the newsroom. A deputy managing editor at KQED works closely with managing editors to set editorial priorities on coverage across our platforms. A deputy managing editor assists managing editors in shaping coverage, and often manages and directs editors, reporters and producers throughout the newsroom. 

Deputy managing editors work closely with managing editors to work as part of our newsroom leadership to take our editorial priorities and help decide how to greenlight stories and projects with those guiding principles in mind.

Deputy managing editors also provide direction, editing and help to other senior editors as needed, but work as a strong and empathetic leader and manager to senior editors as well.  

California Newsroom Editor Addendum

The California Newsroom, a collaboration of public radio and nonprofit news outlets in the state spearheaded by KQED, is seeking a deputy managing editor to lead statewide content planning and coordination. This position is a six-month, limited-term position with a possibility to be extended.

This position requires a journalist who is skilled in leading collaborations and partnerships across multiple newsrooms. We are seeking an empathetic and human-centered manager who works well with people at all levels of experience, from early-career reporters to seasoned editors. The deputy managing editor will also be a key editorial strategist, working closely with news directors, reporters and editors from multiple outlets to serve the needs of all the partner newsrooms, from major outlets in large markets to smaller stations with limited resources and personnel. 

This editor will work in collaboration with journalists spread across 14 public radio stations and other partners such as the nonprofit news organization CalMatters to ensure coverage of significant issues, assigning and editing daily news and in-depth features and projects. The editor will also be responsible for coordinating California coverage for a national audience in partnership with NPR.

This editor will work closely with the California Newsroom Managing Editor to ensure that content production aligns with larger strategic goals. The Deputy Managing Editor will step in to run the entire California Newsroom operation in the absence of the Managing Editor, so we’re seeking candidates with both impeccable news judgment and advanced managerial skills. This is a remote position, but the editor must reside in California. The Deputy Managing Editor will manage from 1-4 journalists.

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. We value the contributions of marginalized people in society, including Black, Indigenous, and all people of color, people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people, and we believe that these communities must be centered in the work we do. We strongly encourage members of these communities to apply.

KQED Code of Ethics: https://www.kqed.org/about/code-ethics
 

The mission that drives us:

KQED provides citizens of Northern California with a community-supported alternative to commercial media.   We provide citizens with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions; convene community dialogue; bring the arts to everyone and engage audiences to share their stories. We help students and teachers thrive in 21st-century classrooms, and take people of all ages on journeys of exploration- exposing them to new people, places and ideas.




Essential Functions:
  • Coordinates with newsroom leaders throughout California on daily news coverage, major breaking news and long-term joint projects.
  • Maintains a running database of assignments and planning.
  • Oversees California Newsroom employees assigned to content production and planning. 
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Non-Essential Functions:
  • Occasionally fills in for other colleagues.
  • Represents KQED at events.

Knowledge/Experience Required:
  • At least five years of experience in a similar role in a newsroom or news environment.
  • Interest and knowledge in California news.
  • Excellent communication and coordination skills; clear communication with colleagues.
  • Excellent news judgment.
  • Thorough command of journalistic principles, ethics and standards.
  • Ability to meet deadlines and goals while working under pressure.
  • Proven collaboration skills, which are essential in working with fellow KQED staffers across departments and with partner organizations.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Ability to stay focused, organized, communicative and proactive while working with a number of journalists and staffers across the organization and dealing with several different editors.
  • Ability to stay organized and prioritize tasks when working on multiple projects at once.

Knowledge/Experience Desired:
  • Non-English language skills (fluency in Spanish, Mandarin or other widely spoken languages in California).
  • Previous work as a newsroom manager.
  • Proven capacity to identify opportunities for stories of high relevance to audiences.
NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may be required to perform other related duties as necessary to meet the ongoing needs of this organization.

job.title: Senior Creative Copywriter
job.description:
Who we are:

Burson, part of WPP, is the global communications leader built to create value for clients through reputation. With highly specialized teams, industry-leading technologies and breakthrough creative, we help brands and businesses redefine reputation as a competitive advantage so they can lead today and into the future. When you work at Burson, you are part of a global community of lifelong learners who thrive at the edge of innovation.

WPP (LSE/NYSE: WPP) is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com 

For more information visit bursonglobal.com and follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

 

We´re always on the lookout for spectacular talent. Currently at Burson we are looking for a Senior Creative Copywriter to join our Strategy & Creative team in Madrid or Barcelona.

What you’ll do:

  • Come up with earned-first concepts, campaigns, activations and content for clients across different sectors.
  • Write a lot – and well – across formats: copy, claims, manifestos, scripts, presentations and whatever else the idea requires.
  • Partner closely with the Head of Strategy & Creative and our team of makers to bring creative thinking to teams and projects across the agency.
  • Get involved in new business processes from the start, helping shape the creative response from the client brief all the way to the final presentation.
  • Spot and develop proactive opportunities for existing clients, turning ideas into work that can be sold in and brought to life.
  • Bring fresh ideas, references, creative judgment and practical solutions to the agency’s everyday work.
  • Present and defend ideas with energy and conviction, both internally and with clients.
  • Help us build a stronger creative culture and raise the ambition of the work across the agency.

 

What will contribute to your success:

  • 4-6 years of experience in a creative, PR, social or integrated agency. Your exact background matters less than the quality of your thinking, writing and ideas.
  • Excellent spoken and written Spanish and strong level of English.
  • A real command of words combined with visual sensitivity and the ability to think beyond copy.
  • Curiosity about earned media, influence and integrated communications, especially if you come from a more traditional advertising background.
  • The ability to think big when the opportunity calls for it, while also finding solutions for smaller, everyday briefs.
  • Confidence using AI as part of your creative process: to research, explore routes, prototype and sharpen your ideas.
  • Flexibility to work across different sectors, audiences and communication challenges.
  • A collaborative, low-ego approach and an appetite for working with different teams and specialisms.
  • Ambition, curiosity and excitement about helping us build the next chapter of earned creativity at Burson.

*This role can also be based in Madrid.

 #LI-AY1

You belong at Burson:

Our vision is for Burson to be the leading ‘academy company’ for creative communications professionals and emerging leaders. We provide a dynamic environment where ambitious colleagues come to elevate their skills, expand their networks, and ultimately, produce the best solutions for today’s leading brands. Our commitment to your growth is reflected in our robust benefits and people programs, which include professional development opportunities, mentorship programs with industry leaders, a vibrant and inclusive company culture fostering collaboration and innovation and packages designed to reward and retain top talent. We invest in our people because we believe their success is our success.

At Burson, we’re an agency of learn-it-alls. We recognize that the things we do best, creativity and communications, require a level of nuanced understanding. That’s why it’s imperative for us to hire extraordinarily talented people of all backgrounds and identities. Without that we can’t do the essential work of inspiring bold ideas, fostering constructive dialogue, cultivating meaningful experiences, and driving innovation and creativity for our partners. Your unique point of view—your talent—is what makes you a #BursonPerson, and it’s how we deliver exceptional results for our clients, together.

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process.

When you click the "Submit Application" button below, this will send any information you add below to Burson. Before you do this, we think it's a good idea to read through our  Recruitment Privacy Policy. California residents should read our  California Recruitment Privacy Notice. This explains what we do with your personal data when you apply for a role with us, and, how you can update the information you have provided us with or how to remove it.

job.title: Account Manager (Healthcare Communications)
job.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centered creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Job Summary: 

Real Chemistry is looking for an Account Manager to join our growing team!

Real Chemistry is looking for driven, savvy game changers who are ready to dive into the trenches and make an immediate impact. We are currently seeking an Account Manager with client services experience in healthcare. The position offers a great opportunity for an individual with a passion for healthcare to work with leading clients in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical devices and health IT fields. 

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Lambertville, Boston, Chicago, Carmel, or San Francisco—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs.

What You’ll Do:

  • Responsible for exceptional client service and account management activities for 3-4 accounts
  • In collaboration with account associate, senior management and project management staff, drive flawless and timely project execution and high-touch client communications
  • Participates in development of clients’ marketing strategies and tactics; collaborates with multiple internal stakeholders to ensure consensus around tactics’ scope and approach
  • Support overall account development, resourcing fiscal performance and growth
  • Support day-to-day client contact in executing ad hoc requests and delivering planned activities and materials
  • Develop draft scope of works, contracts, presentations, creative briefs, PR and marketing materials and other internal/external communications
  • Ensure client feedback is gathered, understood and addressed as appropriate across deliverables and internally
  • Document status and otherwise communicate need-to-know information to all project stakeholders to ensure progression along critical path
  • Sets meetings, provides agendas and contact reports
  • Ability to run client calls or meetings independently
  • Manage account finances; must be able to track budget, raise invoices and POs

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • Our Company values – Best Together, Impact-Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always and Accountability with an “I” – really speak to you.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.
  • You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines.

What You Should Have:

  • Highly organized with a mindfulness of deadlines, the ability to manage multiple tasks based on priorities and a strong attention to detail
  • Independent thinker confident in taking ownership of assets and material development, but a team player who enjoys collaboration
  • Professional presence, performs with a sense of urgency and with a client service orientation
  • Has confidence to manage upward when required; able to communicate with managers when deadlines will not be met or when issues are foreseeable
  • High energy, able to effectively operate in fast-paced, growing and evolving environment
  • Demonstrated strong work ethic, with a track record of following through on client requests and with high-quality deliverables on schedule and on budget
  • Has good understanding of social media vehicles and is comfortable managing and drafting communications around them
  • Strong written and oral communication and presentations skills
  • Good management of Microsoft Office tools (PowerPoint, Word, Excel) – particularly PowerPoint
  • Excellent business communication ability including informal/formal presentation and writing skills; this includes confident public speaking both internally and externally with clients, vendors, and affiliates
  • Ability to mentor junior staff and delegate accordingly in order to achieve project deadlines
  • Able to communicate with managers when deadlines will not be met
  • Able to devise and articulate solutions to problems on an ongoing basis
  • Able to clearly communicate project updates, scopes and recommendations to clients
  • Ability to develop project scopes and client and vendor contracts
  • Demonstrated experience with media monitoring, research and taking on projects with limited supervision
  • BA or equivalent work experience required

Pay Range: $63,000 - $72,000 
This is the pay range the Company believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting.  Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, skills, certifications, and geographical location. The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.
