Job Title

Principal Designer

Job Description


About The Position:


People Inc. is looking for a Principal Designer to take on some of the company’s most varied, visible, and important work.


You’ll work directly with the Chief Communications Officer and Chief Design Officer on the work that most visibly represents People Inc.: our events, our brand identity, our sites, what we put in front of investors, and the spaces we work in. Much of it has no precedent, so not every project starts with a defined brief. You’ll collaborate with leadership to frame the problem, and along with the Senior Creative Director, develop the concept and creative direction and bring it to life.


That means pairing ambitious creative thinking with close attention to the details that make the work successful. For events, you’ll work directly with vendors, production companies, and internal partners to carry the design through production, and stay involved through on-site execution. You’ll bring fresh ideas for what our events can be and the resourcefulness to make the most of the budget, spaces, materials, and time available.


You’ll lead other designers and outside partners project by project while staying hands-on. This is a role for someone highly experienced and influential who loves making the work and seeing it through.


In-office Expectations: At least three days per week at our 225 Liberty Street headquarters in New York City.


About The Team:

_____________________________________________________________________________


The Design Group at People Inc. brings together multiple teams supporting Revenue Design, Brand & Editorial Design, Product & UX Design, Design Systems, Creative Operations, Transactional Creative, and Events.

 

This role will work across corporate, brand, communications, and experiential design, partnering closely with senior leadership and designers across the organization.


About The Positions Contributions:


Weight %

Accountabilities, Actions and Expected Measurable Results


Corporate, Brand & Communications Design ›› 70%

  • Lead high-visibility work from problem definition through final execution, including:
    • People Inc. Villa at Cannes, People Talks, Dinner with People, and Brand Showcases
    • People Inc. and People Incorporated sites, corporate and brand identity, and presentation systems
    • Investor Relations materials, including earnings decks, campaigns, and employee communications
    • Office and experiential design, video walls, sizzle reels, and other motion-led experiences
  • Work directly with senior leadership and cross-functional partners to establish creative direction, present work, make decisions, and maintain a high standard of craft. 


Creative Direction, Mentorship & Design Development ›› 30%

  • Define loosely defined problems and develop clear creative approaches before execution.
  • Direct designers, agencies, and creative partners project by project; provide feedback, run creative reviews, and mentor designers and emerging leaders.

Bachelor's degree preferred in design, graphic design, visual communication, or related field, and/or equivalent experience.

job.description:
Job Description:


The New York Post is one of America’s most iconic and recognizable news brands — delivering bold headlines, unforgettable scoops, and sharp commentary since 1801. With a legacy built on fearless journalism and a distinctly New York attitude, The Post has evolved far beyond its print roots to become a modern media powerhouse.


Today, the New York Post Digital Network is one of the most influential voices in the industry, reaching over 80 million unique users each month across our expansive, ever-growing portfolio. Anchored by NYPost.com, PageSix.com, and Decider.com, our digital brands deliver must-read breaking news, sports, entertainment, pop culture, and lifestyle coverage with the same wit, edge, and energy that define The Post. With innovation at our core, we’ve built a true multi-platform ecosystem — spanning web, mobile apps, video, audio, social, print, TV, and commerce. From viral headlines and exclusive stories to original series, podcasts, and live events, we’re engaging audiences where they are — and always on the pulse of what’s next.


We’re looking for a Data Engineer to join our technology team and work on the systems that power The Post’s digital future. This is a hands-on engineering role with a focus on infrastructure services, data pipelines, and identity enrichment. Along the way you’ll also participate in the product development of data-dependent systems such as AI answer services, personalization systems, machine learning, and audience services.


You will build and maintain the foundational data services that power analytics and machine learning for our newsroom, and product teams to deliver cutting-edge thoughtful digital experiences at scale. You’ll work alongside senior engineers, product managers, and data teams, contributing to high-performance systems.


Please Note: Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States on a permanent basis. Sponsorship, including employment visa sponsorship or transfer, is not available for this position now or in the future.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, build, and operate cloud-based data pipelines supporting specialized needs of our consumer websites, native mobile apps, and information services.
  • Work daily with compute services, query services, storage services, and big data services with technologies like Vertex AI, Lambdas, DynamoDB, Cloud Functions, S3, Kubernetes, Glue, and BigQuery inside AWS and GCP.
  • Develop and maintain data ETL pipelines for real-time and batch processing of large-scale content and event data.
  • Write clean, testable, and maintainable code (Python preferred).
  • Collaborate with product, editorial, and data science teams to deliver infrastructure and services that meet business needs.
  • Monitor, optimize, and improve the reliability, security, and cost efficiency of cloud-based systems.
  • Write and present ideas clearly. Document functional requirements for both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Participate in code reviews, architecture discussions, and agile sprint ceremonies.

  • MS or BS in computer science, or related field.

  • Proficiency in Python, SQL, and PySpark
  • Working knowledge of common AWS and/or GCP services
  • Experience building and deploying data pipelines (e.g., Airflow, Dataflow, Glue, or similar tools)
  • Knowledge of data warehouse technologies (BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, etc.)
  • Firm grasp of the tools of the trade including AI tooling, IDEs, Git, JIRA, and agile methodologies.
  • Familiarity with web standards and protocols.
  • Comfort with code reviews, writing unit tests, QA and UAT processes, and exposure to end-to-end testing frameworks.

  • Proactive approach to problem-solving.

  • Familiarity with content-management systems, media, news, publishing, video technology, ad technology, or other high-traffic consumer-facing industries.

The New York Post is one of America’s most iconic and recognizable news brands — delivering bold headlines, unforgettable scoops, and sharp commentary since 1801. With innovation at our core, we’ve built a true multi-platform ecosystem — spanning web, mobile apps, video, audio, social, print, TV, and commerce. From viral headlines and exclusive stories to original series, podcasts, and live events, we’re engaging audiences where they are — and always on the pulse of what’s next. 


We are seeking an experienced, highly analytical, and execution-oriented Vice President, Strategy & Business Transformation. In this role, the incumbent will work closely with the Chief Technology & Strategy Officer and the senior leadership team to build and operationalize enterprise capabilities. Key responsibilities include translating strategic priorities into actionable business decisions, aligning resources around our highest-value opportunities, and driving measurable results.

 

This is a highly visible, hands-on role for a strategic thinker who can move seamlessly between executive-level problem-solving and practical implementation. The successful candidate will help establish the frameworks, processes, governance, and operating rhythms that enable leaders to make informed decisions, prioritize investments, manage competing resources, and accelerate strategic initiatives.

 

The ideal candidate combines the analytical rigor of a management consultant with the pragmatism of an operator. They are comfortable navigating ambiguity, challenging assumptions, influencing senior stakeholders, and turning complex business questions into clear recommendations and measurable outcomes.


Importantly, this role serves as an enabler and facilitator of enterprise strategy. Business leaders retain accountability for decisions and execution within their respective functions.

 

Key Responsibilities:

 

Enterprise Strategy & Executive Alignment

  • Partner with the Chief Technology & Strategy Officer and executive leadership to translate the enterprise operating model into actionable priorities, processes, and governance.
  • Facilitate executive alignment on strategic priorities, organizational objectives, decision rights, and resource allocation.
  • Help define the Strategy Team’s mandate, operating model, engagement approach, and partnership with business functions.
  • Prepare executive presentations, decision briefs, and recommendations to support critical business decisions.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen cross-functional alignment and accelerate enterprise-wide initiatives.

 

Strategic Portfolio & Initiative Management

  • Establish and maintain a consolidated view of enterprise initiatives, strategic investments, resources, ownership, milestones, and expected business outcomes.
  • Develop consistent evaluation frameworks to assess initiatives based on strategic alignment, financial and operational value, ownership, and execution capacity.
  • Facilitate portfolio reviews and recommend opportunities to accelerate, continue, sequence, redesign, or discontinue initiatives.
  • Identify resource constraints, competing priorities, dependencies, and opportunities to redirect capacity toward higher-value business objectives.
  • Establish transparent portfolio reporting and tracking mechanisms.

 

Business Strategy & Decision Support

  • Lead and support high-priority strategic engagements across the organization, translating complex business questions into actionable recommendations.
  • Develop business cases, financial analyses, scenario models, and strategic assessments to inform investment and resource decisions.
  • Create structured decision-making frameworks that clearly outline business questions, supporting evidence, alternatives, financial implications, risks, and recommendations.
  • Work backward from defined decision milestones to ensure strategic engagements produce timely, actionable outcomes.
  • Challenge assumptions and identify opportunities to improve business performance, operational effectiveness, and organizational alignment.

 

Strategy Operations & Governance

  • Design and implement the Strategy Team’s operating processes, including initiative intake, prioritization, engagement selection, and delivery tracking.
  • Establish and facilitate regular enterprise strategy reviews, portfolio reviews, and executive decision forums.
  • Develop governance tools, templates, decision logs, dashboards, and accountability mechanisms.
  • Clarify roles and responsibilities across executive sponsors, initiative owners, working teams, and decision-makers.
  • Streamline existing reporting and meeting structures to improve decision velocity and reduce unnecessary administrative processes.

 

Enterprise Performance & Organizational Effectiveness

  • Partner with Finance, Human Resources, Technology, Product, Editorial, and Revenue leadership to connect enterprise strategy with financial investment, organizational capacity, and business performance.
  • Develop an enterprise scorecard and key performance indicators to measure strategic progress, financial impact, execution, audience growth, and organizational effectiveness.
  • Monitor initiative performance, identify barriers to execution, and facilitate timely resolution of cross-functional issues.
  • Support change management and organizational adoption of new strategy processes and operating practices.
  • Build the capabilities, tools, and knowledge transfer necessary to establish a sustainable Strategy Operations function.

 

Qualifications & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Strategy, or a related discipline; advanced degree or MBA preferred.
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in corporate strategy, management consulting, business operations, enterprise transformation, or strategy execution.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and implementing enterprise prioritization, portfolio management, and strategic operating frameworks.
  • Strong financial acumen, including business case development, financial modeling, investment analysis, and resource planning.
  • Proven ability to partner with CEOs, C-suite executives, and senior functional leaders.
  • Experience facilitating complex business discussions, challenging assumptions, and navigating competing priorities and resource tradeoffs.
  • Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, executive communication, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to translate complex information and ambiguity into concise insights, options, and actionable recommendations.
  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and influencing stakeholders without direct reporting authority.
  • Media, digital publishing, advertising, audience development, subscription, product, or technology experience strongly preferred.

job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 


Software Engineer — Publishing Platform


Downtown Music Publishing is looking for a driven individual to join us as a Software Engineer to help build our next-generation music publishing platform from the ground up. You'll help in shaping the architecture, tooling, and engineering culture of a catalog management platform that powers musical work registration, rights tracking, and royalty collection for publishers worldwide. Currently seeking candidates local to the Nashville Area.


What you'll do


●      Build a new platform from first principles — data model, API design, and infrastructure — rather than maintaining legacy systems, while making pragmatic decisions that hold up at production scale.

●      Design and implement a schema-first GraphQL API (Apollo Server) over PostgreSQL, including multi-tenant data isolation (row-level security), type-safe query layers, and performance patterns like DataLoader batching.

●      Develop React/TypeScript (Next.js) interfaces used by both internal teams and clients to manage catalogs, registrations, and data-quality workflows.

●      Build AI-native features as a core part of the product: AI-assisted data ingestion and matching, agent-accessible APIs via Model Context Protocol (MCP), and LLM-powered workflows using the Vercel AI SDK and Amazon Bedrock.

●      Work in an AI-augmented, spec-driven development workflow — architecture specs, agent-assisted implementation, and rigorous automated review are how the team ships, not an experiment on the side.

●      Own components end-to-end: design, implementation, integration testing against real databases, deployment (AWS CDK), and operational responsibility.

●      Model and implement music publishing domain logic — works, writers, shares, agreements, and society registration formats (e.g., CWR) — with the precision that financial and rights data demands.


You are / have


●      Bachelor's degree in computer science, software development, or equivalent experience.

●      5+ years of experience developing web-based software solutions.

●      Experience architecting new systems or services from scratch — you're comfortable with ambiguity, and you document the "why" behind decisions, not just the "what."

●      Strong proficiency in TypeScript and Node.js across the full stack.

●      Solid relational database fundamentals: schema design, migrations, transactions, and query performance in PostgreSQL (or similar).

●      Experience with both traditional software development lifecycle and agentic software development — including spec-driven development, AI-augmented engineering, and working effectively with coding agents.

●      Interest in the music industry — prior experience with rights management, royalties, or metadata standards (CWR, DDEX, ISWC/ISRC) is a plus, not a requirement.


Ideally, significant experience with some of the following technologies or similar tools:


Backend: Node.js, GraphQL (Apollo Server, schema-first), PostgreSQL, etc.

Frontend: React, Next.js, TypeScript, modern state management (e.g., Zustand)

AI/Agents: Vercel AI SDK, SpecKit, CodeX, Amazon Bedrock, Model Context Protocol (MCP), LLM tool design.

Infrastructure: AWS (including CDK), Docker, Terraform, GitHub Actions

Testing: Vitest, Testcontainers (integration testing against real databases), Playwright

Observability: Datadog, Sentry, structured logging

We are looking for a Lead Machine Learning Engineer to build, ship, and operate reliable machine learning and AI systems that create durable value across UMG. This is a senior individual-contributor role for an engineer who combines strong software and systems expertise with practical knowledge of the AI and ML lifecycle.


You will turn models, data products, and AI workflows into maintainable production capabilities across revenue forecasting, artist, catalog intelligence and talent scouting, release marketing, and rights and ecosystem integrity. job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. Job Summary

Universal Music Group (UMG) is the world’s leading music company. We are committed to artistry, innovation, and entrepreneurship, with businesses spanning recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content across more than 60 countries.


The A/V Senior Manager leads the strategy, architecture, engineering, and operational excellence of UMG’s global audiovisual and workplace technology capabilities. This role enables reliable, secure, and intuitive experiences across conferencing, telephony, meeting rooms, workspace reservation, digital signage, performance spaces, and related collaboration technologies.


Based in Nashville, this is a global leadership role overseeing and enabling a distributed A/V and Workspace Engineering team across Australia, the United States, and the United Kingdom. The leader partners closely with Infrastructure, Facilities, Security, Operations, and business stakeholders to deliver consistent standards while supporting the distinct needs of UMG’s offices, artists, and business functions.


Key Responsibilities

·    Strategy and roadmap: Define and execute UMG’s global A/V and workplace technology strategy, translating business needs into a prioritized, outcome-oriented roadmap and investment plan.

·    People leadership: Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing, globally distributed team. Set clear expectations, support career growth, manage performance, and attract and retain exceptional technical talent.

·    Architecture and standards: Establish reference architectures, engineering standards, design patterns, and governance for conferencing, telephony, room systems, workspace technology, and associated integrations.

·    Portfolio and lifecycle management: Evaluate, select, implement, standardize, and retire platforms and devices across their lifecycle, balancing user experience, interoperability, resilience, security, supportability, and total cost of ownership.

·    Service reliability and operations: Strengthen incident, problem, change, and request-management practices; improve service availability; and drive disciplined root-cause analysis and continual service improvement.

·    Automation and observability: Create a practical framework for inventory, telemetry, monitoring, automation, capacity planning, and health reporting so that teams can identify issues proactively and make decisions using reliable data.

·    Stakeholder partnership: Build trusted relationships with senior leaders, Facilities, Real Estate, Security, Network, End User Computing, Production, and business teams. Explain trade-offs clearly and influence outcomes across organizational boundaries.

·    Budget and vendor management: Own or contribute to budget planning, sourcing, contract management, vendor performance, and financial optimization for the A/V and workplace technology portfolio.

·    Risk, security, and compliance: Partner with Security and Risk teams to incorporate appropriate access controls, privacy, resilience, data protection, and lifecycle controls into A/V and workplace solutions.

·    Innovation and continuous improvement: Monitor industry trends and emerging technologies, test promising capabilities, and recommend adoption when they create measurable value for UMG.

·    Executive communication: Provide concise reporting on service health, priorities, risks, investments, roadmap progress, and business outcomes to senior leadership and key stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

·    Leadership experience: Progressive experience leading A/V, workplace technology, unified communications, or related infrastructure engineering teams, including responsibility for direction, delivery, and talent development.

·    Technical depth: Strong knowledge of enterprise A/V and workplace technologies, including conferencing and collaboration platforms, telephony, room and workspace reservation systems, digital signage, signal flow, and related integrations. Experience with Dante or comparable audio-over-IP technologies is expected.

·    Engineering and architecture: Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, integrating, automating, and supporting reliable A/V solutions in complex enterprise environments.

·    Operational discipline: Strong background in IT service management, incident and problem management, change enablement, service measurement, and continual improvement.

·    Program and commercial management: Experience managing cross-functional programs, business analysis, vendor relationships, budgets, and competing priorities.

·    Communication and influence: Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex technical issues in plain language and convert business needs into practical technology outcomes.

·    Hands-on problem solving: Comfortable deep-diving into existing and emerging technologies, diagnosing issues, evaluating options, and guiding teams toward pragmatic solutions.

·    Education and experience: Bachelor’s degree in technology, engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience, plus at least eight years of relevant A/V, workplace technology, unified communications, or infrastructure experience.

·    Global collaboration: Experience working across regions, time zones, cultures, and organizational boundaries. Occasional travel may be required but is not expected to be part of the regular work schedule.


Preferred Qualifications

·    Experience operating A/V or workplace technology services at global scale, including distributed offices and high-visibility executive, artist, or performance environments.

·    Experience with AV-over-IP, DSP, room control, room analytics, digital signage, device management, and enterprise collaboration ecosystems.

·    Relevant certifications such as CTS/CTS-D, Dante, ITIL, PMP, or equivalent practical experience.

·    Experience building service catalogs, operating models, technology standards, or reference designs that improve consistency and reduce operational complexity.

·    Experience in the music, media, entertainment, creative, or live-events industries.


How Success Is Measured

·    Improved reliability, availability, and user experience across critical A/V and workplace services.

·    Reduced repeat incidents and faster, more consistent resolution through effective service management and root-cause practices.

·    Clear standards, lifecycle plans, inventory visibility, and adoption of supported solutions across locations.

·    Responsible use of budget and vendor capacity, with transparent reporting on value, risk, and total cost of ownership.

·    A strong, engaged, and developing global team that delivers predictably and is recognized as a trusted partner by the business.

Founded in 2007, SoundCloud is a creator-first platform helping artists build and grow their careers by providing them with the most advanced tools, services, and resources. With over 4x the music catalog of every other major streaming platform, spanning 40+ million artists across 190+ countries, SoundCloud is where emerging artists find their sound, hidden gems are discovered, and music culture is shaped in real time.   SoundCloud is looking for a software engineer to join our Media Streaming Team, with a mission to operate a media streaming platform at global scale, delivering the best possible audio experience to creators, listeners, and partners alike. We are handling petabytes of data and gigabytes per second of traffic. You will join a tightly-knit team where you will help shape how millions of people experience music.  

Read about engineering at SoundCloud

Key Responsibilities: 

  • Contribute to building, scaling and maintaining backend APIs and services that serve millions of users
  • Collaborate closely with Android, iOS, web, and full-stack engineers to deliver seamless end-to-end media experiences
  • Ensure performance, scalability, and maintainability of SoundCloud’s services
  • Debug complex issues across systems, ensuring a consistent experience for users globally
  • Participate in architecture discussions, code reviews, and roadmap planning
  • Be part of on-call rotation to ensure the reliability and availability of SoundCloud’s systems

Experience and Background:

  • 4+ years of experience in building and operating large-scale backend or distributed systems
  • Proficiency in Go
  • Hands-on experience with infrastructure as code (IaC) using Terraform
  • Experience with cloud-native environments such as AWS or GCP
  • Experience with microservices, SQL/NoSQL databases, and container technologies
  • You care about the craft of software engineering: continuous delivery, defensive programming, automated testing, clean code principles
  • You have a strong sense of ownership and are comfortable navigating ambiguity in fast-moving environments
  • You bring a humble attitude, an eagerness to help your colleagues, and a desire to do whatever it takes to make the team succeed 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience designing APIs and backend services consumed by multiple client platforms
  • Experience with Scala or other functional programming languages
  • Knowledge of API communication patterns (e.g., gRPC, GraphQL)
  • Exposure to media streaming, playback, audio engineering or adjacent domains
  • Familiarity with audio/video codecs, streaming protocols (HLS, DASH), and transport container technologies
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools and a strong intuition for their strengths, weaknesses, and emerging opportunities

About us:

  • We are a multinational company with offices in the US (New York and Los Angeles), Germany (Berlin), and the UK (London)
  • We provide a flexible work culture that offers the opportunity to collaborate and connect in person at our offices as well as accommodating work from home
  • We are deeply committed to ensuring diversity, equity and inclusion at all levels of our organization and fostering a community where everyone’s voice, perspective and experience is respected and heard.
  • We believe a strong team is made by investing in employees through mentorship, workshops and enrichment opportunities

Benefits:

  • Interested in a gym membership, photography course or book? We have a Creativity and Wellness benefit!
  • Employee Equity Plan
  • Generous professional development allowance
  • Flexible vacation and public holiday policy where you can take up to 35 days of PTO annually
  • Various snacks, goodies, and 2 free lunches weekly when at the office

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion at SoundCloud

SoundCloud is for everyone. Diversity and open expression are fundamental to our organization; they help us lead what’s next in music by understanding and empowering our creators and fans, no matter their identity. We acknowledge the challenges in the music industry, and strive to influence an inclusive culture where everyone can contribute respectfully and thrive, especially the historically marginalized communities that many of our creators, fans and SoundClouders identify with. We are dedicated to creating an inclusive environment at SoundCloud for everyone, regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, migration background, national origin, age, disability status, or care-giver status.

At SoundCloud you can find your community or elevate your allyship by joining a Diversity Resource Group. Diversity Resource Groups are employee-organized groups focused on supporting and promoting the interests of a particular underrepresented community in order to build a more inclusive culture at SoundCloud. Anyone can join, whether you share the identity or strive to be an ally.

job.title: Reporter, State AGs
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking two aggressive, enterprising reporters to cover state attorneys general as national political and policy actors. Each reporter will be a founding member of POLITICO's new State AGs team, and will report on how AGs are shaping tech, energy, health care, consumer protection and antitrust policy regionally and nationally, and the dynamics shaping multistate and partisan coalitions.

 

The reporters will cover four overlapping areas:

  • The anchor states. California, New York, Texas and Florida run the most powerful AG offices in the country, and their actions on tech, finance, energy and health care often set national standards.
  • Other key states. The offices that drive coalition strategy and national policy fights, including Illinois, Massachusetts, New Jersey and Washington on the Democratic side, and Tennessee, Missouri, Louisiana and Utah on the Republican side.
  • A redrawn AG map. November's elections gave Democrats AG offices in Texas, Ohio, Georgia, Iowa and Kansas. The beat will follow how those offices take shape and how Republican AGs respond.
  • Coalition dynamics. How multistate coalitions form and fracture, who leads and who follows, how DAGA and RAGA shape them, and where AGs of both parties find common ground.

 

A deep source network inside AG offices of both parties will be essential, going well beyond public filings and press releases. Those sources will drive exclusive news on investigations and lawsuits, along with reporting from inside coalition conversations on which cases to bring, which companies to target and which states will sign on.

 

The beat will focus closely on how AGs decide where to intervene, against business or against the federal government. Democratic AGs have become the front line of legal resistance to the Trump administration, while Republican AGs have often acted as its partners and force multipliers. The beat will also track how coalitions form, who leads them and who follows, where AGs of both parties find common ground, and how the office has become a launchpad for national ambition.

 

The policy portfolio will include health care, antitrust, AI and tech platforms, consumer protection, climate and energy, financial services, ESG and DEI, labor, and the limits of federal power — the enforcement fights where AGs are most active and where their actions carry the biggest consequences for companies and investors.

 

The reporters will work hand in hand with POLITICO's California, New York and Florida teams, which already cover their states' AGs closely as political figures and policymakers.

 

What You'll Need:

  • Reporting experience covering politics, policy, government or the law
  • A demonstrated ability to break news and deliver original, incisive reporting
  • Deep familiarity with state politics and with the state-federal legal battles of the past decade
  • The ability to build a network of sources in AG offices, DAGA, RAGA, or the legal and political circles around them
  • A strong interest in the personalities, rivalries and ambitions that drive AG offices
  • An entrepreneurial spirit and eagerness to help build an exciting new part of our journalism
  • The ability to juggle fast-moving breaking news with ambitious enterprise reporting
  • The ability to write clearly, accurately and efficiently on deadline for an influential, professional audience
  • A collaborative spirit and willingness to work with reporters and editors across POLITICO's state, legal and policy teams
  • A rigorous commitment to fair-minded, accurate and nonpartisan journalism

 

We’re open to candidates based in Arlington, VA (HQ); New York, NY; or Sacramento, CA. If you’re not near one of our offices, we still encourage you to apply.

 

Compensation: $90,000-$140,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

About Us.

POLITICO illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow's headlines, not reports on yesterday's news. As politics has increasingly become the defining force of our era, our work has never been more vital. 


Cabinet secretaries and Ministers start their mornings with our analysis. CEOs shape strategy around our reporting. Advocacy leaders rely on our insights to move policy. We deliver the straightforward facts and clear-eyed analysis they need to navigate the most complex political landscape of our lifetimes. 


Our 1,100+ publishing professionals across the world's key democratic capitals—Washington, Brussels, London, Paris, Berlin, Sacramento, and New York—form the world's premier politics and policy newsroom. We tell the story of how power really works by explaining who wields it and how they plan to exercise it, connecting dots others miss and delivering scoops from sources others don't even know exist. 


Innovation has always been a core tenet of our story. At launch, we bet that depth would trump scale, that talent would trump traffic, and that politics would become central to modern life. In 2011, we made another bet and launched POLITICO Pro to help decision-makers understand the business of government, transforming both how they shape government action and the business of journalism itself. 


These bets have made POLITICO the most successful digital news startup of its generation and the indispensable resource for leaders who shape the future. Today, we are a rarity in media: a growing, profitable, and sustainable news organization. 


POLITICO is a subsidiary of Axel Springer SE, a family-owned transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York. Axel Springer is dedicated to shaping the future of journalism in the free world, believing that a free and informed society is essential to democracy. Learn more about Axel Springer.

job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking an ambitious, enterprising reporter to cover the legal and corporate ecosystem around state attorneys general as part of a new POLITICO newsletter. The reporter will be a founding member of POLITICO's new State AGs team, and will focus on the lawyers, firms, companies and power brokers who work with AGs, against them and around them. 

 

State AGs’ biggest cases are often built and argued alongside outside counsel, and a growing roster of firms has built dedicated state AG practices to defend companies and help them manage AG risk. Those practices are staffed increasingly by former AGs, deputies and senior aides

 

The beat will cover that world closely. The reporter will dig into investigations, lawsuits and settlements, the corporate strategies for fighting or heading off AG action, and the relationships, rivalries and money that determine which cases get brought

 

The beat will also track which companies and industries fund RAGA and DAGA, and how corporate members and donors engage with AGs and try to shape their priorities on both sides.

 

The policy portfolio will include health care, antitrust, AI and tech platforms, consumer protection, climate and energy, financial services, ESG and DEI, labor, and the limits of federal power — the enforcement fights where AGs are most active and where their actions carry the biggest consequences for companies and investors.

 

The reporter will work closely with the State AGs team's other reporters, the product's senior editor, and POLITICO's legal, tech, energy and health teams on sourcing and coverage planning.

 

What You'll Need:

  • Reporting experience covering the law, the legal industry, corporate litigation, or regulation and enforcement
  • An understanding of how state AG enforcement, multistate litigation and settlements work
  • A demonstrated ability to break news and deliver original, incisive reporting
  • The ability to build a network of sources among outside counsel, defense firms, in-house lawyers and former AG officials
  • An entrepreneurial spirit and eagerness to help build an exciting new part of our journalism
  • The ability to juggle fast-moving breaking news and write clearly, accurately and efficiently on deadline for an influential, professional audience
  • A collaborative spirit and willingness to work with reporters and editors across POLITICO's state, legal and policy teams
  • A rigorous commitment to fair-minded, accurate and nonpartisan journalism

 

We’re open to candidates based in Arlington, VA (HQ); New York, NY; or Sacramento, CA. If you’re not near one of our offices, we still encourage you to apply.

job.title: Producer, Audio/Video
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a skilled video producer/editor for a daily technology show. In this role, you’ll oversee recording sessions, make creative and editorial decisions to shape episodes, ensure high quality and accuracy, and edit episodes to completion. 


The show is a companion product to a daily newsletter, and you’ll work closely with the hosts, newsletter authors, and editors to highlight the best reporting and analysis each day — while building a distinct product that stands alone and features the unique strengths of a conversational format.


Our shows are multiplatform products, with audio, video, and social media elements. The ideal candidate is a strong video editor; experience with audio editing is a strong plus. Please note your skillset in your application. 


This is a Sunday-Thursday role and requires some evening work to produce a daily early-morning show (the estimated schedule is 2pm-10pm EST). We’ll consider candidates to work out of our HQ (Arlington, VA), New York, San Francisco or Sacramento.


Who You Are:

  • An experienced producer with a track record of writing scripts or briefings for shows and translating complex reporting into compelling pod/vodcasts. 
  • A strong session producer with experience coaching talent and working with experienced hosts and newer voices. 
  • A skilled video editor able to produce tight, polished edits on a deadline
  • A keen follower of tech and AI news, with an interest in how those overlap with politics and policy. 
  • Experienced in multiplatform distribution, finding production efficiencies between audio, video and social media, and producing for different channels and audiences
  • A team player, great at giving and taking notes and working across different teams of people

What You’ll Do:

  • Oversee the virtual recording of a daily tech news podcast — including technical aspects and helping coach talent and guide editorial direction
  • Collaborate with hosts, editors, and the audio/video team to identify daily topics
  • Edit and publish clean, final cuts of episodes, often under tight deadlines
  • Write headline and caption copy for podcast feeds, YouTube and other social platforms
  • Partner with teams across the newsroom on distribution and publishing
  • Monitor episode performance metrics and use audience insights to inform future episodes

What You’ll Need:

  • 3+ years’ experience in podcast or video production, with significant experience in news, politics, or policy
  • Strong editing ability; producing clean, polished video under tight deadlines (audio editing a strong plus).
  • Sharp editorial judgment and storytelling instincts grounded in journalistic standards
  • Strong communication skills for coordinating with hosts, editors and cross-functional partners
  • Familiarity with audience analytics and platform metrics to help guide content strategy

This role is based in our Arlington, VA HQ. We’re also open to candidates in New York or California (Sacramento or San Francisco).


Compensation:

  • $90,000-$110,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a creative and strategic Senior Video Producer to help make and grow our video products across YouTube, podcasts and social media. This role is a player-coach — you’ll be a hands-on producer and editor for key interviews and series, and work with the team on strategy and execution of other projects. 


You’ll join in shaping the visual identity and creative direction of multiple video products, working closely with hosts, editors, and newsroom partners to turn strong reporting into compelling, distinctive video. You’ll also play a key role in POLITICO’s YouTube presence — from programming strategy to growth and performance.


Who You Are:

  • An experienced video producer with a strong editorial sensibility and a track record of building and overseeing video projects — including booking and managing crews for field shoots. 
  • A great video editor, who can create excellent videos and give guidance to the edits of others. 
  • A creative editor and storyteller who enjoys shaping look, feel, and format — not just executing a run of show.
  • A strategic thinker who understands how video lives on YouTube and other platforms, and how to design content accordingly.
  • A strong collaborator who can work across the newsroom to surface smart ideas and translate them into scalable video concepts.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own the production of a weekly video show — including running field shoots (when needed), overseeing recording sessions, and editing a strong video from beginning to end. 
  • Help oversee POLITICO’s long-form video podcast ecosystem, helping define the visual identity, brand, and publishing strategy for each show — and ensuring they feel distinct from one another.
  • Grow POLITICO’s YouTube channel, including strategy, programming mix, performance analysis, and audience growth.
  • Work with more junior video editors on social videos and other projects, giving feedback as necessary.
  • Assist on key projects, big interviews, high-profile news moments, and other such needs as they arise.

What You’ll Need:

  • 6+ years of experience producing video, ideally in news, politics, or policy. Experience with audio is a strong plus. 
  • Significant experience with video editing and post-production workflows, as well as overseeing the work of other editors.
  • Strong editorial judgment grounded in journalistic standards and POLITICO’s mission.
    Experience managing projects in a fast-paced newsroom environment.
  • Deep familiarity with YouTube strategy, analytics, and platform-specific best practices.
  • Excellent communication and organizational skills, with the ability to juggle multiple projects at once.
  • Comfort experimenting with new formats and iterating based on performance and feedback.

  • $100,000-$135,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

Job Description


PLEASE NOTE BEFORE APPLYING:

  • This Analyst position requires work to be performed onsite full time.
  • Positions for this Analyst role are available in the following states: California, Hawaii, Nevada, Oregon, Washington

Are you passionate about the chance to bring your analysis experience to a world class organization that is leading the way in both content and technology to serve and protect our citizens home and abroad?  Do you have the skills necessary to provide research and expertise to the national security community, the US military, law enforcement, and the private sector? Then Thomson Reuters Special Services (TRSS) is looking for you!


Key Responsibilities
In this opportunity as an Analyst, you will be responsible for performing a wide range of work, from due diligence assessments to threat management reports. We leverage openly available data and our own proprietary holdings to develop relevant, insightful products.


As an Analyst, you will also contribute to a variety of areas including:

  • Providing on-site client support, including but not limited to client inquiries, requests for ad hoc reporting, miscellaneous research, and advice on analytic methods.
  • Providing insightful, well-researched analysis and guidance to clients based on rigorous, in-depth analysis using public records, proprietary data, social media data and other open source data.
  • Becoming a practitioner of the latest in research and analytic methodologies, and an expert in TRSS proprietary data and technology solutions who effectively communicates actionable insights through a variety of media, to include data visualization technologies and data processing methods.
  • Working closely with client managers and TRSS Analysts to develop strong collaborative practices in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Demonstrating personal accountability and ownership of work, with an emphasis on exhibiting success in accomplishing progressively more complex tasks, projects, and collaborations.
  • Participating in analytic development at TRSS, to include mentorship, training and developing analytic best practices.

 

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years previous work experience in research and analysis, public records, open source and/or social media data to support research and analysis.
  • Bachelor's required, master's preferred.  
  • Experience conducting investigative research and analysis to identify risks, relationships, patterns, and areas of potential concern.
  • Familiarity with analyzing complex networks, organizational structures, business relationships, and associations among individuals and entities.
  • Experience gathering and synthesizing information from multiple sources, evaluating source credibility, and identifying gaps or inconsistencies in available information.
  • Ability to translate complex research into clear, well-supported written assessments that distinguish facts from judgments and communicate uncertainty.
  • Strong reading and formal writing skills, with demonstrated ability in composition and source evaluation.
  • Strong critical thinking skills and attention to detail, with demonstrated high proficiency using open source and research database tools and an emphasis on incorporating multiple data streams into a single deliverable.
  • Demonstrated ability to engage with project teams and clients in a collegial and professional manner and respond quickly to their requests.
  • U.S. Citizenship essential to comply with government contract/agency or department of Federal Government requirements.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. national security clearance.
  • Position is contingent on the candidate’s ability to clear a customer specific background investigation.
  • This position will have access to highly sensitive public record information and as a result, all new hires and current employees in positions of this level will be subject to periodic background checks.

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting federal government agencies, law enforcement, national security, or other mission-driven clients in a research or analytical capacity.
  • Experience with link analysis, data visualization, geospatial analysis, or other advanced analytic techniques.
  • Familiarity with legal, regulatory, or investigative processes and handling sensitive or restricted information.
  • Experience conducting investigative research and analysis to identify risks, relationships, patterns, and areas of potential concern.
  • Familiarity with analyzing complex networks, organizational structures, business relationships, and associations among individuals and entities.
  • Familiarity with advanced open-source research techniques.
  • Experience tailoring analytic findings to different audiences through briefings, presentations, or other decision-support products.

#LI-CS1

 

 


What’s in it For You?

  • Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.
  • Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.
  • Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
  • Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
  • Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.
  • Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.
  • Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

 

 

In the United States, Thomson Reuters offers a comprehensive benefits package to our employees. Our benefit package includes market competitive health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance programs, as well as a competitive 401k plan with company match. In addition, Thomson Reuters offers market leading work life benefits with competitive vacation, sick and safe paid time off, paid holidays (including two company mental health days off), parental leave, sabbatical leave. These benefits meet or exceeds the requirements of paid time off in accordance with any applicable state or municipal laws. Finally, Thomson Reuters offers the following additional benefits: optional hospital, accident and sickness insurance paid 100% by the employee; optional life and AD&D insurance paid 100% by the employee; Flexible Spending and Health Savings Accounts; fitness reimbursement; access to Employee Assistance Program; Group Legal Identity Theft Protection benefit paid 100% by employee; access to 529 Plan; commuter benefits; Adoption & Surrogacy Assistance; Tuition Reimbursement; and access to Employee Stock Purchase Plan.

Thomson Reuters complies with local laws that require upfront disclosure of the expected pay range for a position. The base compensation range varies across locations. Job Description


We are looking for a Strategic Account Executive to expand our presence across Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, Costa Rica, and Guatemala by developing new business opportunities and growing strategic customer relationships within the assigned geography.


This role is ideal for a highly autonomous, results-driven sales professional with a strong hunter mindset and proven experience selling SaaS technology solutions to corporate or enterprise clients.

The successful candidate will be responsible for driving new customer acquisition, managing key commercial relationships, and contributing to the growth of the business across the region in our Platform "Thomson Reuters Confirmation"

Key Responsibilities

  • Drive business growth across the assigned territory by identifying, prospecting, and closing new customers.
  • Develop and manage strategic accounts within Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, Costa Rica, and Guatemala.
  • Independently generate leads through LinkedIn, databases, networking, and other prospecting channels.
  • Coordinate meetings and build relationships with key decision-makers and senior stakeholders.
  • Lead consultative sales conversations to understand client needs and position the appropriate SaaS solutions.
  • Prepare and deliver compelling commercial proposals tailored to customer requirements.
  • Manage the full sales cycle from prospecting through negotiation and close.
  • Support retention, upselling, and renewal opportunities within existing accounts where applicable.
  • Present monthly pipeline updates, sales results, and business progress to leadership.
  • Prioritize activities and opportunities based on business direction and market potential.
  • Lead important business initiatives and contribute to the execution of commercial strategies within the region.
  • Provide market insights and specialized recommendations to management to support decision-making and growth plans.
  • Manage budget considerations related to projects or programs within the scope of the role.
  • Partner with internal stakeholders to support complex customer needs and ensure effective account development.

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in consultative sales of SaaS technology solutions within the corporate and/or enterprise segment.

  • Ability to work independently with a high level of ownership, structure, and accountability.

Preferred Qualifications

  • MBA or other advanced business degree.

Job Title: Lead Consultant – Software Implementation


As a Lead Consultant, you will lead the successful implementation of software solutions for clients across multiple geographies. You will combine strong SQL and software implementation expertise with consulting, stakeholder management, and customer-facing skills to deliver projects from discovery through go-live and post-production support.

This role is ideal for a detail-oriented, client-focused professional who can understand business requirements, configure and deploy product solutions, conduct testing and training, and ensure a high level of customer satisfaction. You will collaborate closely with customers and internal teams, including Product Development, Support, Pre-Sales, Sales, and Technology.

  • Lead end-to-end software implementation projects from kickoff through go-live, hypercare, and transition to the support team.

  • Use SQL for data analysis, configuration, troubleshooting, validation, and implementation support.
  • Collaborate with customers to define and execute User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and resolve identified issues.
  • Support production-readiness planning, go-live activities, and post-production support for escalated issues.
  • Deliver customer training on product functionality, configuration, and effective system usage.
  • Build and maintain strong client relationships and manage key stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.

job.title: Senior Software Engineer — Customer Files Orchestration
job.description:
Job Description

Job description
Senior Software Engineer — Customer Files Orchestration  

CoCounsel Legal is seeking a Senior Software Engineer to help build and operate the Customer Files Orchestration Service – the system that makes a customer's own documents usable by CoCounsel Legal's agents. 

Every file a customer brings to CoCounsel passes through this team: upload, storage, extraction, embedding, and indexing, orchestrated end-to-end. You make millions of customer files available to CoCounsel. Bringing a customer's content together with Thomson Reuters' world-class proprietary content and the latest frontier models – including TR's own custom large language models – is what makes our products highly differentiated and our agent experiences genuinely grounded. This team is a critical part of what makes that combination possible. 

It is also, unavoidably, a hard distributed systems problem. Supporting millions of files means real engineering: dedicated workers, fair queuing so one busy customer cannot starve another, durable state, idempotent processing, and honest reasoning about consistency and delivery guarantees across systems this team does not own. 

The team owns what it builds, designing, implementing, testing, deploying, scaling, and operating the service end-to-end. As a Senior Software Engineer you own a meaningful part of that service outright. You are eager to ship something you’re proud of and become someone the team trusts. 

Key responsibilities:

Design & Technical Ownership 

  • Own the orchestration service end-to-end – Take an ambiguous problem, shape it into a design, write the ADR, build it, ship it, and operate it. You and the team are accountable for the outcome, not just the pull request. 

  • Make and defend the calls that define this domain – Where eventual consistency is safe and where only a strongly-consistent read is correct; at-least-once with idempotent processing versus the real cost of exactly-once; lease and heartbeat models for crash recovery; compare-and-swap state transitions across asynchronous service boundaries. 

  • Build the queuing and flow-control machinery – Fair queuing so one busy tenant cannot starve another, rate limiting, backpressure, circuit breaking, dead-letter handling, and autoscaling. 

  • Treat our APIs as a product – CoCounsel's file and workspace APIs serve a growing set of consumers beyond orchestration. Versioned contracts, documented behavior, backward compatibility, and deliberate change management are part of the work, not paperwork after it. 

  • Design for correctness at scale, not correctness in a test – Anticipate the failure modes that only appear under concurrency and load and build systems where whole classes of bugs cannot occur rather than fixing them one at a time. 

Reliability & Operations 

  • Operate what you build – Take a primary on-call rotation for the service, lead incident response, and drive the post-mortem that keeps the same failure from recurring. 

  • Make the system explain itself – Instrument and trace well enough to tell "we never notified downstream" apart from "we notified downstream too early", and to answer a customer's "where did my file go?" in minutes rather than days. 

  • Reduce operational toil deliberately – Automate the recurring manual fix and treat a runbook step that exists only in someone's head as a defect. 

Technical Leadership & Collaboration 

  • Raise the bar around you – Mentor engineers through code review and design review. Bring positive energy to the team.  

  • Work well across boundaries – Some stages of this pipeline are owned by other teams. Partner with the storage, extraction, indexing, connectors, and front-end teams to ensure we all ship something great. 

  • Fully integrate Architecture and DevOps – You are part of a team where engineers do the system design. There are no DevOps engineers because everyone is responsible for developing and operating. 

  • Communicate trade-offs plainly – Make the cost of correctness, the meaning of a throughput number, and the risk in a deadline legible to product partners and to your own team. 

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's or master's degree – Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 

  • 5+ years building production software – With a track record of owning significant components in systems that real customers depend on. 

  • Extensive AWS and production Python experience – This is a Python service on AWS, and you should be able to move confidently through both the code and the infrastructure. 

  • Concurrency in Python, and a healthy respect for how treacherous it is – You understand the GIL and what it does and does not protect you from, you have written and debugged production asyncio code, and you have been bitten by the classics: fire-and-forget tasks that swallow their own failures, blocking work smuggled onto the event loop, semaphores and pools that quietly cap throughput far below the worker count, and background tasks racing the state they are meant to be updating. 

  • Kubernetes in production – Our workers and APIs run as pods with event-driven autoscaling (KEDA). You have tuned scalers and resource requests, and you have debugged the real failure modes. 

  • Large-scale orchestration or data pipeline experience – Systems that move large volumes of work through multiple stages across service boundaries, where retries, partial failure, and long-running steps are the normal case rather than the exception. 

  • Consistency models – You can explain where eventual consistency is safe and where it silently corrupts a user-visible outcome, and you have debugged the difference in production. 

  • Delivery guarantees – At-least-once versus exactly-once, why idempotency is usually the real answer, and what it costs to get it wrong. 

  • Queues, fair queuing, rate limiting, and backpressure – Practical, hands-on understanding, including multi-tenant fairness and noisy-neighbor isolation. 

  • API design instincts – Versioned contracts, clear ownership, backward compatibility, and treating an internal API as something other teams build on. 

  • Real operational ownership – You have carried the pager for something you built, debugged it under pressure, and come out with a fix rather than a workaround. 

  • Strong engineering fundamentals – Testing, code review, observability, CI/CD, and infrastructure-as-code as habits rather than obligations. 

  • Clear communication – You can write a design down, defend it, change your mind when the evidence says so, and explain the result to someone who does not share your context. 
     

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Documents and document management systems – Extraction, OCR, format handling, very large files, and the integration surface of third-party DMS platforms. 

  • Event-driven architectures and streaming – Kafka/MSK or similar, managed queueing such as SQS, and event-driven autoscaling. 

  • Durable workflow engines – Temporal, Step Functions, or similar, with a clear view of when they are worth adopting. 

  • Retrieval, embedding, or indexing pipelines – Supporting LLM or agentic applications. 

  • Prior exposure to the legal industry – A real bonus, and a meaningful head start on understanding what our customers actually need from their documents. 

  • Team topologies – This organization uses its vocabulary natively (stream-aligned teams, platform teams, and the boundaries between them) to reason about how services and teams are shaped.

job.title: Valuation and Technical Accounting Manager
job.description:
Valuation and Technical Accounting Manager


The Valuation and Technical Accounting Manager will support and help lead key accounting aspects of global M&A transactions under IFRS, ensuring compliance and accuracy throughout the process. This role will partner closely with Finance, Legal, Tax, and Business leadership teams to support strategic acquisitions and integrations, as well as disposals/divestitures and separation activities where applicable.

The position will be responsible for supporting due diligence, acquisition accounting, intangible asset valuation support, and the integration of acquired entities into our financial systems. In addition, this role will support disposal accounting considerations and the separation of divested businesses, ensuring alignment with corporate policies and global standards.

This role also contributes to consistency in M&A accounting practices by helping implement standard approaches, maintaining strong documentation, and supporting timely and accurate financial reporting for transactions. The Manager will foster collaboration across teams and maintain clear communication with stakeholders to enable successful execution of the company's growth strategy.


About the Role

  • Support and help lead the accounting workstream for M&A projects, ensuring compliance with IFRS standards, particularly IFRS 3, 10, 13, IFRS 5, and IAS 36 and 38.
  • Support comprehensive due diligence on potential acquisitions and divestitures to assess financial health and identify accounting considerations.
  • Support acquisition accounting processes, including preparation of accounting entries and schedules and the coordination and review of purchase price allocations and related documentation.
  • Support disposal/divestiture accounting processes, including held-for-sale/discontinued operations considerations (where applicable), gain/loss support, and related disclosures.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support smooth financial integration of acquired entities and, where relevant, effective financial separation of divested businesses (including intercompany considerations and TSA impacts).
  • Contribute to the development and maintenance of accounting policies, procedures, templates, and checklists to support M&A activities and promote consistent execution.
  • Provide guidance and practical support to finance and accounting teams on acquisition accounting, disposal accounting, and integration/separation processes.
  • Support analysis and reporting on the financial impact of acquisitions and disposals, providing insights to senior management and key stakeholders.
  • Support preparation and review of financial reporting disclosures related to M&A transactions, ensuring compliance with IFRS and company policies.
  • Stay updated with developments in IFRS and other relevant accounting standards and share implications with the team.
  • Support retention of transaction documentation and make materials available to local audit/tax teams where and when required.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with internal stakeholders and external partners and support cross-team efforts to improve processes and efficiencies.

About You

  • Fluent in English.
  • Strong experience in accounting, with a focus on IFRS and M&A-related projects.
  • Experience in valuation, particularly in intangible asset valuation for purchase price allocation.
  • Experience preparing accounting position memos and addressing related technical accounting matters is a plus. 
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with global and diverse teams.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience working in a multinational company.

job.description:
At DistroKid, we help artists share their music with the world. Around 40-50% of the world's new music is released through DistroKid today.

Summary:

We are seeking a Senior Data Engineer to join our team at DistroKid. The successful candidate will play a crucial role in designing, developing, and maintaining our data infrastructure, ensuring the seamless flow of data across various teams and platforms. This role will partner with our current data engineers, data analysts, data scientists, and work closely with database administrators, software developers, security, devops, system operations and AI enablement peers. This is a fantastic opportunity to have a significant impact across our entire business, and there is broad scope for the successful candidate to bring new approaches and best practices into our existing infrastructure.

If you have a strong background in data engineering and a passion for music and the entertainment industry, we encourage you to apply for this exciting opportunity to make a significant impact on the global music distribution landscape.

What You’ll Do:

  1. Individual contributor ownership within an existing small team of data analytics, science and engineering, reporting into the VP of Data. Furthermore, broader collaboration with software developers, database administrators, security, devops, system operations and AI enablement teams to design, develop, and maintain scalable and reliable data pipelines and ETL processes. Your work will shape and help scale critical infrastructure that is core to the experience of millions of our artists. 
  2. Work closely with the data science and backend services teams to assist with their needs, including aiding robust data pipelines and designing, deploying and maintaining critical machine learning and AI infrastructure.
  3. Ensure data quality and consistency by implementing robust data validation, transformation, and cleaning processes.
  4. Develop and maintain data warehousing solutions to provision efficient storage, retrieval, and analysis of large datasets.
  5. Monitor and improve the performance of database systems and associated pipelines, ensuring high availability and responsiveness.
  6. Leverage agentic tooling and modern LLM software to efficiently produce high-quality code and architecture, alongside robust monitoring and oversight.
  7. Stay up-to-date with the latest data engineering trends, technologies, and methodologies, and contribute to continuously improving the company's data infrastructure and practices.

job.title: Finance Assistant (w/m/d) – BERLIN
job.description:
Finance Assistant (w/m/d) – BERLIN

Wir suchen ab sofort eine:n Finance Assistant (w/m/d) für unseren Standort Berlin.

Du arbeitest gerne strukturiert, hast ein gutes Gespür für Zahlen und möchtest praktische Erfahrung in einem abwechslungsreichen Finance-Umfeld sammeln? Du bist zuverlässig, genau und behältst auch bei mehreren Aufgaben den Überblick? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung!

In dieser praxisnahen Support-Rolle unterstützt du unseren Head of Finance im operativen Tagesgeschäft. Du musst noch kein Finance-Profi sein: Wichtig sind uns Organisationstalent, Genauigkeit, Verlässlichkeit und die Bereitschaft, bestehende Prozesse sorgfältig umzusetzen. Eine umfassende Einarbeitung in unsere Abläufe, Systeme und deine konkreten Aufgaben ist vorgesehen.

DEINE AUFGABEN

  • Du unterstützt den Head of Finance bei den täglichen Finance- und administrativen Aufgaben.

  • Du arbeitest nach bestehenden Finance-Prozessen und stellst sicher, dass Aufgaben sorgfältig und zuverlässig erledigt werden.

  • Du verfolgst offene Vorgänge mit unserem Shared Service Centre nach und unterstützt dabei, dass Anfragen abgeschlossen werden.

  • Du aktualisierst Excel-Tabellen, Reports und Finance-Tracker.

  • Du unterstützt bei einfachen Datenanalysen und prüfst Informationen auf Vollständigkeit und Richtigkeit.

  • Du hilfst bei der Pflege von Prozessdokumentationen, erinnerst an Abläufe und beantwortest grundlegende Fragen aus dem Team.

  • Du unterstützt bei Kunden- und Lieferantenanfragen, beim Forderungsmanagement und bei routinemäßigen Mahnläufen; komplexere Themen stimmst du mit dem Head of Finance ab.

  • Du hilfst bei der Anlage von Kund:innen, Lieferant:innen und Projekten, einschließlich der Erstellung und Nachverfolgung von Tickets.

  • Du unterstützt bei einfachen Finance-System- und Workflow-Themen zwischen Business, Shared Service Centre und Finance Systems Team, zum Beispiel bei fehlenden Freigaben oder Änderungen von Zuständigkeiten.

  • Du prüfst Reise- und Ausgabenabrechnungen auf Vollständigkeit und klärst offene Punkte.

  • Du unterstützt nach Anleitung bei der Vorbereitung von Umsatzsteuererklärungen, Zahlungsläufen und routinemäßigen Monatsabschlussaufgaben.

  • Du übernimmst weitere klar definierte Finance- und administrative Aufgaben nach Bedarf.

DEINE SKILLS

  • Erste Erfahrung im Finance-Bereich ist von Vorteil, aber kein Muss – wichtiger sind Neugier und Lernbereitschaft.

  • Du verfügst über gute Excel-Kenntnisse und arbeitest sicher mit Tabellen.

  • Du arbeitest gerne mit Zahlen und prüfst Details sorgfältig.

  • Du bist organisiert und kannst Aufgaben systematisch abarbeiten.

  • Du kannst Anweisungen gut aufnehmen und bestehende Prozesse zuverlässig umsetzen.

  • Du arbeitest genau, verlässlich und übernimmst Verantwortung für die vollständige Bearbeitung deiner Aufgaben.

  • Du fragst nach, wenn etwas unklar ist.

  • Du verfügst über gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

  • Du bringst eine positive, praktische Haltung und die Bereitschaft mit, Neues zu lernen.

  • Interesse an Technologie und KI-Tools, die effizientes Arbeiten unterstützen, ist ein Plus.

WAS WIR DIR BIETEN

  • Mitarbeit an spannenden, zukunftsorientierten und interdisziplinären Kundenprojekten

  • Ein kreatives, unterstützendes Team, das gemeinsam an Zielen arbeitet und voneinander lernt

  • Ein modernes Design-Büro am Rosenthaler Platz mit inspirierender Arbeitsumgebung

  • Gutschein-Benefits oder ein Firmen-Deutschlandticket für Festangestellte

  • Trainings- und Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten

ÜBER UNS

M+C Saatchi ist eine globale Agentur für Markenkommunikation, die unter dem Dach des weltweiten M+C Saatchi Netzwerks in London gegründet wurde. Heute zählt die Agentur mehr als 2.000 Mitarbeiter:innen, mit Büros unter anderem in Mailand, London, Sydney, Amsterdam, Kapstadt, New York, Los Angeles und Berlin. Zum Kernangebot gehören Markenstrategie, Kampagnen, PR & Influencer Relations, Sponsoring, Events & Brand Experience, Social Media sowie Content-Produktion. Mit dem M+C Saatchi Deutschland Team realisierte die Agentur in den letzten Jahren unter anderem Projekte für Peloton, The North Face, ING, Porsche, Porsche Design, Mercedes-Benz Vans, Nike, Ferrero, Heineken, WHOOP, UEFA, Riot Games und Volkswagen. Unser Ziel ist es, Kund:innen dabei zu unterstützen, wirkungsvolle 360°-Kommunikation zu schaffen, die ihre Zielgruppen begeistert.

Bereit, mit uns zu wachsen und praktische Finance-Erfahrung zu sammeln? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung!
