job.title: Retention Specialist, Risk
job.description:
Job Description


The Renewal Executive proactively manages a portfolio of customer renewals, serving as the primary customer contact throughout the renewal cycle. This role is accountable for timely, accurate renewal execution, customer retention, risk management, and identifying account growth opportunities. Operating at the TR5 level, the Renewal Executive handles complex and non-standard customer situations, uses data and insight-driven workflows to shape renewal strategy, and partners across Sales, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, Technology, Support, and Customer-to-Cash to deliver a consistent customer experience. 


Key Responsibilities 


Renewal Management and Retention 


  • Own the end-to-end renewal process for an assigned portfolio, proactively engaging customers within the renewal window and driving timely, accurate completion. 
  • Develop and execute account-specific renewal and retention strategies, including plans for complex, non-standard, or at-risk situations. 
  • Prepare and deliver quotes, contracts, and related documentation; coordinate approvals and ensure accurate processing through close. 
  • Maintain renewal pipeline, account status, customer commitments, and next steps in CRM and workflow tools; provide accurate input to forecasts and book-of-business reviews. 
  • Identify renewal risks early, determine root causes, recommend mitigation actions, and engage the appropriate internal partners or leaders when escalation is needed. 

Customer Relationships and Experience 


  • Build trusted customer relationships and serve as the primary point of contact for renewal, usage, billing, and general account-management questions. 
  • Communicate complex information clearly and adapt the approach to customer needs, seniority, and risk level. 
  • Coordinate the resolution of customer issues across internal teams, follow actions through to closure, and maintain a high standard of responsiveness. 
  • Gather, analyze, and synthesize customer feedback; share actionable insights to improve products, processes, and service delivery. 
  • Support onboarding, product education, webinars, and self-service adoption for accounts without assigned Customer Success coverage. 

Growth, Migration, and Value Selling 


  • Monitor account usage, customer needs, and business priorities to identify relevant upsell, cross-sell, product migration, and adoption opportunities. 
  • Use consultative and solution-selling techniques to connect product capabilities, including AI-enabled solutions, to measurable customer outcomes. 
  • Partner with Account Managers to validate customer needs, shape territory and account plans, develop value propositions, and progress opportunities to close. 
  • Leverage automated tools and insight-driven workflows, such as Gainsight, Salesforce, Certinia, and Next Best Action, to advance renewals and growth opportunities. 
  • Guide customers through product transitions by building a clear business case, addressing change concerns, and reinforcing the value of moving from legacy offerings to newer solutions. 

Analytics, Forecasting, and Operational Excellence 


  • Analyze customer, usage, renewal, and performance data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities and translate insights into action. 
  • Provide regular, accurate updates on renewal status, retention outlook, customer risk, and growth opportunities to Sales and management. 
  • Monitor key renewal, retention, customer experience, and operational metrics and take corrective action when performance is off track. 
  • Maintain high standards for document accuracy, data quality, task completion, and compliance with policies and contracting requirements. 

Leadership and Cross-Functional Contribution 


  • Mentor and support junior team members through knowledge sharing, training, and guidance on renewal and customer-management best practices; may act as a team lead. 
  • Lead or participate in global initiatives and projects that improve the Corporate customer experience, renewal performance, or operating model. 
  • Exercise sound judgment in complex situations, influence stakeholders, and coordinate across a highly matrixed environment. 

Required Qualifications 


  • University degree in Business, Finance, Communications, Law, Accounting, Marketing, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered. 
  • 3-6 years of experience in Customer Success, renewals, account management, sales, or a related customer-facing role; SaaS or technology experience preferred. 
  • Demonstrated experience managing a portfolio of renewals and addressing complex or non-standard customer situations. 
  • Experience identifying and progressing retention, upsell, cross-sell, migration, or adoption opportunities using consultative and value-selling approaches. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication, negotiation, analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills. 
  • Experience with CRM and customer workflow platforms such as Salesforce, Gainsight, or Certinia, plus proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. 
  • Ability to work effectively in a highly matrixed environment with Sales, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, Support, Technology, and Customer-to-Cash partners.

job.title: Legal Editor (HK Cases) - Primary Law Editorial
job.description:
Legal Editor (HK Cases) – Primary Law Editorial – Product Research


Job Description

Legal Editors are responsible for legal research, analysis, and writing to support the development and maintenance of Thomson Reuters’ legal information in all media. Members of this team are tasked with ensuring that published legal information contains and delivers premium legal content.

Legal Editors work collaboratively with colleagues in Asia, Australia, New Zealand and across the globe to ensure Thomson Reuters customers have access to the most accurate, current, and appropriately annotated versions of Hong Kong legislation, including Judicial, Legislative, Regulatory, and Court Rules materials in all media. Our Legal Editor (HK Cases) must have sound editorial judgment as they play a key role in ensuring the quality of our Editorial content.

Our Asia and Emerging Markets (AEM) Editorial team is hiring to fill three Legal Editor (HK Cases) roles in our Manila office. As a member of the AEM Editorial Manila team, you may read and analyze court decisions and classify the decision or short summaries of each point of law in the decision for Westlaw and print. Alternatively, you may be responsible for analyzing and assigning value to cases or legislation references cited by a judge in their reasons for judgment. Strong analytical and writing skills, productivity, and quality are necessary to maintain Thomson Reuters’ world class judicial content.


Key Responsibilities

  • Legal Research, Analysis, Validation, and Writing: Create and classify legal information in the form of classification, legislative and case relationships, and other features and enhancements. Identify key legal issues in editorial materials while demonstrating competence in Westlaw navigation and online research tools.
  • Editorial Responsibility: Adhere to editorial publishing schedules and quality standards. Verify your own work and that of other staff as required for accuracy and completeness, and ensure information is properly presented and organized. Maintain and develop legal knowledge and skills as needed, and stay current on legal trends and developments related to editorial responsibilities.
  • Individual and Leadership Development: Participate in team meetings and the employee evaluation process (including self-evaluation and giving and receiving feedback). Develop knowledge of Thomson Reuters Legal publications and products and those of competitors.
  • Self-direction: Prioritize your own work and understand the roles and responsibilities of each team member and how each role impacts production. Demonstrate competence on company-specific systems necessary to perform job functions.

Required Qualifications

  • Have a Juris Doctor or Bachelor of Laws degree or other equivalent, relevant legal training.
  • Are familiar with Hong Kong common law principles.
  • Are a self-starter with aptitude for legal research, writing, and analysis.
  • Have a keen eye for detail and established proofreading skills, and can pivot your attention to address high-priority updates on short notice.
  • Are an analytical thinker who uses logic and discretion to collaborate with global teammates to solve difficult problems where proofreading alone cannot establish accuracy.
  • Are decisive, with a focus on making quality decisions quickly.
  • Can interpret, analyze, organize, and communicate complex legal concepts.
  • Are comfortable with personal computers and familiar with word processing and online applications.
  • Can prioritize tasks and projects and pursue them with energy and drive.
  • Can work well as part of a global and collaborative team and community.
  • Are a strong, proactive, and assertive communicator who can speak and write clearly and effectively with all contacts, both in and outside Thomson Reuters, across the globe.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in legal publishing, editorial work, or legal research.
  • Familiarity with Hong Kong legislation and court materials.

job.title: Multimedia Editor (Training)
job.description:
Join our team at the Guardian and be a part of a diverse and inclusive global organisation that delivers fearless, investigative journalism, and holds power to account. Our team of award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial professionals, and industry-leading digital experts are committed to making a difference and represent a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We offer a challenging and exciting environment for career development, with a focus on training, growth and fostering an inclusive culture.

 

We are looking for a multimedia editor (training) to help build multimedia capability across our newsroom, in line with the Guardian’s Project Berger transformation. You’ll identify skills and development needs, design and deliver practical training, and work directly with journalists to help them create ambitious, engaging video and off-platform storytelling.

 

Combining hands-on video production expertise with coaching and mentoring, you’ll work directly with editors, reporters and production staff to develop their skills and confidence. You’ll provide practical support, tailor training to different levels of experience and help teams collaborate effectively with specialist multimedia producers. You’ll work closely with the Project Berger team throughout.

 

This is a 12-month fixed-term contract or staff secondment aligned to a 12-month training programme.

 

About the role

  • Work with journalists from predominantly text-based backgrounds to identify opportunities for ambitious and distinctive video/social storytelling, championing a visual, multi-format approach to our journalism.
  • Deliver practical, hands-on training, working directly with journalists to develop their multimedia skills, confidence and enthusiasm for video and off-platform journalism.
  • Support journalists to understand how to adapt stories and angles for different platforms, audiences and formats.
  • Help colleagues understand audience needs and behaviour across platforms, including the Guardian, YouTube, Instagram and TikTok.
  • Use audience data, feedback and learning evaluation to help assess what works and inform future training.
  • Support journalists and editors to understand how text, video, photography and graphics can work together to tell stories effectively.
  • Help colleagues develop practical production skills across a range of formats, including filming, editing, loops, carousels, headline cards and social graphics.
  • Work closely with other Guardian training teams and offices to ensure a coordinated approach to skills development, sharing expertise and avoiding duplication. Contribute to wider training programmes and masterclasses where required.

 

About you

  • Experience of designing, delivering or supporting training, coaching, mentoring or other learning and development activity.
  • Demonstrable experience of developing video stories and an understanding of how to structure compelling visual narratives for different platforms.
  • Ability to communicate technical and editorial concepts clearly to colleagues with different levels of experience.
  • Experience of creating video journalism for social platforms, including an understanding of different audience needs and behaviours.
  • Strong knowledge of video production equipment and editing and visual design tools, such as Adobe Premiere Pro and Figma.
  • Experience of video production, including practical filming, editing and working with contributors and presenters. 
  • Understanding of effective learning and development principles, including different learning styles and approaches.
  • Strong understanding of Guardian editorial standards, accuracy, verification, copyright and legal considerations relevant to video/social production.
  • Experience of managing projects, schedules and competing priorities.
  • Ideally, you’ll have a demonstrable ability to bring a diverse perspective to this role. 

 

We actively encourage applications from groups traditionally underrepresented in the UK media.

 

We operate in a hybrid environment working at least three days a week from our offices in King’s Cross in London.

 

The salary band for this role starts at £68,000, with the final offer determined by the successful candidate's skills, experience, and responsibilities.  

 

How to apply

To apply, please upload your latest CV and a cover letter which outlines why you’d love to take on this role, and why you’re a great match for what we’re looking for. 

We appreciate the time taken to prepare each application we receive. We do not use AI-assisted technology to review applications; every application is reviewed by a member of our recruitment team. 

 

The closing date for applications is Thursday 3rd December 2026.

 

All roles at the Guardian are open for everybody to apply. It is important to us that you feel supported and comfortable throughout your recruitment process, in order to perform your best. Please let us know if there are any changes we could make to help your application, this includes providing documents in accessible formats or personalising the process to better support your needs.

 

Benefits at the Guardian

You'll have six weeks of annual leave per year (plus bank holidays) with the option to purchase an additional 5 days. Our pension scheme is generous; if you contribute 5% then we will contribute 8-12% (depending on your age). We believe in giving back, which is why employees are given 2 volunteering days annually and the option of payroll giving. Season ticket loans are also available.

 

You are entitled to life cover, private healthcare, income protection, and eye tests. You can also opt in to dental insurance.

 

We have enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave policies in place. We also support our employees by offering an IVF, menopause, baby loss, and trans equality policy.

 

Culture and wellbeing

We want everyone to feel like they belong at the Guardian and we champion diversity of thought. Our various employee forums provide a platform to use their voice to foster an inclusive workplace. We became the first major media organisation to achieve B Corp status.

 

We offer tools to help you prioritise your wellbeing including access to our employee benefits platform which provides tailored support for health and wellbeing. In addition, we also offer free yoga and pilates classes. These run alongside our corporate gym membership and cycle to work scheme.

 

Our canteen has views overlooking the Regents Canal and caters for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

 

Learning and development

We encourage personal and professional growth. Employees have access to a broad range of tools and solutions, and we are happy to support the pursuit of professional qualifications through vocational courses and apprenticeships.

job.description:

Launching in November as an always-on series, new episodes will be released twice a week in video and audio formats on the Guardian’s website and platforms including YouTube and Spotify.

 

The video editor will shape the material into a polished, engaging and visually distinctive film, with a particular focus on pace, storytelling and editorial rhythm.

 

This is a 12-month fixed-term contract or staff secondment.

 

About the role

  • Develop a strong, coherent video narrative, creating the structure, selecting the strongest moments and creating the overall flow of the conversation.
  • Bring excellent editorial judgement and a strong instinct for sizzle cutting, pacing, rhythm, hooks and moments that capture and sustain audience attention.
  • Shape the material into a compelling, polished piece that feels premium and editorially distinctive, while preserving the integrity and substance of the interview and is engaging to a YouTube-first audience.
  • Review and organise supplied footage, audio, project files and supporting assets, ensuring an efficient and well-managed editing workflow.
  • Attend shoots where necessary, working with the producer to start an edit plan while recording
  • Work in Adobe Premiere Pro, maintaining an organised, efficient and technically sound workflow, including appropriate media management, sequences and timelines.
  • Use Adobe After Effects and supplied GFX templates as required, adapting and integrating graphics, titles, captions and other visual treatments into the edit.
  • Undertake audio post-production, including dialogue clean-up, balancing levels and reducing distracting noise where possible, then deliver a clean, consistent final mix.
  • Maintain clear communication with the producer and executive producer, respond constructively to feedback and manage the work efficiently to meet the agreed deadline.

 

About you

  • Demonstrable experience editing long-form YouTube content, documentaries, video podcasts, interviews or other editorially driven digital video.
  • A strong portfolio showcasing storytelling, sizzle cutting, pace, narrative structure and editorial rhythm.
  • Excellent working knowledge of Adobe Premiere Pro, including offline editing, media organisation, timeline management, project handover and export workflows.
  • Working knowledge of Adobe After Effects, with the ability to use supplied templates and integrate motion graphics into an edit.
  • Experience working with interview or conversation-led material and shaping longer conversations into compelling, well-paced viewing experiences.
  • An understanding of YouTube-first content, audience retention, effective openings and the importance of maintaining visual engagement across longer-form films.
  • Experience using B-roll, cutaways, graphics, captions and other visual devices to support storytelling and add texture to interview footage.
  • A good understanding of online finishing, quality control, export settings, codecs, resolutions, frame rates and delivery specifications.
  • Knowledge of digital accessibility best practice for video and audio content, such as accurate captions and transcripts, audio description, and accessible on-screen text and graphics (e.g. WCAG guidelines).
  • Experience working with producers and incorporating editorial feedback under tight turnaround times.

Through our music division, AEG Presents, one of the world’s leading operators of tours, concerts, and music festivals, we help shape the sound of now. We work with artists at every stage of their careers to bring live music to life, connecting artists with fans on stages around the world.

Headquartered in Los Angeles, AEG Presents is driven by creativity, innovation, and purpose, and powered by people who want their work to show up in the real world.

If you’re ready to help create moments that matter, there’s a place for you here. Because it happens here.

The DevOps Manager is responsible for leading and coaching DevOps / Platform Engineers in the maintenance, uptime, monitoring, and automation of our applications and systems. You will design and deliver software to improve availability, performance, and efficiency, your goal will be eliminating manual tasks, evaluating designs, and providing feedback to internal and external teams on how to build the most robust software platforms possible. job.title: Singapore Correspondent
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

 

Our commitment to inclusion and fairness

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI. 

 

The Role

The Financial Times is seeking a Singapore Correspondent to cover one of the world’s most important financial centres. Normally operating solo - although in close cooperation with the SE Asia correspondent and the finance team around the world - the role covers everything from investment banks to oil trading and local politics. For an enterprising reporter, the scope is considerable.

Singapore has evolved into one of Asia’s main financial hubs and a global centre for commodity trading. All the dealmaking is of core interest to the FT, as are the numerous entrepreneurs and family offices - most especially from China - that have set up shop. The city-state attracts its share of colourful characters and dubious behaviour: from the collapse of Barings to the Wirecard scandal, significant parts of the action were in Singapore.

The city is not just a centre for making deals; it is an important player itself. Temasek and GIC are role models for many of the world’s sovereign wealth funds and their activity is another important source of stories. Singapore’s much-admired social model, and the tensions that exist in Singaporean society nonetheless, often interest the outside world.

The Singapore correspondent also has responsibility for Malaysia, which is enjoying a resurgence in the semiconductor industry, and charting an independent course in regional geopolitics. There may also be opportunities to cover stories elsewhere in SE Asia, especially when following supply chains and deals that pass through Singapore.

News is the heart of the job - and you will find strong demand from FT editors - but we want and expect the correspondent to write across a range of formats, from sharp analysis to magazine features. There will be opportunities for travel. Singapore is an important venue for FT Live and you will be asked to represent the FT at events. 

Your Skills

The core of the job is writing and reporting. You will have solid experience as a journalist, most likely in financial reporting or as a foreign correspondent, with a demonstrated ability to cultivate sources and break news. You should be able to write for all parts of the website and newspaper, from strong spot news to deft analysis on a range of subjects.

You will be motivated and full of ideas for stories, not just waiting for the news to arrive. Good communication skills are important. You should regularly pitch ideas to editors in Hong Kong and deliver copy when promised. You should also be collegiate: forging a close relationship with FT correspondents across the region will be crucial to your success.

Singapore is one of the world’s wealthiest cities and a comfortable place to live. The reporting environment, however, requires a degree of resilience and diplomacy. The state maintains tight control over the local media. Some information may not be publicly announced or readily available, requiring a correspondent to work hard and keep up their sources in order to stay in the game.

 

Please submit your application by the end of the day, Thursday 3rd December 2026.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

job.description:
INTERNSHIP DETAILS 

 

SPRING INTERNSHIP 

APPLICATION DEADLINE FOR STUDENTS: 11/20/2026 

SPRING INTERNSHIP PROGRAM DATES: 1/11/2027 – 4/16/2027  

*The Songwriters & Composers Wing Intern position pays county/state minimum wage rates, based on work location. 

 

 

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

 

The Recording Academy Songwriters & Composers Wing is seeking a “rock star” student for a spring 2027 Internship with our team. 


Celebrating music through the Grammy® Awards, The Recording Academy continues its legacy as the premier national organization for honoring achievements in the recording arts and supporting the music community. As a membership organization, we represent the most talented music professionals in the world. Our members include recording artists, producers, engineers, attorneys, music supervisors, composers/arrangers, managers, agents, social media and record label executives and many others. 


Our paid Internship Program offers a unique opportunity for full-time college students (juniors or seniors) to gain on-site training in office administration, events management and artist relations, in exchange for college credit. Candidates should be energetic, hard-working and have aspirations of a career in the music industry. 

 

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

 

  • Internship duration is for a semester (12 weeks or equivalent). 
  • Hours are part-time (20-24 hours a week). 
  • Intern will work with the chapter office on local events during regular business hours as well as some evenings and weekends. 
  • Internship will provide in-depth exposure to professional recording industry techniques and practices. 
  • Projects may include assistance with event management, educational programs, newsletters, membership recruitment, database management, demographics analysis, and administrative office support. 

 

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE  

 

  • Currently enrolled in a college/university. One year of course work towards degree in related field is preferred. 
  • Letter from school stating that intern will receive college credit for the Recording Academy internship. 
  • Display an interest in music and commitment to a career in the recording industry. 
  • Possess strong verbal, written and analytical skills. 
  • Exhibit proficient computer skills. 
  • Be a junior, senior or graduate student. 


PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAIN ROLES:   

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.   


While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, and sit for long periods of time, and work at a computer for long periods of time. The employee will be required to lift and/or move up to 60 pounds.   

 

 

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES 

 

RECORDING ACADEMY 

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators. 

 

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY 

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation. 

 

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION 

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives. 

 

MUSICARES 

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs. 

 

GRAMMY MUSEUM 

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include GRAMMY in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States. 

 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY 

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. The Recording Academy will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship to the Recording Academy. This policy governs all aspects of employment, including selection, job assignment, compensation, promotion, discipline, termination, access to benefits and training, recruitment, hiring, transfer, and social and recreational programs.

job.title: Intern, MusiCares Research & Wellness in Music
job.description:
INTERNSHIP DETAILS  

  

SPRING INTERNSHIP  

APPLICATION DEADLINE FOR STUDENTS: 11/20/2026  

SPRING INTERNSHIP PROGRAM DATES: 1/11/2027 – 4/16/2027   

*The MusiCares Research & Wellness in Music Intern position pays county/state minimum wage rates, based on work location.  

  

  

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR  

  

Since 1989, MusiCares, the philanthropic affiliate of the Recording Academy, has been the largest safety net for everyone who works in music. MusiCares has provided over $145 million in assistance to music people across all professions for basic living needs, medical care, mental health, substance use treatment and disaster relief. In recent years, recognizing critical gaps in evidence, MusiCares has begun investing in research, both internally and through partners, to inform our programming and the industry more broadly.  

 

MusiCares is seeking an undergraduate or graduate-level intern to support two key areas of our research efforts: developing our research strategy and our Wellness in Music survey.  

 

This is a remote position, and the selected individual may choose to work from MusiCares’s offices in Santa Monica or New York City, if located in those cities and preferred. 

 

  

WHAT YOU'LL DO  

  

Wellness in Music Survey Support: 

 

In 2020, MusiCares launched our Wellness in Music survey, an annual survey examining the financial, health and mental wellbeing of people in music. The survey has grown to be a formative set of data to inform MusiCares and the music community on key issues affecting this population.  

Each spring, MusiCares launches the survey through our network of thousands of individuals and across social media, and later completes analysis to identify key findings and trends. As part of this effort, MusiCares compiles and amplifies these findings through media outreach. In 2027, we will be taking the opportunity to refine the survey to improve the depth and quality of data captured.  

 

Responsibilities include:  

 

  • Refine and update the Wellness in Music survey, taking into account MusiCares’s data needs, available external data, and gaps in industry information. 
  • Partner with the ED and VP, HHS to define an analysis plan. 
  • Collaborate with the MusiCares team to disseminate the survey through our network and on social media. 
  • Conduct analysis, per the defined analysis plan. 
  • Support the development of messaging for external dissemination. 

 

Research Strategy Assessment and Design Support (approximately 4 weeks): 

 

  • Conduct a detailed review of existing research and data on the health and wellbeing of music people and compile into key findings. 
  • Identify key trends in emerging research, as well as critical gaps in our understanding. 
  • Collaborate with the Health and Human Services team to understand areas in which research and evidence could better inform their programs. 
  • Support the development of an organizational research strategy.

job.title: Education & Community Engagement Manager
job.description:
This is a hybrid position. Applicants must reside in the Tri-State Area to be on location for occasional programming and meetings.



WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 

The Education and Community Engagement Manager supports the development, implementation, and refinement of Grammy Museum Education & Community Engagement programs with a focus on educator-facing initiatives, curriculum development, professional development, student recruitment, and regional program support. Based in New York City, you will help expand the Museum’s East Coast education presence and support programs primarily East of the Mississippi River including Grammy in the Schools, professional development sessions, and seasonal Grammy Camp support.

 

You will provide curriculum expertise across programs to ensure consistency, continuity, and alignment with the Museum’s educational goals. You will build and maintain relationships with K-12 teachers, school partners, districts, and arts education organizations to support educator engagement, student recruitment, and professional development. You will also support application and recruitment processes for student and educator programs, ensuring outreach, application review, and participant communication reflect program goals and expand access for students and teachers.

 

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 

Professional Development & Educator Engagement

  • Lead planning, development, and facilitation of educator professional development programs, including virtual, in-person, district-based, and conference-based sessions.
  • Build and maintain relationships with K–12 teachers, school districts, arts coordinators, and education partners to support professional development, program participation, student recruitment, and ongoing educator engagement.
  • Identify and cultivate professional development opportunities with schools, districts, conferences, and partner organizations.
  • Collect and synthesize educator feedback to inform future professional development offerings, curriculum tools, and program improvements.

 

Program Alignment

  • Provide curriculum expertise across Education programs to ensure consistency, continuity, and alignment with departmental learning goals, while remaining adaptable to different student, teacher, and community contexts.
  • Develop and refine learning objectives, instructional materials, rubrics, classroom extensions, and develop and maintain program manuals.
  • Support alignment of programs with music education, arts education, career and technical education, college/career readiness, and workforce development frameworks where appropriate.
  • Collaborate with internal team members to connect curriculum and instructional design across Grammy Camp, Grammy in the Schools, Industry Sessions, professional development, and other education initiatives.

 

Recruitment, Applications & Program Process Support

  • Support recruitment for student and educator programs including outreach to schools, teachers, districts, community partners, and professional networks, building an application pipeline.
  • Support application and review processes for selected programs, including outreach, applicant communication, submission tracking, rubric development, review coordination, and documentation.
  • Help ensure recruitment and application processes are accessible, organized, and aligned with program goals, student readiness, educator needs, and equity of access.
  • Collaborate with the Coordinator and program leads to maintain accurate applicant records, support review timelines, and communicate next steps to applicants and participants.

 

Grammy in the Schools Support

  • Support planning and implementation of Grammy in the Schools programs, particularly those based on the East Coast and primarily East of the Mississippi River.
  • Assist with educator and school partner communication, program planning, instructional materials, and on-site implementation.
  • Collaborate with team members to ensure Grammy in the Schools programming is educationally consistent, student-centered, and aligned with the Museum’s broader learning goals.
  • Support development of program resources that help students connect music learning to industry pathways, creative careers, and transferable skills.

 

Grammy Camp Support

  • Support Grammy Camp planning and implementation including curriculum alignment, faculty support, student learning outcomes, and summer travel for on-site program delivery.
  • Support faculty onboarding, curriculum implementation, instructional planning, and integration of curriculum benchmarks across the camp model.
  • Help ensure consistency across camp cities while supporting local adaptation based on partners, faculty, students, and facilities.

 

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with the Vice President, Senior Director, Senior Manager, and Coordinator to support program strategy, planning, implementation, and evaluation.
  • Collaborate with Marketing, Communications, Advancement, Production, Guest Services, and Finance as needed.
  • Support public programs in New York as needed.
  • Represent the Education & Community Engagement team in meetings with schools, districts, partners, artists, faculty, and external stakeholders.
  • Travel for programs, conferences, partner meetings, Grammy Camp, Grammy in the Schools and other education initiatives as needed.
  SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s degree required. Master’s degree preferred in music education, arts education, curriculum and instruction, education, music industry, or a related field.
  • 3-5+ years of experience in music education, arts education, curriculum development, professional development, or youth program implementation.
  • Experience designing or facilitating professional development for educators preferred.
  • Strong understanding of secondary music education, music technology, ensemble instruction, career-connected learning, and/or music industry pathways.
  • Experience developing curriculum, lesson plans, educator resources, rubrics, or instructional materials.
  • Experience supporting student or educator recruitment and application review processes preferred.
  • Ability to build relationships and collaborate with educators, students, artists, K-12 schools, districts, partners, and internal teams.
  • Strong writing, facilitation, and presentation skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple programs and timelines.
  • Willingness and ability to travel including significant summer travel to support Grammy Camp.

job.title: Mgr, Software Engineering - Realtor.com
job.description:
Mgr, Software Engineering - Realtor.com Mgr, Software Engineering Realtor.com Austin, TX Apply NowSign Up for Job Alerts Return to search results Mgr, Software Engineering Location: Austin, TX, United States Category: Technology Job ID: 3445 Apply Now Description Recognized as the No. 1 site trusted by real estate professionals, Realtor.com® has been at the forefront of online real estate for over 25 years, connecting buyers, sellers, and renters with trusted insights and expert guidance to find their perfect home. Through its robust suite of tools, Realtor.com® not only makes a significant impact on the real estate industry at large, but for consumers, navigating the biggest purchase they will make in their life, by providing a user

experience

that is easy to use, easy to understand, and most of all, easy to make decisions. Join us on our mission to empower more people to find their way home by breaking barriers to entry, making the right connections, and building confidence through expert guidance.

About the Role

Every visit to realtor.com passes through our edge before it reaches anything else. As Manager, Engineering for Edge Security and Delivery, you'll lead the team that owns that front door: DNS, CDN and edge routing, web application firewalls, bot defense, and DDoS protection for one of the most visited real estate sites in the US. You'll inherit an experienced team of edge engineers, grow it with new hires, and lead the shift from protection added case by case to an edge that is secure by default. You'll report to the Director of Edge Security and Traffic Engineering and work closely with product, data, security, and platform teams across the company. Top Reasons to Apply: Own the front door for a top real estate marketplace, serving billions of requests a month across hundreds of CDN distributions. Build, not just maintain: the role comes with a mandate and approved headcount to stand up a secure-by-default edge program. See your impact in the business. Bot traffic shapes audience metrics, lead quality, and ad revenue, so the team's work shows up in numbers leadership watches. Lead a small, senior team with clear ownership and few handoffs. Join an engineering org that is serious about AI-assisted engineering, with the tools and support to use it well.

What You'll Do

Lead, coach, and grow a team of about 5 engineers today, growing to about 7. Hire to a high bar, write development plans, and handle performance constructively. Own the roadmap for edge security and delivery: CDN, edge routing and compute, WAF, bot management, DDoS protection, and origin protection standards. Make protection the default. Every new public page, API, and distribution should launch covered, enforced through CI checks and launch review rather than follow-up tickets. Run the bot defense program. Deliver one bot signal shared with audience measurement, ads, leads, and sign-in, and balance stopping bad traffic against blocking real customers. Cut detection time. Build the observability that lets engineering spot edge attacks and misconfigurations in minutes, not weeks. Set edge standards for product teams that own their own origins, and review the launches that cross the edge. Own operational excellence for a Tier 1 path: on-call, incident response, postmortems with real follow-through, and change management. Manage edge vendors and spend: CDN, WAF, and bot management contracts, renewals, and cost per request. Drive AI adoption on the team and measure whether it actually improves outcomes. What You'll Bring: 2+ years managing software or infrastructure engineers, including hiring and performance management. 7+ years of engineering experience, with depth in at least one of: CDN and edge delivery, web application security, bot and abuse mitigation, or large-scale traffic engineering. Hands-on credibility with AWS edge services (CloudFront, Lambda@Edge or CloudFront Functions, AWS WAF, Shield, Route 53) or equivalents such as Akamai, Fastly, or Cloudflare. A strong grasp of HTTP, TLS, DNS, and caching, plus the OWASP Top 10 and common abuse patterns such as scraping, credential stuffing, and form spam. job.description:
Who we are:

Burson, part of WPP, is the global communications leader built to create value for clients through reputation. With highly specialized teams, industry-leading technologies and breakthrough creative, we help brands and businesses redefine reputation as a competitive advantage so they can lead today and into the future. When you work at Burson, you are part of a global community of lifelong learners who thrive at the edge of innovation.

WPP (LSE/NYSE: WPP) is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com 

For more information visit bursonglobal.com and follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

More about the role:

Burson Buchanan is a boutique advisory firm within the Burson Group, focused on financial communications, litigation and government investigations, and crisis and risk management. Buchanan advises corporate clients, investment firms and organizations on stakeholder engagement and reputation management through moments of transformation, complexity, and opportunity. Our team leverages decades of experience navigating high-stakes matters, while integrating Burson's proprietary technology and insights, enabling us to deliver strategic advisory for the intelligence era. 

Burson Buchanan is seeking a highly driven Associate to support client engagements across capital markets situations, litigation, and high-stakes issues management. This role is ideal for a rising strategic communicator with experience working on sensitive, business-critical challenges for clients.

The Associate will work closely with Buchanan team members on multi-faceted programs involving crisis response, high-profile litigation, and major capital markets events including M&A, IPOs and activist defense. They’ll have a front-row seat and opportunity to shape the most critical and high-profile challenges facing companies today.

The right candidate will bring a fast, focused approach to every engagement. They’ll stay responsive around the clock to clients and colleagues, get up to speed quickly on each client, and take pride in producing polished deliverables under pressure. Above all, they’ll thrive in a close-knit team and enjoy contributing meaningfully in a fast-paced, collaborative, and high-performance environment.

What you'll do:

Litigation & Issues Management

  • Support the development and execution of communications and stakeholder engagement strategies for crisis, litigation, government investigations, policy matters, and corporate reputation challenges.
  • Conduct research, rapid situational analysis and synthesize findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Assist in message development, positioning, and scenario planning for sensitive issues affecting corporate operations and leadership.
  • Draft press releases, statements, talking points, key messages, and media background materials.

Financial & Investor Communications

  • Contribute to financial communications programs, including the development of stakeholder communications materials related to M&A, IPOs, shareholder activism, and quarterly earnings.
  • Conduct research on market trends, investor sentiment, and peer positioning to support strategic recommendations.
  • Assist in preparing materials for interactions with analysts, shareholders, and financial media.

Client Engagement & Account Management

  • Serve as a core member of Buchanan client teams, supporting ongoing project management.
  • Support senior leadership in the development of briefings, memos, media materials, Q&A documents and client-facing research.
  • Help coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure seamless execution and strong client service.

Media Engagement & Issues Tracking

  • Support proactive and reactive media engagement for corporate, financial, and crisis-related matters.
  • Lead media monitoring efforts on client engagements, tracking notable developments, and delivering impactful insights.

Experience that contributes to success:

  • 1-2 years of experience in public affairs, corporate communications, financial communications, or public relations—agency or in-house.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting clients on issues such as litigation, government investigations, crisis and reputational management, policy/public affairs, and corporate financial events (e.g. M&A, IPOs, shareholder activism situations).
  • The ability to prepare quality client-facing materials under compressed timelines.
  • Ability to think critically, analyze complex information, and anticipate risks and opportunities.
  • Excellent verbal communication skills and comfort interacting with senior leaders.
  • Proactive, organized, and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.

Preferred:

  • Experience with financial research tools including platforms such as the Bloomberg Terminal, AlphaSense, and Capital IQ.
  • Understanding of capital markets, investor relations and financial media engagement.
  • Familiarity with litigation and regulatory communications.
  • Prior agency experience strongly preferred.

Our vision is for Burson to be the leading ‘academy company’ for creative communications professionals and emerging leaders. We provide a dynamic environment where ambitious colleagues come to elevate their skills, expand their networks, and ultimately, produce the best solutions for today’s leading brands. Our commitment to your growth is reflected in our robust benefits and people programs, which include professional development opportunities, mentorship programs with industry leaders, a vibrant and inclusive company culture fostering collaboration and innovation and packages designed to reward and retain top talent. We invest in our people because we believe their success is our success.

At Burson, we’re an agency of learn-it-alls. We recognize that the things we do best, creativity and communications, require a level of nuanced understanding. job.title: Executive
job.description:
Opportunity

Are you an ambitious graduate or early-career professional looking to make a mark in the advisory world? Brunswick Group is looking for a talented Executive to join our Stockholm office.
Brunswick Group advises companies, institutions, and organizations across the Nordics on communication and stakeholder engagement.

We help our clients build and protect their reputations, manage change, and communicate effectively with investors, employees, customers, and other stakeholders. Our work spans both day-to-day communications and critical moments, including major corporate and financial milestones such as mergers, acquisitions, IPOs, as well as complex reputational and regulatory challenges.

As an Executive at Brunswick, you will support client teams with timely news updates, research and analysis of business, financial markets, media and political developments. You will develop a deep understanding of our clients' businesses and help ensure the smooth running of client projects and accounts. You will learn from experienced advisers and take on increasing responsibility as you develop your skills.

About the Role

As an Executive at Brunswick, you will contribute to client engagements, working alongside experienced advisers. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:

  • Monitoring client, competitor and market developments in real time, identifying material issues and ensuring timely escalation to internal teams and clients.
  • Producing concise, high-quality briefings and alerts that distil complex information into clear, actionable insight.
  • Conducting rigorous qualitative and quantitative research to inform client strategy and positioning.
  • Supporting the effective management of client mandates by tracking workstreams, drafting meeting notes and developing clear action plans.
  • Preparing detailed reporter backgrounders and targeted media lists to support engagement strategies.
  • Analysing media coverage, stakeholder sentiment and broader industry trends to identify risks and opportunities.
  • Contributing to competitive and peer analysis to inform clients’ strategic decision-making.
  • Coordinating logistics for stakeholder meetings, announcement days and other critical moments, ensuring seamless execution and close attention to detail.
  • Building a strong understanding of clients’ sectors, stakeholder landscapes and the broader policy and market environment, while beginning to develop an external professional network.

 

What We're Looking For

At Brunswick, we seek ambitious individuals who are dedicated to learning and professional growth. In addition to considering experience, we value potential, strong work ethic, analytical thinking, and excellent written and verbal communications skills. Standout candidates demonstrate the following:

  • A keen interest in financial and business matters; understanding of financial terminology is an advantage.
  • Interest in and understanding of business strategy.
  • Recent graduate or 1–2 years’ experience in a professional setting.
  • Awareness of current and relevant global issues.
  • Strong analytical, strategic thinking and problem-solving ability.
  • Strong research, writing and communication skills.
  • Ability to operate effectively in an entrepreneurial, fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to prioritise competing tasks while maintaining close attention to detail.
  • Excellent written and spoken proficiency in a Nordic language, alongside fluent English.

Why Join Us

At Brunswick, we believe that business and enterprise can be great positive forces in the world. Our mission is to help our clients succeed, fulfil their potential and play their most positive and effective role in society. This ambition is reflected in the people we hire, the work we do and the high standards we set across our global firm.

Joining Brunswick early in your career offers the opportunity to work on some of the most interesting and complex challenges facing businesses today. You will gain exposure to a diverse range of clients and industries, take on responsibility early and learn from experienced advisers across our global network of offices. With no two days the same, Brunswick offers a collaborative environment where you can continuously develop your skills and build a strong foundation for your career.

Alongside professional development opportunities, we offer a range of benefits supporting your financial wellbeing, health, family and community.

 

About Brunswick

Brunswick is a global advisory firm. We help companies tackle high-stakes issues, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, and deliver high-impact outcomes. 

Our clients value our ability to anticipate, shape, and respond to the key players and forces in the financial and investment arena, regulatory and geopolitical universe, NGO community, workforce and beyond. They rely on us for deep experience, fresh perspectives and original thinking. So, in Brunswick you will find an exceptional range of experience and talent with a rich mix of backgrounds. From the beginning, we have prioritized attracting, developing, and retaining the best professionals in the industry, united by a culture of inclusivity, excellence, and intellectual curiosity.

Founded in 1987 in London, the firm has organically grown to 27 offices in 18 countries across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia and Australia. We operate as a “one-firm firm” with no individual profit centers. This allows us to assemble fully integrated, bespoke teams for each client, able to draw on the full resources of Brunswick anywhere in the world. 

 

Brunswick is an equal opportunity employer.  All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law. Please read our Global Privacy Notice to understand how your data is managed.

job.description:

The Head of FinOps is a Senior Leadership role within the Business Platform Delivery Organisation accountable for WPP’s end-to-end FinOps capability, covering cloud and SaaS spend management, cost allocation, forecasting, optimisation, recharges and Ttechnology Support. The role leads the FinOps team as the primary point of support for cost visibility, reporting, recharge management, user guidance, and platform access across OpCos, projects and clusters.

Working closely with budget holders, the Cloud Hub, platform teams, ET Finance, and Procurement, the role will strengthen financial governance, improve spend transparency, resolve cost and recharge-related challenges, and embed FinOps best practices into Enterprise Technology decision-making. FinOps Strategy, Governance & Leadership

FinOps Platform & Product Ownership

Why we're hiring:

The Threat Hunter is responsible for proactively identifying advanced threats that evade traditional security controls. This role involves hypothesis-driven investigations, leveraging threat intelligence, and analyzing telemetry across endpoints, networks, and cloud environments to uncover stealthy adversary activity. The Threat Hunter plays a critical role in reducing dwell time and strengthening organizational resilience under the Autonomic Security Operations model.

What you'll be doing:

Proactive Threat Hunting

  • Execute hypothesis-driven hunts based on adversary TTPs and threat intelligence.
  • Analyze telemetry from SIEM, EDR/XDR, NDR, and cloud-native platforms to identify anomalies.
  • Develop and maintain hunting queries and scripts for automation and repeatability.
  • Validate detection coverage through purple team exercises and adversary emulation.

Threat Intelligence Integration

  • Incorporate emerging threat intelligence into hunting hypotheses and detection pipelines.
  • Maintain awareness of global threat actor tactics, techniques, and procedures (MITRE ATT&CK).

Continuous Improvement

  • Document hunt findings and feed insights into detection engineering and SOC workflows.
  • Maintain a backlog of hunting hypotheses and visibility gaps for remediation.
  • Contribute to automation of hunting workflows using scripting and SOAR platforms.

Strategic Alignment to GCAT SOC10x

  • 10X People: Continuous learning and knowledge sharing within the team.
  • 10X Process: Embed agile, hypothesis-driven hunting workflows.
  • 10X Technology: Leverage AI/ML analytics for anomaly detection and hunt acceleration.
  • 10X Visibility: Ensure comprehensive telemetry ingestion across hybrid environments.
  • 10X Speed: Reduce dwell time and accelerate detection-to-response cycles.

 

What you'll need:

Technical Expertise

  • Strong knowledge of threat hunting methodologies and frameworks (MITRE ATT&CK, TaHiTI).
  • Proficiency in SIEM, EDR/XDR, and log aggregation tools across hybrid infrastructure.
  • Scripting skills (Python, PowerShell) for automation and data analysis.
  • Familiarity with threat intelligence integration and behavioral analytics.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Ability to work closely with SOC, IR, and engineering teams.
  • Skilled in documenting hunt outcomes and communicating findings effectively.

Certifications (Preferred)

  • GIAC GCTI, GCIH, or equivalent advanced security certifications.

Key Attributes

  • Automation-first mindset with focus on scalability and resilience.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication and teamwork capabilities.

Why we're hiring:

Lead the end-to-end Business Support function for WPP Production, ensuring reliable 24/7 support across front-line application support, client-facing digital support and technology service management. The role owns the support operating model from initial demand and L1 triage through L2 service ownership and escalation to L3 engineering, vendors or managed service providers. It is accountable for establishing, maturing and owning the Service Introduction capability, alongside service governance, operational readiness and acceptance, platform stability, stakeholder communication and continual improvement. Working side by side with Product, Engineering and DevSecOps, the role will address the current Service Introduction capability gap by creating a consistent, proportionate and risk-based approach through which frequent product change, major releases and increasingly complex integrations transition efficiently into BAU support. The role also provides governance and performance oversight for managed service providers, including alignment of service-introduction and acceptance requirements.

What you'll be doing:

KRA 1: Service Leadership and Operational Performance
• Set and lead the 24/7 support strategy, service model and operating structure across retained and managed service teams, with clear escalation routes to L3 engineering and suppliers.
• Ensure demand received through service management channels is understood, categorised, prioritised, resolved or routed appropriately, with clear ownership and communication through to closure.
• Maintain a responsive, SLA-driven service for internal teams and client agencies, minimising disruption and ensuring support interactions are clear, structured and professional.

KRA 2: Service Introduction, Transition and Operational Readiness
• Establish, mature and own the Service Introduction and support-acceptance capability for new and changed services, addressing the current capability gap and ensuring changes transition efficiently into BAU support.
• Design, implement and continuously improve proportionate, risk-based Service Introduction and operational-readiness criteria for incremental product change, major releases, new platforms and complex integrations.
• Work with Product, Engineering, DevSecOps, delivery teams and service providers early in the lifecycle so support requirements, dependencies, monitoring, documentation, knowledge transfer and escalation models are established before release.
• Ensure service-introduction and operational-readiness requirements align with the acceptance standards of relevant managed service providers, including Kyndryl where applicable.
• Establish clear ownership and support models for end-to-end integrations that span applications, engineering teams, suppliers and service providers.

KRA 3: Service Governance, Stability and Risk
• Define and maintain service governance, support structures, change enablement, path-to-production and regular service reviews, with clear boundaries between delivery ownership and support acceptance.
• Safeguard the health, reliability, scalability and long-term stability of business-critical workflow, production and digital platforms through monitoring, maintenance, upgrades and production control.
• Ensure releases and changes are operationally ready and followed by appropriate validation and service-health checks.
• Ensure appropriate processes for user access, permissions, password resets and application licence administration, including coordination with service providers where required.

KRA 4: Incident, Problem and Escalation Management

• Support effective commercial and performance governance of managed service providers and suppliers.

KRA 9: Cross-functional Alignment

job.title: Senior Strategist, Brand & Experience Strategy
job.description:
Job Description:

About Dentsu Creative

Business-Driven and Creatively Obsessed. We are dedicated to helping our clients achieve growth. We understand the challenge of standing out in an increasingly competitive marketplace. We recognize that experiences are becoming indistinguishable across industries, and new technologies can both enable creativity and risk commoditization. In this context, the need for a distinct competitive edge is crucial. We believe that embracing creativity is key for sustainable business growth. However, the conventional definition of creativity will not suffice. Our view on creativity goes beyond norms; it’s not just how we execute, but a mindset that permeates our organization and our clients’ businesses. We call it Transformative Creativity. It’s outcome-focused creativity unleashed to solve business problems. This unique brand of creativity sets us apart and drives our clients to success.


About Our Strategists

We’re Proactive Leaders. Great strategists are proactive and take the initiative to lead teams and clients with new ideas and provocative thoughts. We get ahead of the ask, anticipating the next step and setting the agenda with the energy and optimism it takes to ensure that our work is fresh, our clients feel our partnership, and the team stays ahead of the curve and delivers exceptional ideas.


We Challenge the Status Quo. Our strategists take pride in challenging the status quo, always seeking fresh angles and leading with innovative ideas. We push past right, to find what is interesting. We challenge assumptions. We generate the energy and enthusiasm needed to help our teams and clients find the next level in an ever-evolving world, embodying a challenger mindset.


We’re Makers and Doers. At every level, from CSO to junior planner, our strategists are makers who take pride in creating things, not just managing projects. We hold ourselves to a high standard of creation, putting hands on keyboards and turning ideas into tangible outputs, fostering a culture of hands-on involvement and tangible creativity that make ideas in our heads a reality in the world.


We Cherish a Growth Mindset. We value and fuel a growth mindset, encouraging our strategists to be their best and embrace feedback that challenges their thinking and actions. Our culture is hard on the work but kind to our people, recognizing that personal growth is key to our agency’s success.


We’re Radical Collaborators. We are radically collaborative, working fluidly across teams and skill sets with the outcome in mind, not personal egos. Our strategists know that together we are stronger, actively seeking others’ input to solve problems and elevate the work, fostering a culture of collective excellence.


Role Overview

As a Sr. Strategist, Brand Experience Strategy, you will report to the Group Director, Brand Experience Strategy. You will join a team of smart, creative strategists shaping how spirits, alcohol, and non-alcohol brands come to life across retail, restaurant and bar, entertainment, digital, social, experiential and trade. You lead day-to-day strategy on assigned accounts, keep pulse on leading market and consumer trends, turn insight into go-to-market plans, and partner closely with Account, Creative and Analytics teams to make sure great strategy becomes great work in market. 

  • Support strategy leads to create and drive experience strategies, programs and go-to-market plans that both inspire and drive business for our clients
  • Synthesize signals across data, culture, and category to provide teams a clear point of view – not just information, but interpretation and impact on what we need to do.
  • Develop clear, inspiring, evidence-based briefs, POVs, brand and program frameworks, and consumer journeys
  • Lead smaller strategy projects on assigned accounts, projects, and deliverables with minimal oversight
  • Acts as an inspirational and strategic catalyst for our cross-disciplined team of account management, creative, analytics, technology, and production
  • Build strong knowledge of the spirits industry and competitive landscape
  • Uses AI to accelerate research synthesis, pressure-test hypotheses and sharpen output quality – keeping human judgment at the forefront as a clear, defensible strategic point of view at the center of every recommendation.

 

Qualifications

  • 4+ years developing integrated brand strategies, with some experiential, events, shopper or retail-strategy (or equivalent) experience
  • Experience in the spirits/alcoholic beverage category preferred; experience in other beverage or CPG categories will also be considered
  • Acts as a catalyst to creative, media, data, account and other brand teams in finding new ways to add value to brand experiences and identifying future opportunities
  • Demonstrates the maturity and leadership to be a key player on a collaborative, multi-disciplinary cross-agency tea
  • Demonstrates proficiency in using and translating all types of data into insights that drive creative thinking and client growth
  • Proactively seeks out opportunities to make the work better in a collaborative way
  • Has a passion for solving problems and is comfortable using AI as a tool to work faster and sharpen thinking
  • Has built strong relationships with middle-level team members and clients, earning their trust and respect
  • Demonstrates and fosters a collaborative spirit and way of working so ideas can flourish

 

Joining Our Creative Community

We aspire to be the most integrated network in the world for a lot of reasons. A big one is to make sure people always have your back. We don’t want talent to be islands at Dentsu Creative. We want this to be the place where you can do the work of your life while having a life. This means offering an inclusive culture that embraces individual ways of working - a culture that values compensating employees for their contributions in a multitude of ways. For everything we ask of our people to do right by our clients and creative standards, we commit to giving back equally in investing in your unique career aspirations and learning and development needs. Seeing and celebrating our people is where we find joy. When you are a part of our creative network, you get an all-access pass to our global playground. There’s a purposeful, flexible infrastructure for you to jump toward initiatives that excite you in partnership with specialists in entertainment, experience, data, earned attention and more. Your voice and unique lived experience are beyond valued. We want you to be loud, raise your hand and leave your imprint on how we continue building our creative culture while shaping what the very future of creativity can be. So, why not choose your own adventure? Let us be your springboard

Please Note: Direct mail strategy experience is required for this role. Candidates should have experience incorporating direct mail into broader customer lifecycle and omnichannel marketing strategies.


Merkle is a leading data-driven, technology-enabled, global performance marketing agency that specializes in the delivery of unique, personalized customer experiences across platforms and devices. For more than 30 years, Fortune 1000 companies and leading nonprofit organizations have partnered with Merkle to maximize the value of their customer portfolios. The agency's heritage in data, technology, and analytics forms the foundation for its unmatched skills in understanding consumer insights that drive people-based marketing strategies. Its combined strengths in performance media, customer experience, customer relationship management, loyalty, and enterprise marketing technology drive improved marketing results and competitive advantage.

 

We are champions for meaningful progress and we strive to be a force for good—for our people, for our clients, for the industry and for our society. We keep our people at the center, creating space for growth, understanding and learning so they can thrive. We embed diversity, in our mindset, in our solutions and in our teams to empower an inclusive, equitable and culturally fluent environment. Building this culture within our teams makes us better collaborators with each other and with our clients, driving better outcomes for all. Merkle is an agency of dentsu.

 

As Director, Customer Lifecycle Marketing Strategy, you will join a team of experienced marketers who focus on helping Merkle clients achieve their business goals. 

 

You will be a key member of our client account team and will ensure that the programs we execute are based on a deep understanding of our client’s business and strategic objectives.  You’ll appreciate the importance of strong relationships and become a trusted advisor to the client and Merkle account team. You will be a person who thrives in both analytic as well as creative thinking and will be nimble in solving for client problems.  As a leader your skills and passion for communicating strategy will get others to believe in the ideas that you present and follow that belief through to execution.

job.description:

Job Description:

This role is part of Merkle’s expanding Audience Platform Analytics practice, helping clients unlock value from their data and marketing technology investments. The practice supports the strategic implementation, adoption, measurement, and optimization of leading platforms across Customer Data Platforms solutions (such as Adobe Experience Platform, Salesforce etc.), Content Supply Chain, CMS, Planning & Workflow Management. Our goal is to help clients rapidly deploy and maximize the value of these platforms by establishing right strategic initiatives, robust measurement frameworks, driving adoption, enabling data-driven decision-making, and demonstrating ROI. Through audience intelligence, real-time personalization, omnichannel orchestration, content performance analytics, and operational insights, we help organizations improve efficiency, accelerate business outcomes, and realize measurable value across the end-to-end customer and content lifecycle.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead CDP engagements by providing expertise in the strategy, design, development and activation of marketing omni-channel use cases and customer journeys within Adobe Experience Platform
  • Develop and execute roadmap for Adobe tech stack, ensuring alignment with business objectives, integration with organization’s Martech ecosystem, and deliver measurables results that drive incremental benefits.
  • Build frameworks required to define use cases based on a detailed understanding of clients’ needs and goals.
  • Conduct audience analyses using data attributes and business knowledge, developing audiences based on testing and targeting strategies.
  • Manage transformation through journey mapping, insight development, development of transformational roadmaps, and value quantification.
  • Lead client engagements by providing expertise across Content Supply Chain Analytics, audience platforms, data strategy, measurement, testing, and cross-channel customer engagement.
  • Define and implement measurement frameworks, KPI strategies to track performance, operational efficiency, adoption, and business value realization.
  • Lead the development of use cases and value hypotheses based on client objectives, platform capabilities, data availability, and organizational readiness.
  • Provide solutioning and strategic guidance to connect Content Supply Chain capabilities with audience activation, personalization, and omnichannel marketing execution.
  • Design and govern taxonomies, metadata frameworks, and measurement requirements.
  • Establish baseline metrics and measurement methodologies to quantify the impact of Content Supply Chain, and audience platform investments.
  • Build reporting frameworks, and insights programs that connect operational, content, and marketing performance metrics to business outcomes and ROI.
  • Collaborate across cross-functional teams to develop strategic and analytics solutions for CDP and Content Supply Chain initiatives.  
  • Develop Merkle points of view (POVs), thought leadership, and industry content related to Audience Platforms, Content Supply Chain Analytics, measurement, and value realization.
  • Possess a deep understanding of the nuances in marketing to customers across different verticals and environments.
  • Collaborate with leadership, key stakeholders and partner agencies to turn ideas into actionable plans.

 

 

Skills and Experience:

 

  • Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) experience is the top priority with CDP strategy, journey orchestration, and measurement expertise as requirements.
